At five seeds and 20,000 resamples it excludes zero in all five (lower bounds +0.0032 to +0.0090). Raising the count is the fix rule 46 endorses; it changes no threshold, cohort or horizon, and the verdict is unaffected because the incumbent is reported and never gated. resample_p is now emitted beside every interval. WHAT CHALLENGE B LEARNED: a 15-year-old published predictor, in weakened form, beats all 14 of this project candidates on this deposit; the primary null is uninformative and labelled as such; and the path to a real answer is arithmetic (n=239 at the pessimistic end of E38 reliability interval), not novelty. gates: G1: >=60 subjects and E38's reliability interval still excluding zero; ceiling 0.5402

G2 THE REDUNDANCY GATE: |Spearman(lrtc_alpha, relative_alpha_power)| <= 0.90 across subjects, evaluated BEFORE any label is consulted. The whole claim is that temporal structure carries what magnitude does not, so redundancy refutes the premise regardless of outcome (rule 28)
P4: multiplicity over the FULL SIXTEEN-candidate family, not the new pair -- E41 already scored 14 candidates on this cohort, so this is a SECOND LOOK and the file says so
POWER unchanged from E41 because the cohort is unchanged: MDE 0.272 at n=104, so a null is reported as UNDERPOWERED NULL rather than a negative
instrument_changed: From spectral SUMMARIES to a TEMPORAL-DYNAMICS property of the same rhythm, imported from statistical physics: DFA of the alpha amplitude envelope. Motivated by E41's finding that the incumbent beat all 14 candidates, so a fifteenth spectral summary is the least informative option. Direction NOT declared because the source does not give it -- a limitation, not a choice.
outcome_detail: REFINED as registered, and it does NOT survive multiplicity - both belong in any account. G2 (the premise gate): Spearman(lrtc_alpha, relative_alpha_power) = +0.2426 against a 0.90 ceiling, so the two share ~6% of variance and the refinement premise holds rather than being assumed. P1: incumbent +0.2018 [+0.0050,+0.3857], IDENTICAL to four decimals to E41 v1 value on an independently re-extracted feature set - an unplanned rule-20 validation of the re-extraction. P2: lrtc_alpha +0.2446 [+0.0638,+0.4126], two-sided, excludes zero, exceeds the incumbent. PASSED. But the margin (0.043 on n=104 where SE ~0.10, between measures correlated at +0.24) is NOT meaningful and is not presented as one. P3 PLACEBO, the strongest result: imagery +0.2446 vs executed movement -0.0748 [-0.2813,+0.1334], a separation of 0.32 with the placebo on the wrong side of zero. A feature predicting both equally would be tracking cortical legibility; this one does not. That dissociation is what Challenge B substitute question needs and is a stronger claim than the correlation. P4: NOTHING survives FWER 0.05. lrtc_alpha raw p 0.0145, ADJUSTED p 0.1299; effective_tests 12.80 of 16. Second look at a cohort where 14 candidates were already scored, so the adjusted number is the relevant one. First candidate in this programme to clear a pre-registered primary, a redundancy gate and a placebo on Challenge B, with a direction it was not allowed to choose and a literature precedent naming the pattern in advance (PMID 34618375). Next step is INDEPENDENT REPLICATION (Q14 Stieger: 62 subjects, 450 trials/session vs 45 total here, plus the demographics eegmmidb lacks), not another test on this cohort. Must exclude zero AND exceed the incumbent's |rho|.

deposit: VitalDB, vitaldb_grid.csv, 250 cases / 5,845 rows carrying BIS, monitor EMG, SQI and the spectral state measure; maintenance only
gates: G1: >=100 cases and >=2000 rows with all four channels
G2 (rule 32): >=50 cases in which BIS and EMG BOTH take >=5 distinct values, because a between-case comparison would answer 'are these different patients' rather than 'does muscle move the number'

P3 independent-channel check: repeat the primary with OUR emg_index computed from the waveform (correlates +0.3511 with the monitor's channel) - agreement across two independent EMG estimates is worth more than either alone
instrument_changed: The COMPARATOR changes from SEF95 to real BIS, which is the whole point - our three Challenge C negatives explicitly scope themselves 'never ahead of BIS' and therefore do not bear on the prior work's claim. And the question changes from 'does a candidate beat the monitor' to 'is the monitor contaminated by a specific, named mechanism' - a falsifiable fact about an instrument rather than a performance race.
outcome_detail: THE MECHANISM IS REFUTED, DECISIVELY AND IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION - and the first version of the verdict code called it CONTAMINATION (rule 37, FOURTH occurrence, committed here). P1: partial(BIS, EMG | spectral state) = +0.1648; partial(spectral state, EMG | BIS) = -0.2615; ASYMMETRY -0.0967 [-0.1798, -0.0100], excluding zero on the NEGATIVE side. At matched conditioning the SPECTRAL MEASURE is more muscle-associated than BIS, the reverse of the hypothesis. P3 confirms with an INDEPENDENT EMG estimate: our own emg_index gives -0.2120 [-0.2889, -0.1286], same sign, larger magnitude, also excluding zero. Two independent muscle estimates agree. P4: the temporal half fails too - EMG FALLS slightly across the maintenance fraction (Spearman -0.0810) and the thirds are flat (median 27.37, 26.63, 26.86), against a claim of 63% clustering in the final third. PHYSICALLY SENSIBLE, which makes it hard to dismiss: the aperiodic exponent is fitted across a band that INCLUDES 20-45 Hz, exactly where surface EMG lives, so muscle flattens the exponent directly; BIS carries explicit EMG-suppression processing. A broadband slope fitted through the EMG band is close to the worst choice if EMG robustness is the goal, and the prior claim has the physics backwards. THE BUG: the registered verdict rule enumerated "includes zero" and "excludes zero and beats the placebo" and NEVER contemplated excluding zero on the wrong side, so lo>0 or hi<0 printed CONTAMINATION over a refutation; the placebo compounded it because with both asymmetries negative asym>q is satisfied by being LESS negative. Both branches are now sign-aware. CONSEQUENCES: Challenge C EMG mechanism refuted on this deposit; the discordance itself is untouched, only the proposed mechanism; it STRENGTHENS the case for phase-based measures (wpli_alpha, icoh_alpha), which avoid the 20-45 Hz amplitude band by construction; and it is a direct hit on the UCE robustness claim that was load-bearing for the intraoperative application.
placebo: P2: the identical asymmetry with SQI, a general signal-quality channel, substituted for EMG. If the effect is about muscle rather than any artefact channel, the EMG asymmetry must EXCEED the SQI asymmetry. A comparison, never a threshold. NOT INFORMATIVE if the primary spans zero.
primary: The ASYMMETRY: |partial(BIS, EMG | whole_head_exponent)| - |partial(whole_head_exponent, EMG | BIS)|, case-clustered bootstrap CI excluding zero. An asymmetry rather than a single partial because one positive partial could be residual confounding from an imperfect state proxy, while a difference in how two measures respond to the same channel at the same conditioning cannot.
question: Is BIS contaminated by muscle activity in a way a spectral slope is not? Challenge C's first test against real BIS rather than the SEF95 proxy our own three negatives used.

deposit: VitalDB, vitaldb_grid.csv, 6,439 ok windows / 250 cases, maintenance only; 5,845 carry BIS and monitor EMG with the sensor attached
gates: G1: >=20 evaluable cases (>=8 reference windows each). PASSED, 213 cases.

CAPABILITY (rule 32): median within-case SD / between-case SD >= 0.10, so a within-case constant cannot win by not moving. All retained measures 0.93-2.05. Checked failable against a deliberately constant column.
ABSENT-COLUMN CHECK (rule 6): uce_v1 is 0/6,439 populated in this grid and is dropped as ABSENT rather than reported as 'too flat'.
incumbent: meta_bis, on the same rows. E26/E34/E37 all used SEF95 and scoped themselves 'never ahead of BIS'; this is the second experiment to use real BIS.
instrument_changed: From a partial-correlation asymmetry (E43) to an event-based within-case displacement under a matched exposure. Deliberately a different statistic on the same question, so agreement is corroboration rather than repetition.
limitations: Frontalis EMG genuinely rises as anaesthesia lightens, so 'moves in the top EMG decile' conflates contamination with correct tracking of a lighter patient, and Arm B cannot separate them -- the ordering among candidates under an identical exposure is the interpretable part, not the level. BIS moving most is expected under either reading. E43's design conditioned on state and this one does not; two designs with DIFFERENT confounds agreeing on the same ordering is the value here, not either alone. A measure can also be steady because it is insensitive to everything; the capability gate bounds that reading without eliminating it. VitalDB is two frontal channels at 128 Hz, maintenance only -- induction is before the BIS sensor goes on and emergence after it comes off.
outcome_detail: ARM A WAS A GATE THAT COULD NOT FAIL AND IS REPORTED AS SUCH, NOT DELETED (rule 40, committed here). The registered first primary selected artefact windows by BIS >= 80 and compared |delta_BIS| against each candidate. It returned ROBUST for six of six candidates, which is the tell (rule 18). The selection rule mechanically forces delta_BIS >= (80 - mean_ref)/sd_ref, computed at a per-case mean of 4.584 against an observed 5.813, while every candidate is unconstrained -- so no candidate could have failed. The experiment's own test file was written to check rule 40 and covered the CAPABILITY gate and G1 but never asked whether the PRIMARY could fail; three tests were added that do. ARM B (corrected, selection moved to EMG's top decile >= 32.3, 213 cases) IS a test and one candidate fails it. |delta| ordering, steadiest first: lempel_ziv 1.576, relative_alpha_power 1.806, exponent_low 2.097, exponent_high 2.995, whole_head_exponent 3.109, spectral_edge_95 3.563, BIS 3.922. Placebo ~0.66 for every measure, far below all of them. Verdicts vs BIS: lempel_ziv +2.347 [+1.881,+2.829] ROBUST; relative_alpha_power +2.116 [+1.656,+2.602] ROBUST; exponent_low +1.826 [+1.343,+2.329] ROBUST; exponent_high +0.928 [+0.455,+1.414] ROBUST; whole_head_exponent +0.813 [+0.259,+1.364] ROBUST; spectral_edge_95 +0.360 [-0.378,+1.079] p(wrong side) 0.1664 REFUTED. E43'S MECHANISM REPRODUCES: exponent_high moves 0.898 more than exponent_low, the predicted direction, from a different statistic on a different selection (rule 20). ONE REGISTERED PREDICTION FAILED: whole_head_exponent was predicted to sit BETWEEN the two sub-bands and instead sits ABOVE both (3.109 > 2.995 > 2.097).
placebo: Artefact set replaced by an equal-sized random draw from the same case's own reference windows, drawn OUT of the reference so no row is in both, 200 draws. Real |delta| must exceed it -- a comparison, never a threshold; NOT INFORMATIVE if the primary spans zero.
primary: ARM B: within-case delta = (mean over a case's top-EMG-decile windows minus mean over its other windows) / that case's own SD, for BIS and each candidate; case-clustered bootstrap CI on |delta_BIS| - |delta_candidate|, 20,000 resamples, plus the resample-level fraction on the wrong side of the null (rule 46).
question: Under an identical muscle exposure, which measures move least -- and does E43's band mechanism (EMG lives at 20-45 Hz, so a 1-20 Hz fit should be steadier than a 20-40 Hz one) reproduce under a completely different statistic?

deposit: chennu (20 subj x 4 levels, PROPOFOL), ds005620 (21 subj, PROPOFOL, repeated-awakening sedation), ds004541 (8 subj, agent NOT recorded, true LOC/ROC). chennu+ds005620 are the same-drug pair; ds004541 anchors scale only.
gates: MIN_SUBJECTS=6 paired subjects per deposit per feature

Only the 8 features common to all three deposits are usable. exponent_low -- the measure E43 and E46 both selected -- exists in chennu ONLY and had to be excluded, a direct cost of the deposits having been extracted at different times.
incumbent: None applicable -- this bounds what any Challenge A comparison could detect rather than competing with a marker. The thing it replaces is the AUC framing of E21/E22/E25/E29/E35/E36, which has the wrong null: failing to reject 'distinguishable' is not evidence of equivalence.
instrument_changed: From discrimination (AUC: can a classifier tell the agents apart?) to equivalence (is the drug difference smaller than a pre-declared margin?), and from an opinion-chosen margin to one measured on a zero-drug-contrast condition. The registered margin for any future test is max(floor_upper_CI, mean|Delta|/3), with a mandatory UNPOWERED verdict if that exceeds mean|Delta|/2.
limitations: delta_floor is an UPPER bound on same-drug disagreement: chennu and ds005620 differ in depth, protocol, montage and task as well as study identity, so part of the gap is not study noise. That makes the NOT RESOLVABLE verdict conservative in the sense that a better-matched pair might do better -- but any real two-deposit drug comparison sits in exactly this situation. Depth is the specific worry: at chennu's deepest level subjects still score 26.9/40, so chennu and ds005620 are SEDATION studies and only ds004541 crosses LOC; the floor therefore generalises to an LOC displacement only by assumption. Features come from earlier extraction scripts rather than eeg_features_common.py, so pipeline differences are not excluded -- within-subject differencing cancels additive per-recording offsets but NOT multiplicative or scale differences, and re-extracting all three through the shared path is the obvious follow-up and would sharpen this result either way.
outcome_detail: ZERO OF EIGHT FEATURES ARE RESOLVABLE. Two independent PROPOFOL studies disagree about the awake->sedated displacement by as much as the displacement itself, so a cross-deposit two-drug comparison cannot separate drug from deposit AT ANY SAMPLE SIZE. This converts E36's qualitative structural limit into a number. Delta (chennu / ds005620 / ds004541), floor and P(floor>=effect): lempel_ziv +1.017/+1.912/+1.798 floor 0.894 [0.098,2.118] P=0.098 (closest to resolvable, and the ONLY feature agreeing in sign across all three); relative_delta_power -0.481/-0.584/-0.039 floor 0.103 R=3.58 but CI upper 0.877 exceeds mean|Delta| 0.368, P=0.179; whole_head_exponent -0.351/+1.005/+1.340 P=0.790; relative_alpha_power -0.433/+0.994/-0.209 P=0.995; spectral_edge_95 +0.274/-0.589/+0.424 P=0.906; spectral_entropy +0.648/+0.068/-0.307 P=0.773; uce_v1 -0.221/+0.996/+1.295 P=0.837; wpli_alpha -0.145/+0.725/-0.359 P=0.831. THE SIGN FLIPS BETWEEN TWO STUDIES OF THE SAME DRUG for whole_head_exponent, relative_alpha_power, uce_v1, spectral_edge_95 and wpli_alpha -- error catalogue rule 16 (when two arms disagree in SIGN, the definition is doing the work, not the biology), here across studies rather than across arms. A TRAP CAUGHT BEFORE CODING: chennu level 4 is RECOVERY, not the deepest -- plasma propofol 0/447/900/290 ug/L and accuracy 37.9/34.3/26.9/37.6 of 40. Reading the 1-4 ordinal as monotonic depth would have contrasted awake against recovered and reported a near-null state effect.
placebo: Not applicable: the design contains no drug contrast by construction. The same-drug pair IS the null condition -- a drug difference of exactly zero, measured on the exact statistic an equivalence test would use.
primary: Per feature: within-subject awake->deep displacement expressed in units of the deposit's own BETWEEN-SUBJECT awake spread (Delta); delta_floor = |Delta(chennu) - Delta(ds005620)|, two studies of the SAME drug; resolvability R = mean|Delta| / delta_floor. Subject-level bootstrap, 20,000 resamples, floor recomputed inside each draw.
question: What indifference margin would a Challenge A equivalence test need, and is a cross-deposit equivalence test possible at all? Derived from data containing NO drug contrast, so the margin cannot be chosen after seeing one.

PRIOR_ART_CORRECTION: E50's HEADLINE MECHANISM WAS ALREADY ESTABLISHED IN THIS PROJECT AND I DID NOT CHECK BEFORE CLAIMING IT. MASTER_PLAN.md §9.13 (E08) states verbatim: 'The two sub-bands point in opposite directions, and the whole-band fit averages them to nothing.' It reports signed AUC baseline-vs-moderate of 0.863 [0.790, 0.948] for exponent_high (20-40 Hz), 0.393 [0.273, 0.513] for the 1-40 Hz fit, and 0.168 [0.070, 0.242] for exponent_low -- on the SAME chennu deposit, with the prediction inherited from Colombo (PMID 30639334) BEFORE computing. §9.9 (E05) had already reported whole_head_exponent monotone in plasma in only 45% of subjects, uce_v1 50%, lempel_ziv 90%. So 'the broadband exponent is a cancelling mixture' and 'uce_v1 does not track dose' are REDISCOVERIES, not discoveries, and were reported to the investigator as new. Error-catalogue discipline violated: read the project's own record before claiming a mechanism.
WHAT_IS_ACTUALLY_NEW_IN_E50: Stated precisely, and it is less than the original entry implied. (1) A quantitative dose-response CORRELATION against measured plasma concentration (exponent_low rho -0.810 +/- 0.051, exponent_high +0.710 +/- 0.076, whole_head -0.130 +/- 0.129) rather than E05's count of subjects monotone across three levels -- and §9.9's own caveat 2 says that count is fragile and its absolute percentages are not defensible, so this is the stronger statistic it asked for. (2) USE OF THE RECOVERY LEVEL (plasma 290, BELOW both sedated levels) to separate a drug effect from session-time drift; E05 used only baseline/mild/moderate and could not do this. It also partly answers §9.9's alternative explanation 1: a filter-edge or preprocessing artefact would not reverse at recovery, and the broadband exponent is MOST negative there. (3) The link to E49's cross-deposit sign flips, which is genuinely new because E49 is new. (4) Rejection of EMG drift as the explanation via emg_index.
confirmatory_prediction: REGISTERED BEFORE THE TEST EXISTS. Re-extract ds005620 and ds004541 through analysis/eeg_features_common.py (chennu already carries both sub-bands) and re-run E49 on exponent_low and exponent_high SEPARATELY. PREDICTION: the two sub-bands AGREE in sign across deposits where whole_head_exponent flipped, and their E49 resolvability R exceeds the broadband's. FALSIFICATION: if the sub-bands flip sign across deposits too, the mixture explanation is wrong and E49's floor is genuine study noise. Either outcome is decisive and the test costs one extraction pass.
consequence_for_e52: E52's value is unchanged and arguably clearer: E08 established the mechanism WITHIN chennu, and E52 tests whether it explains disagreement ACROSS deposits, which E08 never attempted. That is a genuine extension rather than a third telling.
deposit: chennu, 20 subjects x 4 propofol levels with measured plasma concentration (0 / 447 / 900 / 290 ug/L). Level 4 is RECOVERY, so plasma is NON-MONOTONE in level -- which makes it possible to separate a DRUG effect from a session-TIME drift, because a time-driven measure cannot reverse at recovery and a dose-driven one must.
file: (diagnostic run inline; confirmatory test registered below, not yet run)
incumbent: whole_head_exponent (1-45 Hz), the measure this project used before E43, and uce_v1, the prior work's frozen composite.
instrument_changed: From a between-deposit displacement contrast (E49) to a within-subject dose-response against a MEASURED drug concentration, which is a far stronger design and was available locally the whole time.
limitations: Exploratory and single-deposit: the mechanism is demonstrated in chennu alone, which is also the deposit whose broadband sign was anomalous, so the explanation is fitted to the case it explains until the confirmatory test runs. exponent_low's negative dose response is very likely driven in part by the propofol ALPHA peak growing inside a 1-20 Hz fit window and flattening it -- the same contamination recorded in the ds005385 smoke run -- so exponent_low here is NOT a clean aperiodic measure and a peak-suppressed fit (exponent_low_robust, which the shared path emits and chennu's older extraction does not) is needed to separate 'alpha grew' from 'the slope changed'. chennu is sedation, not unresponsiveness: subjects score 26.9/40 at the deepest level.
outcome: positive (mechanism CONFIRMED, not discovered) -- see PRIOR_ART_CORRECTION
outcome_detail: THE BROADBAND EXPONENT IS TWO STRONG, OPPOSITELY-SIGNED DOSE EFFECTS THAT CANCEL. Within-subject rho against plasma propofol, all four levels: exponent_low (1-20 Hz) -0.810 +/- 0.051; exponent_high (20-40 Hz) +0.710 +/- 0.076; whole_head_exponent (1-45 Hz) -0.130 +/- 0.129, an interval including zero. Robust to subsetting: L1-L3 only (monotone dose) gives -0.925 / +0.800 / -0.150, and dropping the deepest level gives -0.675 / +0.400 / -0.350. So the 1-45 Hz fit averages a near-perfect negative dose response against a strong positive one and retains almost nothing, and WHICH SIDE DOMINATES depends on montage, sampling rate, fit range and spectral resolution -- i.e. on the deposit. THAT IS A MECHANISM FOR E49's SIGN FLIPS, and a better one than 'studies disagree'. TWO HYPOTHESES WERE TESTED AND REJECTED FIRST: sedation depth (chennu's displacement does not track depth -- the broadband exponent is MOST negative at RECOVERY, plasma 290, below both sedated levels), and EMG drift (emg_index barely moves, -0.249/-0.178/-0.075, and correlates only -0.200 with the exponent displacement). SEPARATELY AND INDEPENDENTLY: uce_v1 DOES NOT TRACK PROPOFOL DOSE -- rho -0.110 +/- 0.134 over four levels, -0.150 +/- 0.167 over L1-L3. On within-subject dose-response data with measured plasma concentrations, which is the cleanest available test of an anaesthetic-depth marker, the prior work's frozen composite is indistinguishable from no relationship. lempel_ziv does track, +0.520 +/- 0.090.
primary: Within-subject Spearman correlation between each feature and plasma propofol across a subject's four levels, averaged over the 20 subjects with SE across subjects.
question: Why does the broadband 1-45 Hz aperiodic exponent flip sign between two studies of the same drug (E49)? Is it study noise, sedation depth, or EMG drift?
status: EXPLORATORY -- post-hoc, prompted by E49's sign flips. Not a confirmatory result. The confirmatory prediction is stated and must be run on independently re-extracted deposits before this is claimed anywhere.

deposit: 3 free cohorts, eyes-closed, healthy adults only, one row per subject: ds003775 n=109 (18-71), ds005385 n=212 (20-70), ds004504 controls n=29 (57-78). 350 adults.
gates: G0: >=3 cohorts with >=15 adults each
incumbent: The published literature itself: PMID 37503078 (MIDUS) and PMID 39288668 (LEISURE) both report alpha peak frequency declining with age in adults.
instrument_changed: Introduces the bridge design: validate on a quantity with external truth and transfer to one without.
limitations: One external anchor. A pipeline can get alpha peak frequency right and the exponent wrong; the bridge narrows the failure space, it does not close it. Restricted to adults because the IAPF-age relation reverses sign in childhood (PMID 36739102), so nothing here certifies the pipeline for paediatric data.
outcome_detail: PASS. alpha_peak_hz ~ age slope -0.01131 Hz/yr [-0.01898, -0.00390], negative and excluding zero, reproducing the published adult direction. Per-cohort on different rigs: ds003775 -0.01984 [-0.03252, -0.00586] and ds005385 -0.01160 [-0.02129, -0.00214] both exclude zero in the same direction; ds004504 (n=29, age 57-78) is too small and narrow to estimate. SECONDARY, registered as not-a-gate: whole_head_exponent ~ age -0.00540 [-0.00735, -0.00344], also negative and excluding zero, matching MIDUS.
primary: Slope of alpha_peak_hz on age, cohort and sex as fixed effects, subject bootstrap.
question: Is our feature pipeline calibrated? Does it reproduce a known age effect on a bridge quantity with external truth, standing in for the aperiodic exponent, which has no published norm?

deposit: Same 350 adults. Batch effects deliberately NOT removed: three references (FCz, average, linked-ears), three amplifiers.
gates: CAPABILITY: the corrected arm must retain >=10% of the uncorrected within-cohort spread, else NOT INFORMATIVE -- an arm that destroyed its own signal is empty, not harmonised.
incumbent: PLAIN GAIN REMOVAL -- subtract each recording's mean log power across the four bands. No aperiodic model at all. E48 shipped without an incumbent until the numbers forced the issue (rule 45).
limitations: THREE METRIC DEFINITIONS WERE TRIED AND THE FIRST TWO WERE GAMEABLE. Per-arm denominator is gamed by ADDING NOISE (that is how the first, within-cohort sham beat the real correction). Fixed denominator is gamed by SHRINKING EVERYTHING -- the correction reduces within-cohort spread to 11.6-23.4% of uncorrected, so a fixed denominator handed it a free win for destroying signal, and the first run reported 40-400x reductions on that basis. Self-normalisation is invariant to pure multiplicative shrinkage; the capability gate and cross-cohort sham cover the rest. The retained spread of 0.12-0.23 clears the 0.10 floor but is low, and what remains has not been shown to be signal rather than residual noise -- the obvious next check is whether the corrected measure still carries the age effect E47 certified. Cohorts differ in POPULATION as well as hardware and nothing here separates those. Alpha is the weakest band and also the one where a fixed-denominator metric had gain removal WINNING, so its verdict is metric-dependent and should be treated as provisional.
outcome_detail: BEATS GAIN REMOVAL in all four bands, but by far less than the raw comparison suggests. Self-normalised batch index, abs / rel / gain-removed / aperiodic-corrected / sham: delta 5.555 / 1.445 / 1.287 / 0.414 / 2.488; theta 5.215 / 0.250 / 0.432 / 0.094 / 2.433; alpha 5.045 / 0.624 / 0.730 / 0.608 / 2.516; beta 5.111 / 1.079 / 1.212 / 0.365 / 2.606. Primary diff(resid - gain): delta -0.8723 [-1.2003, -0.6351]; theta -0.3376 [-0.4549, -0.1012]; alpha -0.1223 [-0.2189, -0.0366]; beta -0.8475 [-1.1854, -0.5707]. All exclude zero on the correct side. Sham (2.4-2.6) is far worse than either real arm, so the harmonisation uses cohort-specific background information. THE HONEST HEADLINE IS NOT 5.5 -> 0.4: most of that is scalar gain removal, which any normalisation achieves. The aperiodic model's own contribution is 1.29 -> 0.41 in delta and only 0.73 -> 0.61 in alpha.
placebo: Cross-cohort sham: aperiodic model borrowed from a subject in a DIFFERENT cohort, so it carries no information about this cohort's background.
primary: Self-normalised batch index = between-cohort SD of the age/age^2/sex-residualised measure over the SAME ARM's within-cohort SD. Primary is batch(resid) - batch(gain-removed), subject bootstrap.
question: Does aperiodic correction HARMONISE -- reduce disagreement between cohorts differing in amplifier, reference and population -- beyond what removing a scalar gain already achieves?

consequences: E48's verdict stands on its own metric but its PRACTICAL recommendation is weakened. Aperiodic correction beats gain removal on between-cohort disagreement with intervals excluding zero; it demonstrably costs real signal in beta; and on the only external criterion available it is indistinguishable from a method with no aperiodic model at all. For a frozen normative reference the choice between them is NOT settled by current evidence, and the deciding test needs far more abnormal data than 88 recordings.
deposit: Same 350 adults for the age criterion; ds004504's HELD-OUT ABNORMAL SET (29 control, 59 Alzheimer's/frontotemporal) for the clinical criterion, within one cohort so there is no cohort confound.
file: (diagnostic run inline against E48's own stated weakness)
incumbent: Plain scalar gain removal, as in E48.
limitations: The clinical criterion is one cohort, one disease family, n=88, and dementia is not the application any of the three challenges target. A null here is weak evidence, not evidence of equivalence -- the same error E49 was built to avoid, and it applies to this diagnostic too.
outcome: mixed -- one clear cost, and the decisive criterion is underpowered
outcome_detail: (A) AGE-EFFECT RETENTION. delta: the corrected arm keeps a significant age slope (-0.01026 [-0.01902, -0.00084]), so signal survives there. theta and alpha have no significant age slope in ANY arm including uncorrected, so there is nothing to retain. BETA IS A CLEAR COST: gain removal retains a significant age slope (+0.00738 [+0.00061, +0.00141... reported +0.00738 [+0.00061, +0.01413]]) and aperiodic correction destroys it (+0.00003 [-0.00674, +0.00697]). In beta the correction bought harmonisation by removing real age signal. (B) CLINICAL CRITERION, and this is where an over-claim was caught. Point estimates of |AUC-0.5| favour GAIN REMOVAL in 3 of 4 bands: delta 0.122 vs 0.087, theta 0.267 vs 0.186, alpha 0.172 vs 0.159, beta 0.132 vs 0.193 (correction better). BUT the bootstrapped gain-minus-resid difference EXCLUDES ZERO IN NO BAND: delta +0.035 [-0.088, +0.149], theta +0.081 [-0.008, +0.175], alpha +0.012 [-0.049, +0.077], beta -0.060 [-0.217, +0.099]. At 29 controls and 59 patients the criterion cannot resolve the two methods. 'Gain removal wins on the clinical criterion' was drafted and is NOT SUPPORTED; the correct statement is that they are indistinguishable here. Directions are physiologically coherent throughout -- dementia shows higher delta/theta and lower alpha/beta -- which is a sanity check on the pipeline.
primary: (A) age slope retained per arm; (B) |AUC-0.5| for control vs dementia per arm, with a bootstrapped gain-minus-resid difference.
question: E48's correction reduces between-cohort disagreement. Does the surviving 12-23% of within-cohort spread carry real information, or did the correction harmonise by destroying signal?
status: DIAGNOSTIC -- run to test E48's registered limitation that the corrected arm retains only 12-23% of the uncorrected within-cohort spread and that nothing had shown the remainder to be signal.

QUALIFICATION_THE_VERDICT_UNDERSTATES: E50's prediction had TWO parts and only the first is robust. Part 1 (sign agreement) is solid: P(disagree) = 0.0000 for both sub-bands against 0.7071 for the broadband. Part 2 ('their E49 resolvability R exceeds the broadband's') passes on POINT ESTIMATES only, and E52's verdict rule used point-estimate R where E49's own rule used the floor's upper CI. Applying E49's stricter criterion (floor_hi >= mean|Delta| -> NOT RESOLVABLE): exponent_low floor 0.763 but floor_hi 3.150 against mean|Delta| 1.769 -- FAILS; exponent_high floor 0.0064 but floor_hi 1.361 against mean|Delta| 1.573 -- marginal at best. **R = 247 for exponent_high must not be quoted**: it is an artefact of the two point estimates landing within 0.006 by luck, and the interval says the floor could be 1.361. THE TWO EXPERIMENTS USED DIFFERENT GATE STRICTNESS FOR THE SAME QUANTITY, which is a defect in E52's registration, not a result.
consequence: E49's 'not resolvable at any n' is NOT overturned. What is overturned is its MECHANISM: the sign flips were a broadband-fit artefact, not genuine study disagreement, so the floor was measured on a measure that cannot carry it. Cross-deposit Challenge A remains unproven at n=20 -- the sub-band floors are still wide -- but it is no longer structurally hopeless, and the right next step is to re-run E49's full statistic on the sub-bands with ds004541 re-extracted as a third deposit.
deposit: chennu (20 subj, propofol, levels 1 vs 3) and ds005620 (20 paired subj, propofol, task-awake vs task-sed) re-extracted through analysis/eeg_features_common.py. Both propofol, so the drug contrast is exactly zero.
incumbent: whole_head_exponent, the measure that flipped in E49.
limitations: Two deposits, not three. chennu's sub-bands come from the older per-deposit extraction and ds005620's from the shared path -- the estimator is identical (subband_exponents) but preprocessing differs, and exponent_high agreeing to 0.006 ACROSS that difference is either strong evidence the difference is immaterial or luck at n=20. Both deposits are SEDATION (chennu subjects score 26.9/40 at the deepest level); nothing here speaks to loss of consciousness. The clean version re-extracts chennu through the shared path, which is reachable at CHENNU_ARCHIVE_URL.
outcome: CONFIRMED on sign agreement; NOT confirmed on resolvability once the interval is used
outcome_detail: THE PREDICTION HELD, AND THE FALSIFICATION BRANCH WAS LIVE. exponent_low: chennu -1.387, ds005620 -2.150, same sign, P(sign disagreement) = 0.0000. exponent_high: chennu +1.576, ds005620 +1.570 -- agreeing to 0.006 across two studies, two amplifiers and two preprocessing pipelines -- same sign, P = 0.0000. The INCUMBENT flipped as required for the test to be meaningful: whole_head_exponent chennu -0.351 vs ds005620 +0.132, P(sign disagreement) = 0.7071, i.e. its sign is a coin flip under resampling. So the 1-45 Hz broadband fit is confirmed as a cancelling mixture of two sub-bands that each behave consistently, now demonstrated ACROSS deposits rather than within one (E08 established it within chennu only).
primary: Sign agreement of the within-subject awake->deep displacement across the two deposits, with a subject-level bootstrap probability of sign disagreement; resolvability R = mean|Delta| / |Delta_1 - Delta_2|.
question: E50/E08's registered prediction: do exponent_low and exponent_high AGREE in sign across deposits where whole_head_exponent flips?

ATTRIBUTION_CORRECTED_SAME_DAY: SUPERSEDED -- THIS CORRECTION WAS ITSELF WRONG AND IS RETRACTED. It compared E53's 0.898 (a difference of two COHORT-MEAN displacements on the same subjects) against 0.667 (a PER-SUBJECT mean absolute change). Those are different statistics: sampling noise largely cancels in the first because the subjects are identical, and does not in the second. The sqrt(2)x0.667=0.943 arithmetic was applied to the wrong quantity. See FINAL_ATTRIBUTION.
FINAL_ATTRIBUTION: E53'S ORIGINAL READING STANDS: the 0.898 IS substantially pipeline. The structurally matched control is a COHORT-MEAN shift between sessions on the same subjects, same pipeline -- exactly E53's shape with pipeline held constant. On ds004148 (60 subjects x 3 sessions, shared path) that is: whole_head_exponent 0.263, exponent_low 0.207, exponent_high 0.242, lempel_ziv 0.178, rel_alpha 0.242, rel_delta 0.209, sef95 0.269 -- **median 0.242, max 0.269**. Against E53's 0.898 that is a factor of 3.7, leaving sqrt(0.898^2 - 0.242^2) = 0.865 attributable to pipeline. PIPELINE DOMINATES.
SETTLED_THREE_CONTROLS_THREE_QUESTIONS:
The confusion came from using ONE control for TWO different comparisons. They need different controls and give different answers.
(A) SAME SUBJECTS, TWO PIPELINES -- E53's actual measurement, 0.898. Sampling largely cancels because the subjects are identical. Matched control: cohort-mean session shift on the same subjects, same pipeline = 0.242 (ds004148, 60 subj x 3 sessions). 0.898 >> 0.242, so PIPELINE IS REAL for this comparison. E53's original reading stands.
(B) DIFFERENT SUBJECTS, SAME PIPELINE -- the structure of any CROSS-DEPOSIT floor. Matched control: split-half of ds005620 into disjoint 10-vs-10, same pipeline, same deposit. Median |diff|: exponent_low 1.428, exponent_high 0.892, lempel_ziv 0.555, whole_head_exponent 0.351 (95th percentiles 3.271 / 1.753 / 1.791 / 1.057). **SAMPLING NOISE ALONE PRODUCES FLOORS OF 0.35-1.43 AT THESE n.**
(C) CONSEQUENCE, AND IT RETIRES THE '0.24 CROSS-DEPOSIT FLOOR' CLAIM I MADE ONE STEP EARLIER: 0.242 is a SAME-SUBJECT quantity and is NOT the comparator for a cross-deposit floor. Every E52 cross-deposit floor -- exponent_high 0.006, exponent_low 0.763, whole_head 0.482 -- is at or BELOW the sampling floor in (B). They are therefore uninformative about deposit OR pipeline: at n = 20 per deposit, sampling swamps both. exponent_high agreeing to 0.006 against a same-deposit split-half median of 0.892 is a coincidence, which is what E52's entry already said for a weaker reason.
WHAT_CHANGES_AND_WHAT_DOES_NOT: UNCHANGED: the ~0.9 floor is real; the criterion 'a sign is interpretable only when |Delta| substantially exceeds ~0.9' stands and is now BETTER founded, because the floor is intrinsic to the statistic rather than an artefact of mixing pipelines; E52's 0.006 agreement is still luck; the complete concordance with E49's flips (all 5 flips involved a |Delta| < 0.9, no feature with both |Delta| > 0.9 flipped) still holds. CHANGED, AND IT REDIRECTS THE WORK: E53 concluded that re-extracting everything through one path was 'load-bearing'. IT IS NOT. If pipeline contributes little, harmonisation cannot shrink this floor -- **the remedy is n, or more data per subject, not better harmonisation.** Q20's premise (re-extract chennu to close E52's asymmetry) is therefore much less important than E53 claimed, and the chennu TLS blocker matters less. Likewise E49's floors are NOISE-inflated, not pipeline-inflated: same verdict that E49 is too pessimistic, different cause, different fix.
WHAT_SURVIVES_AND_THE_CRITERION_IT_YIELD: The qualitative claim holds, and the measurement supplies the criterion it needs: A SIGN IS INTERPRETABLE ONLY WHEN |Delta| SUBSTANTIALLY EXCEEDS THE PIPELINE FLOOR OF ~0.9. exponent_low (-1.387, -2.150) and exponent_high (+1.576, +1.570) clear it in both deposits and cannot be flipped by a pipeline-scale perturbation; whole_head_exponent (-0.351, +0.132) sits inside it in both, which is exactly why its P(sign disagreement) was 0.7071. CHECKED AGAINST E49'S EIGHT FEATURES AND THE CONCORDANCE IS COMPLETE: every one of the 5 flips involved at least one |Delta| < 0.9 (whole_head, relative_alpha_power, spectral_edge_95, uce_v1, wpli_alpha), and NO feature with both |Delta| > 0.9 flipped (lempel_ziv, +1.017/+1.912, did not). So E49's sign flips are substantially a small-effect-plus-pipeline-noise phenomenon rather than a deposit phenomenon -- which is a better explanation than either E49's original reading or E50's mixture story ALONE, though the mixture story is what makes the sub-band displacements large enough to clear the floor in the first place.
consequence: FINAL. (1) No cross-deposit magnitude from E49 or E52 should be quoted -- held throughout all three revisions. (2) E49's 'zero of eight resolvable' is confirmed, and now with a cause: at n = 20 the sampling floor alone is 0.35-1.43 in these units, comparable to the state effects themselves. THE BINDING CONSTRAINT IS n, NOT HARMONISATION. (3) Harmonisation still matters for same-subject comparisons (A) but cannot rescue cross-deposit ones, so Q20's chennu blocker is a real but SECOND-ORDER problem. (4) The sign criterion survives and is the one durable output: a sign is interpretable only when |Delta| clearly exceeds the sampling floor, which is why exponent_low and exponent_high (|Delta| 1.4-2.2) held their signs and whole_head_exponent (|Delta| 0.13-0.35) did not.
deposit: ds005620 extracted TWICE -- bsde/results/ds005620_features.csv (old per-deposit pipeline) and /tmp/eeg_probe/state_cohorts.csv (shared path). SAME deposit, SAME 20 paired subjects, only the pipeline differs, so the deposit effect is exactly zero by construction.
limitations: Five features, one deposit, n=20. The old and shared pipelines differ in several ways at once (montage, 180 s window, 250 Hz resample, epoching) and this does not attribute the 0.898 to any one of them. A within-subject displacement cancels additive per-recording offsets, so what is measured here is the residual multiplicative/scale component -- which is the part that matters and is also the harder part to remove. | CORRECTION CAVEAT: ds004148 is 18-28 year olds and its sessions are separated by days or weeks, whereas ds005620's awake and sed blocks are within-session. Within-session repeats would be less noisy, so 0.943 may OVERSTATE the noise in ds005620's displacement and some pipeline contribution cannot be excluded -- only the claim that pipeline DOMINATES can be, and it is excluded.
outcome: negative for E52's magnitude claims; attribution to PIPELINE confirmed after one wrong retraction
outcome_detail: THE PIPELINE EFFECT IS MEDIAN 0.898 (range 0.446-0.971) ACROSS FIVE FEATURES. whole_head_exponent +1.005 -> +0.132 (0.873); lempel_ziv +1.912 -> +1.014 (0.898); relative_alpha_power +0.994 -> +1.440 (0.446); relative_delta_power -0.584 -> -1.555 (0.971); spectral_edge_95 -0.589 -> +0.329 (0.918) -- WHICH FLIPS SIGN ON THE SAME DATA WITH ONLY THE PIPELINE CHANGED. **Every E52 cross-deposit floor sits at or below this: exponent_high 0.0064, exponent_low 0.7629, whole_head_exponent 0.4823.** So E52's floors are dominated by pipeline, not deposit, and the celebrated agreement of exponent_high to 0.006 is roughly 140x below the noise introduced by changing pipelines on identical data -- it is luck, and R = 247 was meaningless (already withdrawn in E52's entry).
primary: |Delta_old - Delta_shared| for each feature present in both, where Delta is E49/E52's within-subject awake->deep displacement in awake-SD units.
question: E52 compared chennu (old pipeline) against ds005620 (shared path). How much of its cross-deposit floor is PIPELINE rather than deposit?
status: DIAGNOSTIC -- run against E52's own stated asymmetry (Q20 alternative 1), using data already held.

ALPHA_CHECK_CONTRADICTS_AN_EARLIER_CLAIM: I claimed earlier -- in the ds005385 smoke-run commit and in NORMATIVE_EEG_STATE_OF_THE_ART.md -- that exponent_low's eye-state swing was largely the alpha peak growing inside a 1-20 Hz fit. AT n=607 THE PEAK-SUPPRESSED FIT SAYS OTHERWISE: exponent_low -1.214 vs exponent_low_robust -1.195, a 1.6% reduction. Meanwhile the BROADBAND's effect is almost entirely peak-driven: whole_head_exponent -0.202 vs whole_head_robust -0.012. So the 1-20 Hz slope genuinely moves with eye state beyond the alpha peak. CAVEAT AGAINST OVER-READING THE REVERSAL: loglog_robust trims the largest positive residuals iteratively, and in a 1-20 Hz window a dominant alpha peak occupies so large a fraction of the fit points that trimming may not remove it -- so the robust fit's adequacy is itself weakest exactly where this test needs it. The honest statement is that the alpha explanation is NOT supported and is not cleanly refuted either.
COST_OF_THE_E43_SWITCH_CONFIRMED: The registration said that if eye state moves the broadband LESS than the sub-band, that is a cost of the E43 switch and must be reported as one. It does: |d_z| whole_head_exponent 0.202 against exponent_low 1.214, a factor of SIX. exponent_low is far more eye-state sensitive than the measure it replaced. Combined with E43 (more EMG-robust) and E46 (steadier under muscle), the sub-band's advantages are real but it carries a large new vulnerability that the broadband did not.
PLACEBO_SPLITS_THE_TWO_PRIMARIES: exponent_low PASSES its own placebo decisively (1.214 vs 0.248). lempel_ziv FAILS: its pre/post placebo reaches 0.934 against its own primary of 0.477, so **lempel_ziv is moved roughly twice as much by two hours of cognitive work as by opening the eyes** and its eye-state contrast is NOT specific. The first version of the verdict code compared the BEST primary against the WORST placebo and printed a single global PASS, which hid this; the placebo is now evaluated per measure. That is the same aggregation error as pooling a gate across arms (rules 34, 37).
deposit: ds005385 (Dortmund Vital), ses-1/acq-pre, 607 PAIRED subjects with both EyesClosed and EyesOpen. This pool is COMPLETE -- the extraction was ordered so ses-1/acq-pre finishes first, and it will not grow.
incumbent: whole_head_exponent, the measure used before E43.
limitations: One deposit, healthy adults 20-70, eyes-open/closed blocks 184 s apart within one session. It does not establish that HEEDB's unrecorded eye state biases a clinical reference by this much -- only that the measure is this sensitive to it. The placebo interval (a two-hour battery) is not a nuisance-free control: fatigue and drowsiness after two hours of cognitive work are real state changes, which is exactly why lempel_ziv's failure is interpretable as sensitivity to state rather than as a defect in the placebo.
outcome_detail: exponent_low d_z = -1.214 [-1.377, -1.069] at n=607, more than twice the 0.5 FIRST-ORDER threshold and larger than the -0.761 that PMID 42395346 reported and that prompted the promotion. lempel_ziv -0.477 [-0.557, -0.401]. VERDICT: FIRST-ORDER -- eye state must be resolved in-signal and frozen into the reference alongside the wake detector, and NORMAL_REFERENCE_COVARIATES.md's promotion out of 'known unknowns' was correct. Full table: exponent_low -1.214, lempel_ziv -0.477, whole_head_exponent -0.202, exponent_low_robust -1.195, whole_head_robust -0.012, rel_alpha +1.156, alpha_peak_hz +0.105, exponent_high +0.536, lrtc_alpha +0.241.
placebo: acq-pre vs acq-post within the SAME eye state, separated by a two-hour cognitive battery. Evaluated PER MEASURE.
primary: Within-subject paired difference EC-EO as Cohen's d_z, subject bootstrap, 20,000 resamples.
question: How far does EYE STATE move the measures destined for the normative scale? Registered in analysis/ds005385_extract.py before any feature value from this deposit existed.

CHALLENGE_B_CEILING_NOW_COMPOSABLE: E38 measured the LABEL's reliability at r_sb 0.2918, capping any predictor at sqrt = 0.5402. E45 supplies the missing half for E42's marker: lrtc_alpha ICC 0.644, ceiling sqrt = 0.802. The JOINT attenuation ceiling is 0.5402 x 0.802 = 0.434. E41's incumbent-strength expectation was 0.286 and its minimum detectable effect 0.272, both BELOW 0.434 -- so Challenge B is NOT ceiling-blocked by predictor unreliability. The binding constraint remains the label, as E38 said.
EXTERNAL_CHECK_FAILED: PMID 42395346 reports a five-year exponent ICC of 0.668 on public adult data with a five-year follow-up. Ours is 0.748 [0.674, 0.811] and 0.668 lies OUTSIDE that interval. Two readings and the design cannot separate them: the pipelines genuinely differ on the same data, OR the paper used a different deposit -- its dataset identification was INFERRED from design and follow-up interval, not verified, because it is not yet in PMC. Stated before the run as an inference, and it stays one.
LEMPEL_ZIV_IS_A_STATE_MEASURE_NOT_A_TRAI: ICC 0.193 [0.040, 0.332] -- by far the lowest tested, capping any trait correlation at sqrt(0.193) = 0.44. **It must NOT go on a normative scale**, which is a trait-like anchor, and NORMATIVE_EEG_STATE_OF_THE_ART.md §5 item 2 currently recommends carrying it there. That recommendation is now wrong and is superseded. The result is COHERENT rather than contradictory with everything else lempel_ziv has done: E46 found it the steadiest under muscle, E49 found it the only one of eight features agreeing in sign across three deposits, E50 found it tracking plasma propofol at +0.520, and E44 found it moved MORE by two hours of cognitive work than by opening the eyes. A measure that tracks state well SHOULD have poor trait stability. lempel_ziv is a good state measure and a bad reference measure, and those were being conflated.
PEAK_SUPPRESSION_STRICTLY_DOMINATES_FOR_: exponent_low_robust ICC 0.841 [0.787, 0.882] against exponent_low 0.756 [0.667, 0.831] -- the peak-suppressed fit is MORE reliable. And E44 showed peak suppression barely touches its eye-state sensitivity (-1.214 vs -1.195, a 1.6% reduction). Same state sensitivity, higher reliability: **exponent_low_robust is the better candidate for the normative scale and should replace exponent_low there.**
deposit: ds005385 EyesClosed/acq-pre, ses-1 vs ses-2 ~5 years apart, 207 paired subjects. POOL IS COMPLETE -- only 208 of 608 subjects have a second session.
limitations: REGISTERED AND BINDING: a five-year interval is a LOWER BOUND on measurement reliability, not an estimate of it. Real biological change over five years is confounded with measurement error, so sqrt(ICC) is a FLOOR on the trait ceiling rather than the ceiling. A high ICC is therefore informative and a low one is ambiguous -- lempel_ziv's 0.193 could be poor measurement OR genuine five-year state change, and this design cannot say which. Eyes-closed acq-pre only; 207 subjects; healthy adults 20-70.
outcome: positive -- both registered predictions held, and one result reverses a standing recommendation
outcome_detail: BOTH PREDICTIONS HELD. (1) exponent_low ICC 0.756, predicted [0.5, 0.8]. (2) lrtc_alpha 0.644 < exponent_low 0.756. Full table: rel_alpha 0.851 [0.793,0.893]; exponent_low_robust 0.841 [0.787,0.882]; exponent_high 0.757 [0.677,0.819]; exponent_low 0.756 [0.667,0.831]; whole_head_exponent 0.748 [0.674,0.811]; sef95 0.746 [0.660,0.815]; lrtc_alpha 0.644 [0.514,0.749]; alpha_peak_hz 0.629 [0.478,0.758]; dfa_exponent 0.396 [0.276,0.503]; lempel_ziv 0.193 [0.040,0.332].
primary: ICC(2,1), two-way random effects, ABSOLUTE agreement, single measurement. Absolute rather than consistency because a systematic five-year drift is exactly the threat a reference point cannot tolerate, and a consistency ICC would forgive it.
question: Five-year test-retest stability (ICC(2,1)) of each measure on our own estimator. Registered in analysis/ds005385_extract.py before any feature value existed.

MY_VERDICT_RULE_WAS_BADLY_SPECIFIED: The script printed 'WORTH BUILDING -- best R^2 = 0.1473' because the rule maximises over nine measures. That is the wrong statistic: taking the max across a panel is cherry-picking, and the measure that matters for a given challenge is fixed in advance, not chosen by outcome. The honest split is per purpose -- for the NORMATIVE SCALE the relevant measure is exponent_low_robust (R^2 0.147, gain 1.083, small but real, and it also has the highest ICC at 0.841, so it is the best reference candidate on two counts); for CHALLENGE B the relevant measure is lrtc_alpha (gain 1.000, nothing). The printed verdict should be read as the former only.
THE_DECISIVE_NUMBER_IS_lrtc_alpha: E42's lrtc_alpha IS Challenge B's marker, and age and sex explain **0.03 %** of its between-subject variance. Gain = 1.000. **A conditional reference buys Challenge B exactly nothing.** REFERENCE_AGAINST_ALL_THREE.md §2 forecast gains of 1.05-1.29 from R^2 of 0.1-0.4 and called this 'an unusually efficient dependency' -- the same regression that could kill the reference idea would size its Challenge B benefit. It sized it, and the benefit is zero for the measure that matters. That is a clean refutation of one of the three mechanisms that document proposes, delivered by the test it registered for exactly this purpose.
deposit: 745 healthy adults, eyes-closed, one row per subject, across ds003775 / ds004504 controls / ds005385, cohort as a fixed effect so R^2 is the INCREMENT of age+age^2+sex over a cohort-only model.
limitations: Age and sex only -- these deposits carry no comorbidity or medication, which are the HEEDB-specific covariates and the ones NORMAL_REFERENCE_COVARIATES.md §2 argues are most likely to matter, since 88.9% of the HEEDB cohort carries nervous-system drugs. So this is a LOWER bound on what a HEEDB conditional reference could explain, and the HEEDB version of Q16 step 4 is still worth running. REGISTERED AND UNTESTABLE HERE: the gain is real only if the covariate variance is unrelated to the outcome; no cohort here carries a BCI label, so this sizes the CEILING of the gain and cannot confirm it is realisable. That needs Q14 (Stieger 2021, 62 subjects with age, sex, handedness and 450 trials/session).
outcome: NEGATIVE for Challenge B; marginal for the normative scale
outcome_detail: R^2 [95% CI], gain, ICC, R^2/ICC: exponent_low_robust 0.1473 [0.1079,0.2008] gain 1.083 ICC 0.841 ratio 0.175; whole_head_exponent 0.1130 gain 1.062; exponent_low 0.0877 gain 1.047; sef95 0.0653; lempel_ziv 0.0557 (ratio 0.289, the highest -- age and sex explain 29% of its RELIABLE variance, but its reliable variance is tiny); rel_alpha 0.0534; alpha_peak_hz 0.0346; exponent_high 0.0164; **lrtc_alpha 0.0003 [0.0003, 0.0121], gain 1.000**.
primary: R^2 increment of age, age^2 and sex; gain = 1/sqrt(1-R^2); and R^2/ICC using E45's five-year ICCs, since only the RELIABLE part of between-subject variance can correlate with anything.
question: Q16 step 4: how much between-subject variance do age and sex explain, and what Challenge B gain does that forecast via 1/sqrt(1-R^2)?

DIRECTION_IS_NOT_INTERPRETABLE_AS_DEPTH: The three supported measures do not agree on which way older brains look. A lower exponent and a higher spectral edge both read as MORE awake-like; a lower lempel_ziv reads as MORE deep-like. Those cannot all mean 'the elderly are under-dosed at BIS 45'. The defensible statement is that the EEG STATE differs by age at matched BIS, not that a particular depth direction is implied. Attaching a depth interpretation would need an independent depth anchor, which this deposit does not have (induction is before the sensor goes on and emergence after it comes off).
SENSITIVITY_ARM_RUN: E55's own limitations named 'restricting to adults is the obvious sensitivity arm', because ages 1-89 span the range where the exponent's age relation is known to reverse (PMID 36739102). RUN: the cohort is 236 adults and only 4 paediatric cases, so the concern was near-moot -- but the check cost two minutes and the result is cleaner than the original. Adults only: whole_head_exponent -0.228 [-0.360, -0.092] adj -0.236; lempel_ziv -0.188 [-0.307, -0.057] adj -0.197; spectral_edge_95 +0.235 [+0.100, +0.366] adj +0.246; exponent_low -0.084 [-0.222, +0.048] still includes zero. **All three supported effects STRENGTHEN or hold on restriction, and the adjustment still moves nothing.** The finding is not paediatric-driven, and the non-monotonicity caveat is retired rather than merely acknowledged.
THE_ALTERNATIVE_EXPLANATION_THAT_MUST_LE: **An age relation at matched BIS does NOT by itself show BIS is mis-calibrated.** The aperiodic exponent declines with age in ordinary AWAKE resting EEG -- E47 measured -0.0054/yr [-0.0074, -0.0034] on 745 healthy adults through this same pipeline. So a measure that differs by age under anaesthesia may simply be carrying its ordinary baseline age dependence through, with BIS neither creating nor removing it. This design cannot separate 'BIS is mis-calibrated for age' from 'BIS does not remove a baseline age effect that was always there'. **The distinction matters less than it appears, because the REMEDY is the same either way** -- a per-patient expectation subtracts the baseline, and a fixed 40-60 band cannot. So E55 supports the reference's structural rationale for Challenge C while NOT supporting the stronger claim that the monitor is broken. Reporting it as the latter would be an over-claim.
deposit: VitalDB vitaldb_grid.csv: 2,877 maintenance windows inside the 40-60 target band with the sensor attached, aggregated to 240 CASES (age is a case property, so window-level analysis would be pseudo-replication). Ages 1-89, median 59; mean BIS in band 46.9.
gates: G1: >=60 cases (240 available)
P3 CONFOUND GATE: P1 repeated with anaesthetic agent, ASA, sex and BMI additionally partialled out. If the age relation collapses it was drug and comorbidity.
P4 PLACEBO: age permuted across cases, 2,000 draws, 95th percentile of |rho|.
incumbent: BIS itself. Its own age relation is rho = -0.100 unadjusted, and the P2 asymmetry partial(BIS, age | candidate) is reported per candidate.
limitations: Between-case comparison, so every unmeasured case-level confound is open; the four measured ones do not explain it. VitalDB is two frontal channels at 128 Hz, maintenance only. Age 1-89 includes paediatric cases where the exponent's age relation is known to reverse (PMID 36739102), which was not modelled -- a monotone rank correlation across a non-monotone relation is conservative but crude, and restricting to adults is the obvious sensitivity arm.
outcome: positive for 3 of 6, and the confound gate is passed cleanly
outcome_detail: SUPPORTED: whole_head_exponent P1 -0.212 [-0.338, -0.077], adjusted -0.211; lempel_ziv -0.204 [-0.323, -0.076], adjusted -0.209; spectral_edge_95 +0.216 [+0.087, +0.346], adjusted +0.223. REFUTED (CI includes zero): exponent_low -0.066, exponent_high -0.110, relative_alpha_power -0.096. Placebo ~0.123-0.130 throughout, well below the three supported effects. **THE CONFOUND GATE IS THE STRONGEST PART: adjusting for anaesthetic agent, ASA, sex and BMI changes the three supported estimates by at most 0.007** (-0.212 -> -0.211, -0.204 -> -0.209, +0.216 -> +0.223). The age relation is not older-patients-get-different-drugs.
primary: P1: partial Spearman(candidate, age | BIS) across cases, case-level, 20,000 bootstrap.
question: Does BIS 40-60 mean the same EEG state at every age? If not, the fixed target is systematically mis-centred by age, which is the one defect a per-patient reference could repair (REFERENCE_AGAINST_ALL_THREE §3).

RERUN_WITH_THE_FIX: The two design defects were fixed as specified -- k in {12,20,30,40} so every level is a genuine subsample with equal averaging, and a bootstrapped SLOPE of r on sqrt(rho_k) replacing the ratio. RESULT: r(lrtc_alpha) = 0.113, 0.181, 0.196, 0.222 at k = 12, 20, 30, 40 -- **MONOTONE across all four levels**, with the k=45 artefact gone. r(exponent_low) = 0.041, -0.159, -0.116, -0.081, no growth. Slopes: marker +0.508 [-0.271, +1.262] P(<=0) = 0.100; incumbent -0.526 [-1.373, +0.354] P(<=0) = 0.879. DIFFERENCE of slopes, the contrast that controls for the subsampling procedure itself: **+1.034 [-0.063, +2.233], P(<=0) = 0.0305** -- the interval grazes zero at -0.063 while the one-sided probability is 0.03.
VERDICT_WORDING_CORRECTED: The rerun still printed 'REFUTED' because the marker's own slope interval includes zero. **That word is wrong and was changed in the script.** Rule 31: a test that fails its own gate yields an ABSENT verdict, not a negative one. Calling this refuted would tell the investigator to abandon the better-labels route on evidence that leans -- weakly -- the other way: the curve is monotone in the predicted direction at every step, and the marker-minus-incumbent contrast reaches P = 0.03 one-sided. The correct statement is UNDERPOWERED.
WHAT_THE_EVIDENCE_ACTUALLY_SUPPORTS: Weakly consistent with attenuation, not decisive. The growth from k=12 to k=30 is monotone and in the predicted direction, and **the incumbent shows no growth whatever** (slope -0.335 against +0.596). That contrast is the strongest part: if the growth were an artefact of the subsampling procedure it would appear for exponent_low too, and it does not, so it is specific to the marker rather than to the method. But with 104 subjects the correlations carry intervals near +/-0.19, so 0.267 and 0.203 are not distinguishable, and the design cannot presently separate 'attenuated' from 'weak'.
WHY_THE_PRINTED_VERDICT_IS_REJECTED: The script printed 'REFUTED -- the correlation does not respond to label precision'. **Two defects in MY design make that unsafe and neither is a fact about the data.** (1) THE STATISTIC IS A RATIO OF CORRELATIONS. I chose r_k/r_45 because the predictor's reliability cancels in it, and paid for that with an uninterpretable interval: [-1.219, +1.802] at k=12. The verdict rule keyed on that interval containing 1.0, which it always would. A ratio whose denominator is itself uncertain is the wrong statistic and a monotone trend on the same numbers is far better behaved. (2) A DESIGN ASYMMETRY I INTRODUCED. At k=45 the subsample is ALL available trials, so the 12 draws differ only in fold assignment; at k<45 they differ in trial selection AND folds. Lower k therefore receives more variance reduction from averaging, biasing the curve in favour of mid-k -- which is very likely why r falls from 0.267 at k=30 to 0.203 at k=45. The k=45 anchor is not comparable to the others.
consequence: Challenge B's interpretive question remains open but the balance has shifted slightly toward attenuation. Concretely: the observed +0.2446 is consistent with a marker whose correlation rises as label precision rises, and the incumbent's flat/negative slope shows that growth is not an artefact of subsampling. What is still missing is POWER -- 104 subjects and four levels cannot resolve a slope. The decisive version needs more subjects with trial-level labels, which is Q14 (Stieger 2021: 62 subjects, 450 trials/session, demographics) rather than more work on eegmmidb.
deposit: eegmmidb, fully local: 104 subjects with >=45 imagery trials and both resting markers; trial-level features and labels from the committed shards.
incumbent: exponent_low, the measure used before E42.
limitations: Subsampling reduces the DATA behind a label, which is what the attenuation model describes, but does not reproduce the other ways a real label could be better -- more sessions, cleaner paradigm, better-instructed subjects. Growth consistent with Spearman-Brown would show the correlation responds to label precision, not that label noise is the ONLY limit.
outcome: suggestive but not decisive -- attenuation NOT DEMONSTRATED and NOT REFUTED
outcome_detail: r(lrtc_alpha) by k: 0.081, 0.185, 0.267, 0.203 at k = 12, 20, 30, 45. It GROWS from k=12 to k=30 in the direction attenuation predicts, then drops at k=45. r(exponent_low): -0.012, -0.105, -0.092, -0.099 -- FLAT. Slope of r on sqrt(rho_k): lrtc_alpha +0.596, exponent_low -0.335.
primary: Recompute each subject's label from k in {12,20,30,45} trials using E38's OWN out-of-fold estimator (imported, not reimplemented, rule 20), averaged over 12 draws; correlate with the resting marker. Spearman-Brown gives a PARAMETER-FREE prediction of the growth curve from E38's rho_45 = 0.2918.
question: Is Challenge B's marker ATTENUATED by a noisy label -- fixable by better labels -- or simply WEAK? E38's ceiling is arithmetic from a reliability coefficient; nobody had tested whether the correlation BEHAVES like an attenuated one.

ONE_GENUINE_POSITIVE_AND_IT_WAS_NOT_PRED: **Age and sex explain MORE in HEEDB than in the open cohorts.** exponent_low R^2 0.2547 here against E54's 0.0877 -- gain 1.157 against 1.047 -- and exponent_low_robust 0.2081 against 0.1473. The cohort spans age 0-90 with SD 24.1 years where the open adult cohorts span 18-70, and more age variance yields more explainable variance. So the conditional reference is better than E54 measured, while remaining modest and driven entirely by covariates already in hand.
WHY_MEDICATION_EXPLAINS_NOTHING_AND_IT_I: I characterised the ATC chapters as running at 44-64 % prevalence, which is true across the FULL 108,666-patient medication table. **In this cohort they run at 78.5 % mean prevalence, and the nervous-system chapter at 89.4 %.** A binary predictor's variance is p(1-p), maximal at 0.250 and collapsing as p approaches 1: nervous-system drugs carry variance 0.095 against sex's 0.250, and 4 of 14 chapters fall below 0.15. **The covariate hypothesised to matter most is nearly CONSTANT in the population that would be scored.** NORMAL_REFERENCE_COVARIATES §2 argued its near-universality is why it cannot be an EXCLUSION; the same fact makes it weak as a COVARIATE, because a predictor that barely varies cannot explain much variance whatever its true per-patient effect on the EEG. That is a structural reason for the null, not a measurement failure, and it would not be fixed by a better medication table at chapter level -- only by per-drug, per-visit dosing, which HEEDB does not carry.
consequence: **The full HEEDB reference build is not justified by any evidence now available.** REFERENCE_VALUE_MEASURED.md measured the general argument at single-digit percent and named exactly one surviving hypothesis; it is refuted at full n on its own data, and the reason is structural (near-zero covariate variance) rather than a power problem. Keep from the reference thread: exponent_low_robust as the measure (E45 ICC 0.841, E44 retains 98.4 % of eye-state sensitivity, highest covariate R^2 here at 0.2081), and E55's finding that a fixed BIS target is not age-neutral, which stands independently.
deposit: HEEDB strict-normal, Routine service, random sample; 313 recordings with a usable 180 s window. 14 ATC level-1 chapters, 18 ICD-10 chapters, age and sex.
gates: G1 CONFOUND GATE (run first, can kill the analysis): regress window_start_s -- how far into the recording a usable window was found -- on each block. Sicker, more medicated patients plausibly have more artefact, and if that tracked the covariates their R^2 would index data quality rather than brain state, in exactly the direction of the hypothesis. PASSED: oof R^2 AGE_SEX -0.0348, MEDICATION -0.0729, COMORBIDITY -0.1007, all negative.
incumbent: AGE_SEX (age, age^2, sex) -- E54's comparator, measured at best R^2 0.147 on the open cohorts.
limitations: The medication table is per PATIENT and per ATC CHAPTER -- 'ever prescribed' rather than 'on board during this recording', pooling a benzodiazepine with a paracetamol. That is blunt and biases toward the null, so this negative is the weaker of the two possible results; a per-visit, per-drug table could in principle change it. The 180 s window is not vigilance-controlled (94.8% of recordings contain sleep; Q21 showed the metadata cannot locate it), so residual variance is inflated for every block alike -- blocks are comparable to each other but absolute R^2 values are floors. INTERIM at 313 of 600 rows.
outcome_detail: FINAL AT n = 556. AGE_SEX WINS FOR ALL NINE MEASURES. exponent_low +0.2547 against medication -0.0329 and comorbidity -0.0125; exponent_low_robust +0.2081 against -0.0513 and +0.0065; rel_alpha +0.1135; lempel_ziv +0.0716; sef95 +0.0529; whole_head_exponent +0.0433; alpha_peak_hz +0.0333; exponent_high +0.0346; lrtc_alpha -0.0113. Medication is NEGATIVE out-of-fold for all nine and comorbidity for six of nine -- they predict worse than the sample mean. The bootstrapped margin excludes zero on the NEGATIVE side for exponent_low (-0.2671 [-0.2981, -0.1493]), exponent_low_robust (-0.2016 [-0.2610, -0.1121]), lempel_ziv (-0.1095 [-0.1281, -0.0079]) and rel_alpha (-0.1605 [-0.1569, -0.0199]): reliably WORSE, not merely no better. G1 confound gate PASSED (oof R2 on window_start_s: AGE_SEX +0.0229, MEDICATION -0.0332, COMORBIDITY -0.0170).
primary: OUT-OF-FOLD (5-fold) R^2 per covariate block per measure. Cross-validated because 35 predictors against a few hundred rows would inflate an in-sample R^2 by construction; a negative value means the block predicts worse than the sample mean.
question: Do MEDICATION and COMORBIDITY explain more EEG variance than age and sex? The one test that could justify the full HEEDB reference build, specified in REFERENCE_VALUE_MEASURED.md before the data existed.
status: FINAL, n = 556 (600 sampled, 44 rejected for having no window with plausible amplitude)

deposit: vitaldb (250-case grid, maintenance only) — vitaldb_bis.csv joined to vitaldb_grid.csv
gates: M1 join integrity: meta_bis must agree exactly between the two tables and >=90% of grid windows must join
M2 capability: each subparameter finite on >=50% of windows with non-zero variance; a constant column is dropped and reported unusable (rule 32)
outcome_detail:
NO GAIN by the pre-registered rule, and it was close. Out-of-bag median|err| increment C-A = -0.195 BIS units [-0.424, +0.035] over 400 refit draws: the point estimate favours the subparameters, the interval does not exclude zero, and the rule says NO GAIN. The bar does not move afterwards (rule 30).

BOTH MACHINERY GATES PASSED AND ONE PASSED AGAINST THE REGISTRATION S OWN PREDICTION. M1: 5,845 windows / 247 cases joined at 100.0% with 0 meta_bis disagreements. M2: all four subparameters finite on 100% of windows with non-zero variance, including bis_bsr, which the registration expected to fail the variance half. It did not fail, but it nearly did for the predicted reason — only 7.44% of maintenance windows carry any suppression at all (sd 0.0564).

WHAT THE ARMS ACTUALLY SHOW (case-grouped 5-fold, ridge, standardised on training rows only):
  A ours                 median|err| 4.81  mean 7.18  R2 0.343
  B subparams alone      median|err| 6.80  mean 9.21  R2 0.142
  C ours+subparams       median|err| 4.60  mean 6.86  R2 0.407
  D device (SR+EMG)      median|err| 6.28  mean 8.46  R2 0.246
  E all                  median|err| 4.52  mean 6.57  R2 0.450
The probe s central finding survives at higher precision: features computed independently from raw EEG predict device BIS better than the device s own reported subparameters (4.81 vs 6.28). Arm A is 18 columns of which 3 (uce_v1, wpli_alpha, spatial_participation_ratio) are ALL-NaN on this single-channel deposit, so the working set is 15.

THE PLACEBO BEHAVED, WHICH MAKES THE NEAR-MISS READABLE. Shuffling the four subparameter columns within case gives +0.004 [-0.079, +0.085] — a tight null centred on zero. So the -0.195 point estimate is window-level tracking, not four extra columns of case-level information. The result is an underpowered positive rather than a flat nothing, but the registered verdict is NO GAIN and stands.

THE RESULT THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE PRIMARY, AND IT IS THE PER-BAND TABLE. Arm C fidelity by device BIS band: [0,40) n=2330 median|err| 5.48; [40,60) n=2879 median|err| 3.47; [60,80) n=468 median|err| 8.75; [80,100) n=168 median|err| 29.84. Inside the clinical target band the index is good — 3.47 against Lee et al. s 4.1 on their own development data. CORRECTION, made before this outcome was pushed: the [80,100) row was first read as failure to detect wakefulness, and that reading is WITHDRAWN. E22 closed at its gate on exactly this population — every BIS>=80 window in VitalDB is a facial-EMG artefact — and re-measuring inside E58 s own analysis set rather than trusting E22 confirms it: 98.2% of the 168 windows exceed E46 s artefact threshold (meta_emg >= 32.3), median EMG 48.6 against 26.8 in the target band, median SQI 69.9 against 93.7. The row therefore measures failure to reproduce a device reading that is being driven by muscle, which an EEG-only index has no mechanism to reproduce; that is a property of the reference, not a defect of the index. Handing the model the device s own EMG channel (arm E) recovers 5.1 of the ~30 units and no more. The corrected reading makes the deposit s limit sharper: VitalDB contains NO genuine awake-under-monitor windows, so fidelity at the light end is untestable here rather than undermeasured.

THE PRIMARY STATISTIC WAS THE WRONG ONE TO HAVE REGISTERED, AND SAYING SO CHANGES NOTHING ABOUT THE VERDICT. Median absolute error is the statistic least sensitive to the tail, and the tail is where this index fails. The registered comparison therefore asked whether the subparameters help at the centre, where there was least room; on mean|err| (7.18 -> 6.86) and R2 (0.343 -> 0.407) the same fit improves visibly. Those are descriptive, were not registered as decisive, and are not being promoted to a verdict — recorded because rule 30 says a rule can be correctly followed and still have been set to measure the wrong thing.

TWO DECLARED FAILURE CONDITIONS TESTED AND NOT MET: bis_bsr agrees in direction with the device s own BIS/SR track (Spearman 0.410, n=5798); bis_quazi is not a second copy of bis_bsr (Pearson 0.050, Spearman 0.110, far below the 0.9 that would have collapsed the pair).
placebo: the four subparameter columns permuted ACROSS WINDOWS WITHIN CASE, arm C refitted — preserves every case-level marginal and destroys moment-to-moment alignment
primary: out-of-bag change in case-grouped median absolute error against device BIS, arm C (ours+subparams) minus arm A (ours); negative = better
question: Does adding BIS's three missing ingredients (relative beta ratio, QUAZI, SyncFastSlow) improve a from-scratch BIS-like index over the features this repo already had?

deposit: DOSE-I (Zenodo 18483292) — raw 125 Hz EEG read member-by-member over HTTP range requests, beside the depositors' 1 Hz pEEG series
gates: M1 coverage: >=30 recordings with >=100 windows finite on both implementations
outcome_detail:
AGREE. sync_fast_slow reproduces an independent implementation, in the orientation predicted from the parameter description rather than from the data. 38 usable recordings, 12,469 windows.

V1 PRIMARY  median within-recording Spearman(ours, theirs) = -0.5875 [-0.6466, -0.5309]. The sign was fixed in advance by DOSE-I's own documentation -- their SynchFastSlow is the quotient 40-47 Hz over 1-47 Hz, the reciprocal of the Rampil form implemented here -- so a negative relation was the registered prediction, and the INVERTED branch (agreeing in magnitude but running the same way) was a live failure mode the verdict code enumerated first.

P1 PLACEBO  our series circularly shifted 600 s inside its own recording gives +0.0339 [-0.0248, +0.1363] -- flat, interval spanning zero. The agreement depends on the two series describing the same moment, which is exactly what a correlation between two smooth autocorrelated series most needed to prove.

V2 SPECIFICITY, AND IT IS THE MORE INTERESTING NUMBER. Partialling out the depositors' OWN PowerFastSlow -- a pure power ratio over the identical bands -- reduces the agreement from -0.5875 to -0.2706 [-0.3496, -0.2327]. It does NOT abolish it: the interval still excludes zero decisively. So the two implementations share a substantial component that is NOT the power ratio, and a larger component that is. This is the first empirical statement in this project about how much of SyncFastSlow is bispectral rather than spectral, and it bears on BIS itself, whose name rests on that distinction. The printed NOTE ("both may be tracking power rather than phase coupling") is the harsher of the two readings available and the numbers do not require it; the accurate statement is that a real bispectrum-specific component exists and is smaller than the power-shared one.

WHAT THIS LICENCES: the COMPUTATIONAL verifier layer for bis_sfs, which is the only layer its declaration requires, and nothing else. It is not evidence about what SFS measures in either implementation, and nothing here is about consciousness, depth or any clinical quantity.

EXCLUSIONS, REPORTED (rule 14). 21 of 60 attempted recordings were refused by the extractor's uniform-time-axis check (>1% disagreement between elapsed wall time and sample count). Two were examined directly: 10-011 carries an 82.8 s hole among 4 gaps; 10-030 carries 13 gaps totalling 15.7 s. The gaps are real and the refusal is correct -- assuming a uniform axis would have misaligned every window after the hole against the depositors' 1 Hz series (rule 27). The criterion reads only the raw file's own timestamps and cannot see either SFS series, so it cannot be related to the agreement statistic. A gap-aware extractor would recover roughly a third more recordings and is the obvious improvement.

WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT TESTED: bis_sfs's registered direction on unconscious_vs_awake. A feasibility probe the same day had already read the depositors' SFS against SOC, so a prediction registered afterwards would have been a prediction about a number already seen. It is recorded in QUEUE.md as a probe, descriptive; the directional claim stays untested on this deposit.
placebo: our series circularly shifted 600 s within its own recording — preserves every marginal and every autocorrelation, destroys the alignment
primary: median across recordings of within-recording Spearman(ours, theirs); PREDICTED STRONGLY NEGATIVE because their quotient is the reciprocal of Rampil's
question: Does this repo's sync_fast_slow reproduce an INDEPENDENT implementation of SyncFastSlow (DOSE-I column 33), in the orientation its parameter description predicts?

deposit: vitaldb (250-case grid, maintenance only) — vitaldb_bis.csv joined to vitaldb_grid.csv
gates: M1 separation: every predicted band must receive >=5% of rows, or the two-stage model IS the one-stage model
instrument_changed: the model class: one global ridge replaced by a sub-model selected from a first-pass prediction. Cohort, target, folds and error statistic are unchanged from E58.
outcome_detail:
GAIN, and it is a REALLOCATION rather than a free improvement -- which the registered primary was not built to see.

PRIMARY  median |err| on true BIS in [0,40), two-stage minus one-stage = -0.635 [-1.035, -0.203] over 400 out-of-bag draws with both models refitted per draw. Point estimates 5.482 -> 4.764. M1 passed with predicted-band shares 0.306 / 0.643 / 0.051 and stage 2 never fell back for want of training rows.

PLACEBO  a RANDOM partition of the same sizes -- same sub-model count, same parameter budget, no range information -- gives +0.020 [-0.167, +0.248]. Flat. So the gain is range specificity, not extra parameters.

THE COST THE PRIMARY COULD NOT SEE, and it is the reason this outcome is not simply positive. Descriptive slicing after the run: [20,30) 9.69 -> 8.88; [30,35) 6.15 -> 5.14; [35,40) 3.37 -> 2.82 -- the gain is spread across the band rather than sitting at its boundary, which is the good news. But [40,60) goes 3.47 -> 3.91, WORSE by +0.44 on 2,879 windows. The two-stage model trades target-band accuracy for deep-band accuracy. The registration fixed the falsification condition to [0,40) "and nowhere else", which correctly stopped the bar from moving -- and equally stopped the experiment from seeing what it gave up. A band-restricted primary cannot distinguish an improvement from a reallocation. Logged as error-catalogue rule 52.

THE DISCOVERY THAT MATTERS MOST IS NOT ABOUT THE MODEL AT ALL. The [0,20) sub-band carries median |err| 39.96 under BOTH models -- neither touches it -- on 90 windows from 68 cases. Its median SQI is 5.1 out of 100. The device is reporting a BIS value it simultaneously flags as almost entirely unreliable, with EMG elevated at 38.2. This is the MIRROR IMAGE of the [80,100) finding at the other end of the scale: not a deep-anaesthesia population the index fails on, but a population where the reference itself has collapsed. E58's inclusion criterion was BIS present and sensor not off; SQI was shipped in the same table and was never used. E58's and E60's verdicts stand as registered, and their reported errors are if anything PESSIMISTIC in those bands, but the deliverable index's error bars should be quoted from an SQI-filtered cohort -- registered separately, because changing inclusion after seeing results is a change of cohort and not a footnote.

DESCRIPTIVE, unregistered: pooled median |err| also improves, 4.599 -> 4.516, and [60,101) improves 11.50 -> 9.50. The latter is not claimed -- that band is 35-98% facial-EMG artefact and BIS_FAITHFUL_OR_BRAIN_FAITHFUL.md refuses it on separate evidence.
placebo: stage 2 refitted on a RANDOM partition of the same sizes — same sub-model count and parameter budget, no range information
primary: out-of-bag change in median absolute error evaluated on TRUE BIS in [0,40), two-stage minus one-stage; negative = better
question: Does a range-specific ridge, with the range chosen from a first-pass PREDICTION rather than the true target, beat one global fit in the deep clean band [0,40)?

deposit: vitaldb — single-agent cases, propofol (42) vs sevoflurane (67), BIS [40,60), SQI >= 50, 1,306 windows / 109 cases
gates: M1 capability: every candidate finite on >=90% of windows with non-zero variance
