M2 state control (E36's): the phase family's state discrimination must reach 50% of the amplitude family's, or 'leaks less' is 'measures less'
instrument_changed: the phase family: E36 tested INTER-channel wPLI, which is NaN on this one-channel deposit; this tests WITHIN-channel phase (bispectrum, phase-amplitude coupling) on a different deposit with different agents.
outcome_detail:
NO SPLIT by the registered rule -- and a post-hoc diagnostic shows the null is UNINFORMATIVE about E36 rather than evidence against it, because there was no leak in either family to split.

PRIMARY  mean |AUC-0.5| phase minus amplitude = -0.0116 [-0.0589, +0.1273] over 200 case-clustered draws. Includes zero. Partition control: the real 2-vs-7 split ranks 14 of 36 same-size partitions, p = 0.3889 -- against E36's own split ranking as the unique maximum at p = 0.002. Both machinery gates passed (M1 all nine candidates finite on 100% with non-zero variance; M2 phase state discrimination 0.0478 against amplitude 0.0951, exactly at the 50% floor).

THE DIAGNOSTIC THAT CHANGES THE READING, run after the verdict and changing nothing about it. Permuting the agent label across cases 60 times gives a per-candidate null for |AUC-0.5|, and NOT ONE OF THE NINE CANDIDATES EXCEEDS ITS OWN NULL: p(>=observed) ranges 0.233 to 0.883, and the AMPLITUDE family's observed 0.0903 sits BELOW its null mean of 0.0960 (p = 0.583). The largest observed value in the whole table, whole_head_exponent at 0.1438, has p = 0.233.

So the substantive finding is not about families at all: AT MATCHED BIS, PROPOFOL AND SEVOFLURANE ARE NOT LEGIBLE FROM ANY OF THESE NINE FRONTAL MEASURES, out-of-fold with cases held out whole. That is a clean negative and it is mildly FAVOURABLE to Challenge A -- but it means this cohort cannot test E36's split, because a contrast between two families needs at least one family to show the effect.

WHY THE DEPOSIT PROBABLY CANNOT, and it is checkable rather than an excuse. E36's leak was measured on propofol vs DEXMEDETOMIDINE, an alpha-2 agonist producing a pharmacologically distinct sleep-like state. This is propofol vs sevoflurane -- both GABAergic, at matched depth. The remaining VitalDB pairs are desflurane vs propofol and sevoflurane vs desflurane, which are the same GABAergic class or volatile against volatile, so no pairing available here escapes the problem. Challenge A's family question needs a pharmacologically distinct agent: the Dryad ketamine set (Q2) or the Turku dexmedetomidine cohort (data request drafted, unsent).

THE GATE THIS EXPERIMENT SHOULD HAVE HAD ALREADY EXISTED IN THIS PROJECT. E33's machinery gate (c) reads "THE INCUMBENT MUST BE ALIVE -- if the incumbent cannot predict the transition at all, beating it is not a result." E61 gated on capability and on state discrimination and never asked whether the phenomenon being compared was present. Logged as error-catalogue rule 53. The permutation null that establishes it costs one extra loop over the same code.
placebo: agent label permuted ACROSS CASES (fixes the folded statistic null level), plus enumeration of all 36 same-size partitions
primary: mean |AUC-0.5| for agent identity, phase family minus amplitude family, out-of-fold with cases held out whole; negative = phase leaks less
question: Do WITHIN-channel phase measures (bis_sfs, pac_slow_alpha) leak less anaesthetic identity than amplitude summaries at matched depth, extending E36's inter-channel finding?

deposit: vitaldb — 5,845 windows / 247 cases, meta_sqi finite on 100%
gates: G1 survival, evaluated and printed BEFORE the primary: >=30 windows and >=15 cases must remain in [0,20), or a fidelity on the remnant is a selection effect and no error figure may be quoted
instrument_changed: the inclusion criterion: meta_sqi, a column shipped in the same table since the first extraction and never used by any experiment.
outcome_detail:
BAND EMPTIED -- G1 fired and the experiment stopped there, which is what it was written to do.

SURVIVAL AT SQI >= 50, per band, printed before any fidelity:
  [ 0, 20)     90 ->    14  (15.6%)   10 cases   median SQI  5.1
  [20, 40)   2240 ->  2138  (95.4%)  228 cases   median SQI 91.7
  [40, 60)   2879 ->  2792  (97.0%)  240 cases   median SQI 93.7
  [60, 80)    468 ->   448  (95.7%)  183 cases   median SQI 91.6
  [80,100)    168 ->   133  (79.2%)   93 cases   median SQI 69.9

84.4% of the [0,20) windows fail the monitor's own quality flag, against 3-5% in every band from 20 to 80. The registered gate needed 30 windows and 15 cases and got 14 and 10, so NO FIDELITY FIGURE WAS COMPUTED on the remnant and none may be quoted. That refusal is the result and it is stronger than a number: E60's median |err| of 39.96 below BIS 20 was the index being scored against readings the device itself declares unreliable.

THE PICTURE FOR CHALLENGE C IS NOW COMPLETE AND SYMMETRIC, WITH TWO DIFFERENT FAILURE MODES AT THE TWO ENDS AND A CLEAN MIDDLE:
  * the BOTTOM fails on SIGNAL QUALITY -- 84.4% of [0,20) below SQI 50;
  * the TOP fails on MUSCLE -- 98.2% of [80,100) above E46's EMG threshold, 35.0% of [60,80), while both bands retain 79-96% of their windows under the SQI filter, so their failure is NOT a quality-flag failure;
  * the MIDDLE, [20,60), is clean on both criteria: 95-97% SQI survival and 4.6-5.6% artefact.
Each end was diagnosed by a different measured criterion and neither diagnosis transfers to the other, which is why both had to be measured.

WHAT WAS NOT DONE, AND DELIBERATELY. Filtered fidelities for the usable bands were NOT computed, because the registered gate stopped the experiment and continuing past a fired gate is exactly what the gate exists to prevent. The retention figures above (95-97% in [20,60)) mean E58's and E60's published figures already rest on a cohort that is >=95% SQI-clean, so they are quotable as they stand; a filtered refit is available as a successor if a tighter number is ever wanted, and it has not been run.

NO REFUSAL CHANGES. BIS_FAITHFUL_OR_BRAIN_FAITHFUL.md already refused below 20 and above 60. This decides what the lower refusal is FOR.
placebo: none — the differential IS the control: taking the target band as reference is what stops a global filtering improvement being read as a deep-band explanation
primary: relative change in median |err| in [0,20) minus the relative change in [40,60) under SQI >= 50; negative = reference collapse
question: Is the BIS-like index's failure below BIS 20 the index's problem or the reference's? The monitor's own SQI flag decides.

deposit: Stieger 2021 (figshare 13123148, CC BY 4.0) — 186 sessions across 62 subjects, labels only, no EEG touched
gates: G1 coverage: >=40 sessions with both halves, >=20 subjects, >=20 consecutive-session pairs
G2 split validity: mean |odd-even| <= 0.05 and no systematically signed difference — non-exchangeable halves make a correlation between them not a reliability
instrument_changed: the deposit: 450 scored trials per session against eegmmidb 45 in total, and test-retest across sessions in addition to split-half.
outcome_detail:
ABSENT at G2, the exchangeability gate, which is the gate working. Over 185 sessions the signed odd-minus-even difference is +0.0094 (t = +2.68): the first trial of each pair scores systematically higher than the second. Diagnosed rather than assumed -- the bias appears in sessions with an odd number of scored trials (+0.0085) and an even number (+0.0104) alike, so it is not the artefact of one half receiving an extra trial. Something in the task alternates. A correlation between non-exchangeable halves is not a reliability, so NO reliability was reported. G1 passed (185 sessions, 62 subjects, 122 pairs) and the magnitude half of G2 passed too (mean |odd-even| 0.0397 against a 0.05 bound); it was the signed test that failed.

ONE THING ABOUT THE GATE WAS BADLY CHOSEN AND IS RECORDED RATHER THAN QUIETLY FIXED. |t| < 2 is a SIGNIFICANCE criterion: it asks whether a bias is detectable, not whether it is material, and at n = 185 it detects under one percentage point. A design whose gate tightens as data accumulates punishes its own sample size; an equivalence bound was the right form. That flaw was NOT used to rescue this verdict.

SUPERSEDED IN ESTIMATOR, NOT IN VERDICT, by E68, which removes the split entirely using the analytic binomial correction and reports R1 = 0.9652 [0.9568, 0.9706].
placebo: none applicable — this is a reliability measurement, and its control is the registered comparison against E38 on the same statistic
primary: R1, within-session odd-vs-even split-half of session accuracy, Spearman-Brown corrected, subject-clustered bootstrap. FALSIFIED if its lower bound falls below 0.4345, the upper bound of eegmmidb reliability measured in E38.
question: Is Stieger's BCI-ability label decisively more reliable than eegmmidb's, and by how much does it lift E41's attenuation ceiling?

deposit: vitaldb two-channel (BIS/EEG1_WAV + BIS/EEG2_WAV) — 1,304 windows / 109 cases at BIS [40,60), SQI >= 50
gates: M1 aliveness (rule 53), evaluated first: coherence_theta must clear its OWN permutation null, or the differential is a difference of two nulls
instrument_changed: the measure family: INTER-channel connectivity from the second BIS EEG channel, which E61 could not compute because the grid adapter returned one channel.
outcome_detail:
NOT INFORMATIVE -- M1 fired first and ended the experiment, which is what it was written to do. No differential was computed.

coherence_theta scored |AUC-0.5| = 0.0275 against its own permutation null (mean 0.1170, p95 0.1893): p = 0.967, i.e. it sits FAR BELOW the null level rather than above it. It carries no agent information for a theta-minus-alpha differential to be about.

THE OTHER THREE COLUMNS SAY THE SAME THING. coherence_alpha 0.1144, wpli_theta 0.1417, wpli_alpha 0.1406 -- all at or within the null (mean 0.1170, p95 0.1893). Nothing in the connectivity family separates the drugs here.

THE FEASIBILITY PROBE HAD ALREADY KILLED THE ORIGINAL DESIGN, BEFORE REGISTRATION. Over 4,220 usable windows, wPLI is centred on zero with symmetric spread in every band (medians 0.0015-0.0235, IQRs straddling zero) and |rho| with the monitor never exceeds 0.05 -- a noise distribution, because two electrodes about 2 cm apart on a shared reference have no consistent phase lag. Coherence varies (sd ~0.16) but sits at 0.60-0.66 in EVERY band with no band-specific structure, the signature of a shared reference rather than frontal network coupling. So E36's family split is permanently untestable on this deposit, and E64 was narrowed in advance to Akeju's band differential, which a reference-dominated coherence can in principle still support because the shared contribution cancels.

WHAT THIS CLOSES, AND IT IS NOW MEASURED FROM THREE DIRECTIONS. Combined with E61, THIRTEEN measures spanning amplitude summaries, complexity, within-channel phase, inter-channel coherence and inter-channel wPLI have now failed to separate propofol from sevoflurane at matched BIS on VitalDB, none of them clearing its own permutation null. The three independent reasons are all established rather than asserted: (1) the agents sit in DISJOINT patients, 0 of 247 cases carrying more than one; (2) both drugs are GABAergic, and Akeju et al. (PMID 25233374) report alpha power and coherence as effectively identical between them (peak coherence 0.73 vs 0.71) with slow oscillations showing no significant difference, so the published expectation is that most measures should NOT separate them; (3) the montage is a two-electrode strip that supports neither wPLI nor band-specific coherence.

VitalDB cannot answer Challenge A's family question. That is not a failure of any measure and it is not evidence against E36 -- it is a property of the deposit, and it makes the case for a pharmacologically distinct agent decisive: the Dryad ketamine set (Q2) or the Turku/Kallionpaa dexmedetomidine cohort, whose data request is drafted and still unsent.

SECOND OCCURRENCE OF RULE 53 IN ONE SESSION, and the two are instructive together: in E61 the aliveness problem was found post hoc by a permutation null run after a NO SPLIT verdict; here the same check was a registered gate that fired before anything was computed. The rule was written between them.
placebo: agent permuted across cases; plus the same differential on wPLI reported as an ungated sensitivity arm
primary: |AUC-0.5| for agent identity from coherence_theta MINUS the same from coherence_alpha; PREDICTED POSITIVE per Akeju (PMID 25233374)
question: Does Akeju's theta-over-alpha coherence differential separate propofol from sevoflurane at matched depth on VitalDB's two-channel BIS strip?

deposit: six committed feature tables — chennu, ds004541, eegmmidb, hbn, dosei, vitaldb
gates: G1 coverage: a feature is scored only if >=4 deposits carry it with >=15 subjects each
outcome_detail:
H1 ABSENT as registered, and the R table it produced DOES NOT MEASURE TRANSPORTABILITY. The second half is the important part and it is a defect in my own design, found by checking which deposits actually contributed.

H1: Spearman(R, band_hi / lowest Nyquist) = +0.3669 [-0.3504, +0.8661] over 12 features. Includes zero. So exponent_gamma -- which literally fits 50-90 Hz above a 62.5 Hz Nyquist -- is a SPECIAL CASE rather than the extreme of a general gradient, and the anti-alias-rolloff account does not generalise. That verdict stands as registered.

THE R TABLE IS CONFOUNDED BY STATE AND AGE, AND THE CONFOUND IS THE SIGNAL. G1 admitted exactly four deposits per feature: chennu (sedated volunteers), eegmmidb (awake adults), hbn (awake CHILDREN, ages 5-20) and vitaldb (ANAESTHETISED surgical patients). lempel_ziv medians: hbn 0.228, vitaldb 0.441, eegmmidb 0.623, chennu 0.749. The hbn value is low because they are children and the vitaldb value is low because they are unconscious. **Those differences are the features WORKING, not failing to transport**, and R cannot tell the two apart.

So every R below is uninterpretable as a usability statistic: 10 of 12 features exceed 1 and all 12 exceed their shuffled null by 8.6x to 62x, but that is what four cohorts in different states and age ranges are SUPPOSED to look like. The registration named population as one of the things between-deposit spread confounds (rule 50) and then failed to act on it -- naming a confound is not controlling for it.

R values as computed, recorded for the successor to compare against and NOT as a usability ranking: pac_slow_alpha 2.561, lempel_ziv 2.342, exponent_high 2.206, critical_slowing_ar1 1.796, spectral_edge_95 1.747, multiscale_entropy_slope 1.673, whole_head_exponent 1.607, spectral_entropy 1.447, emg_index 1.374, relative_delta_power 1.217, exponent_low 0.987, relative_alpha_power 0.842.

WHAT A CORRECTED DESIGN NEEDS: cohorts matched on STATE (awake resting) and restricted in AGE, which means chennu at sedation level 1, eegmmidb, ds004541 pre-anaesthesia, DOSE-I at MOAA/S 5, and hbn restricted to its oldest subjects -- with vitaldb excluded entirely, since it contains no awake window at all. That is E67, registered as a successor with the cohort as the changed instrument.
placebo: deposit labels shuffled across subject-level rows — R has no natural null at 1, so the shuffled value is what "no deposit effect" looks like for this statistic
primary: H1: Spearman between R = (IQR of per-deposit medians)/(median within-deposit between-subject IQR) and the feature's upper band edge as a fraction of the lowest native Nyquist; PREDICTED POSITIVE
question: Which of this project's features survive a change of deposit, and is the failure explained by how close their band sits to the acquisition Nyquist?

deposit: Sleep-EDFx W vs N3 (142 subj), ds005620 awake vs sedated (21), ds004541 baseline vs post-LOC (8) — all within-subject
gates: G1 aliveness (rule 53), per feature: BOTH arms must show a d_z interval excluding zero, or the sign in the quiet arm is a coin flip
instrument_changed: the contrast: drug-vs-no-drug loss of consciousness, replacing drug-A-vs-drug-B which Q26 established VitalDB cannot support.
outcome_detail:
NOT INFORMATIVE as printed -- and the printed reason is wrong, because THE PLACEBO COULD NOT HAVE FAILED. The per-feature results survive and one of them is worth keeping.

THE PLACEBO IS INVALID (rule 40). It broke the within-subject pairing, which changes the VARIANCE of a paired difference and therefore d_z's magnitude -- but not its SIGN. A group mean difference keeps its direction whether subject i's N3 is paired with their own W or with subject j's. So a sign-agreement rate is mathematically insensitive to this shuffle, the placebo returned 0.500 against a real 0.500 by construction, and the verdict branch fired on an identity rather than on evidence. The correct placebo for a sign statistic permutes the STATE LABEL within subject, which does flip signs. Logged as rule 55.

THE PRIMARY WAS UNDERPOWERED ANYWAY. G1 removed relative_delta_power and spectral_entropy (each fails to move in one arm), leaving FOUR testable features. A binary sign comparison on four features has chance agreement 0.5 and the observed rate was 2/4. No agreement RATE computed from four features could have been informative, and that was knowable before the run from the feature intersection alone.

WHAT DOES SURVIVE, because each cell is a within-subject effect with its own bootstrap interval:
  lempel_ziv            sleep -2.281   propofol +1.551   GA +0.947   REVERSES, and BOTH drug arms agree with each other
  relative_alpha_power  sleep -0.501   propofol +1.184   GA -0.398   reverses against propofol, not against GA
  spectral_edge_95      sleep -2.868   propofol -0.923   GA +0.208   agrees with propofol; GA arm is null
  whole_head_exponent   sleep +4.008   propofol +1.110   GA +0.937   AGREES ACROSS ALL THREE ARMS

whole_head_exponent moving the same direction in natural N3 sleep, propofol sedation and general anaesthesia is the one clean positive here. lempel_ziv falling in sleep while RISING under both drugs is the one clean reversal, and it is corroborated by an independent second drug arm.

BUT THE REVERSAL IS CONFOUNDED BY DEPTH, AND THE REGISTRATION'S OWN PREMISE IS WHAT FAILS. The design argued a sign is depth-invariant "as long as the effect is monotone in depth". This project has evidence against that premise -- E31 was registered specifically to ask whether a sign reversal is a depth-range effect, and bis_rbr's declaration records beta activation rising into light sedation and collapsing after. ds005620's "sed" may be light sedation, where propofol's paradoxical excitation RAISES complexity, while N3 is deep. So lempel_ziv's reversal may be depth, not drug, and this design cannot separate them.

WHAT A CORRECTED SUCCESSOR NEEDS: depth matched between arms with a behavioural anchor present in both. Sleep-EDFx has staged depth; ds005620 has only awake/sed. DOSE-I's per-second MOAA/S is the only behavioural depth scale in hand and it is propofol-only. This is the same wall Challenge A keeps hitting, reached from a new direction.
placebo: within-subject pairing broken (each subject unconscious value paired against another subject conscious value), 200 draws
primary: per feature, sign agreement of the within-subject Cohen d_z between the drug and no-drug arms
question: Does a measure move the SAME way when consciousness falls with a drug (propofol, general anaesthesia) and without one (natural N3 sleep)?

deposit: Stieger 2021 — 185 sessions, 62 subjects, 122 consecutive-session pairs, labels only
gates: G1 coverage: >=40 sessions, >=20 subjects, >=20 consecutive pairs (carried from E63 unchanged)
G2 non-degeneracy: observed variance must exceed the binomial correction, or between-session differences are sampling error
instrument_changed: the ESTIMATOR: analytic binomial correction replacing odd/even split-half, because E63 proved the halves non-exchangeable. Threshold, cohort and horizon are unchanged.
outcome_detail:
PREMISE SUPPORTED, decisively, and this is the result that unblocks Challenge B.

R1 WITHIN-SESSION = 0.9652 [0.9568, 0.9706] against eegmmidb's 0.2918 [0.1163, 0.4345] -- no overlap of any kind. Observed between-session variance 0.018676 against binomial trial noise 0.000649, so G2 passes by a factor of 29. **The within-session attenuation ceiling rises from 0.5402 to 0.9825.**

R2 ACROSS-SESSION = 0.6539 [0.5282, 0.7361] over 122 consecutive pairs -> a subject-ability ceiling of 0.8087, also far above eegmmidb's. The gap between R1 and R2 is learning, which is what the deposit exists to study, and the two cap DIFFERENT designs: a session-level predictor is bounded by sqrt(R1), a stable-ability predictor nearer sqrt(R2).

E38'S CENTRAL CLAIM IS CONFIRMED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. E38 argued that reliability, not n, was Challenge B's binding constraint, and that more trials per subject buys more than more subjects. 450 trials per session against eegmmidb's 45 in total gives 0.965 against 0.292, on FEWER subjects (62 vs 109). The recommendation was right and is now measured.

A CAVEAT I WROTE INTO Q28 IS RETRACTED BY MEASUREMENT. Q28 proposed a within-subject design and warned that "a change score is noisier than a level -- this is not a free lunch". On this deposit it very nearly is: the consecutive-session change has variance 0.012706 against 0.001292 of doubled binomial noise, giving a CHANGE-SCORE RELIABILITY of 0.8983 and a ceiling of 0.9478. Because each session carries ~356 scored trials, differencing two near-noiseless measurements costs almost nothing. Q28's design is fully viable and its stated weakness does not apply here.

Supporting structure: mean consecutive-session change +0.0386 (real learning); between-subject variance is 71.4% of total session variance, leaving 28.6% within-subject for a change design to work with.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT ESTABLISH. It does NOT show a predictor exists. It establishes that E41's null -- rho = +0.0853 against a minimum detectable 0.272 -- cannot be blamed on label attenuation here, so a null measured on THIS deposit would be a real null rather than an artefact. That is precisely the condition Q14 said had to be met before running the correlation, and it is now met. The next step is the Stieger feature pass over the 2 s pre-cue baselines.

E63'S ABSENT VERDICT STANDS AND IS NOT SUPERSEDED. Its gate correctly refused a reliability from non-exchangeable halves; this experiment removed the split rather than the gate.
placebo: none applicable — a reliability measurement, controlled by the registered comparison against E38 on the same estimand
primary: binomial-corrected reliability R1 = (Var(acc) - mean[p(1-p)/n]) / Var(acc); FALSIFIED if its lower bound fails to clear 0.4345, eegmmidb upper bound from E38
question: Stieger's label ceiling, with a binomial-corrected estimator that requires no split — does it clear eegmmidb's?

deposit: Sleep-EDFx five-stage table — 142 subjects, W/N1/N2/N3/REM, within-subject
gates: G1 separation (rule 53): the W-vs-N3 paired contrast must exclude zero, or "which one REM resembles" is meaningless
outcome_detail:
SPLIT, and it lands on exactly one feature. Placebo 0.501 against a real mean of 0.664 over 12 testable features, so the grouping does depend on which state a value came from.

TEN FEATURES place REM with WAKE, which is the CHEAP outcome the registration named in advance: REM EEG is low-amplitude and desynchronised, so any spectral or complexity measure tends there for reasons unrelated to experience. Those ten are NOT evidence of anything about consciousness.

ONE FEATURE DEPARTS. exponent_high places REM with deep sleep in 88.7% of subjects: frac REM-nearer-W = 0.113 [0.064, 0.170], REM position 1.189 on the W->N3 axis -- past N3.

A GROUPING BUG WAS FOUND AND FIXED, AND IT CHANGED THE MEMBERSHIP. The first branch used `frac > 0.5` alone and filed pac_slow_alpha (0.426 [0.348, 0.511]) as "REM with deep sleep" on a point estimate whose interval INCLUDES CHANCE. That is rule 37's family -- a cell spanning the null is neither direction. Corrected to require the interval to exclude 0.5; pac_slow_alpha is now reported AMBIGUOUS and exponent_high is the sole departing feature.

THE MUSCLE EXPLANATION WAS TESTED AND FAILS AT SUBJECT LEVEL. REM has atonia, and exponent_high is fitted over 20-40 Hz where surface EMG lives (E43 established that a broadband slope through that band is MORE muscle-associated than BIS), so muscle was the obvious alternative. Subject-level REM position on exponent_high correlates with REM position on emg_index at rho = +0.068 (n = 140) -- essentially nothing. And the premise does not even hold in these channels: emg_index reads REM at 0.312, HIGHER than N3 at 0.127, so Fpz-Cz and Pz-Oz do not show atonia at all.

BUT THE STAGE MEDIANS REFRAME THE FINDING AND THE HONEST READING IS NARROWER THAN "BEHAVIOURAL OUTPUT". exponent_high: W = +0.070, N1 = +2.104, N2 = +1.985, N3 = +1.599, REM = +2.089. **Wake is the outlier and every sleep stage sits together.** exponent_high is not ordering depth -- its monotonicity check fails and its W-N3 d_z of 1.143 is the weakest of the alive features. What it separates is AWAKE from ASLEEP, with REM counted as asleep despite a wake-like spectrum. That is a defensible arousal-state boundary and it is NOT the same claim as tracking behavioural output.

THE GROUP-LEVEL MUSCLE EXPLANATION SURVIVES AND NEEDS A REAL EMG CHANNEL. emg_index is 0.444 at wake against 0.13-0.32 asleep, so wake does carry more scalp muscle, and a flatter 20-40 Hz slope at wake is what muscle would produce. The subject-level null above does not rule this out at the group level. **Sleep-EDFx PSG files ship a submental EMG channel and our extraction kept only EEG** -- so the decisive test is a re-extraction that carries it, and until that runs the arousal-boundary reading is a candidate rather than a conclusion (rule 50).

NOT A CONSCIOUSNESS DETECTOR. Sleep stage is scored FROM the EEG, so stage and signal are not independent. This measures how a feature orders three scorer-defined states.
placebo: stage labels permuted WITHIN subject — unlike a pairing shuffle this can actually move a fraction-nearer statistic (rule 55)
primary: per feature, the fraction of subjects for whom REM lies nearer W than N3, tested against 0.5 with a subject bootstrap
question: Does any measure place REM sleep with WAKE or with DEEP SLEEP? REM has experience without behavioural responsiveness, so it dissociates the two.

deposit: Sleep-EDFx — submental EMG at 1 Hz on exactly the 710 windows of the committed five-stage worklist, joined to the EEG feature table; 141 subjects with all five stages on both
gates: G1 instrument gate, evaluated first: the EMG channel must show wake above every sleep stage AND REM at or below N3 (atonia), or nothing about muscle can be concluded
instrument_changed: the control variable: a real submental EMG channel replacing emg_index, a scalp-EEG proxy that showed no REM atonia and so failed its own premise.
outcome_detail:
MUSCLE EXPLAINS MOST OF IT. The registered rule printed NOT INFORMATIVE and ITS TEXT MISDESCRIBES THE NUMBERS; the correction is below and it changes the reading.

G1 PASSED DECISIVELY AND THE INSTRUMENT IS VALIDATED. Submental EMG medians: W 3.063 > N1 2.559 > N2 1.472 > N3 1.104 > REM 0.6385. REM carries the LOWEST muscle tone of all five stages -- textbook atonia -- so this is a real muscle channel behaving as physiology says it should. E69's proxy could not do this: emg_index read REM at 0.312 against N3 0.127, i.e. no atonia at all.

S1 IS THE MOST DECISIVE SINGLE NUMBER AND IT HAS NO MODEL IN IT. REM's position on the W->N3 axis is +1.189 for exponent_high and +1.099 for submental EMG -- a difference of 0.090. The feature orders REM relative to wake and deep sleep almost exactly as muscle tone does.

THE PRIMARY, READ CORRECTLY. Distance from chance: 0.387 before adjustment, 0.160 after real-EMG adjustment, 0.280 after permuted-EMG adjustment. Real adjustment removes 58.7% of the distance from chance; the permuted placebo removes 27.6% mechanically; so roughly 31 points of the 39 are attributable to submental muscle. Calling 0.160 against 0.280 "comparable", as the printed verdict does, is simply wrong -- real adjustment removes more than twice what the placebo does.

WHY THE BRANCH FIRED WRONGLY. The registered rule used a 0.5x-of-placebo cut for MUSCLE EXPLAINS IT: 0.160 against a threshold of 0.140, so it missed by 0.020 and fell through to NOT INFORMATIVE. The cut was arbitrary and it forced a three-way branch onto what is a CONTINUOUS attribution. The verdict stands as the rule produced it; the interpretation does not, and the quantitative attribution above is what should be quoted.

SOMETHING DOES SURVIVE, AND IT IS SMALL. The adjusted fraction is 0.340 [0.262, 0.418], still excluding 0.5. So muscle does not account for all of it. But a residual of that size, after a control this well validated, is not a basis for presenting exponent_high as an awake/asleep BRAIN marker.

CONSEQUENCE FOR E69, STATED WHERE A READER WOULD RELY ON IT. E69's one departing feature departs substantially for a peripheral reason. exponent_high is fitted over 20-40 Hz where surface EMG lives, E43 had already measured that such a slope is more muscle-associated than BIS, and this is that prediction confirmed on an independent state axis. The BSDE-relevant reading of E69 -- that some measure separates experience from behavioural output -- is NOT supported. What separates wake from sleep here is largely the jaw.
placebo: residualisation against a WITHIN-SUBJECT PERMUTED EMG vector, since residualising on any covariate removes variance
primary: E69 fraction-REM-nearer-W recomputed after within-subject residualisation of exponent_high on submental EMG
question: Is exponent_high's awake/asleep boundary (E69) explained by submental muscle tone?

deposit: Sleep-EDFx five-stage EEG table joined to the submental EMG table on recording_id — 142 subjects, 12 features
gates: G1 aliveness per feature: the unadjusted W-vs-N3 d_z interval must exclude zero
G2 POSITIVE CONTROL: emg_index, a muscle proxy by construction, must rank in the top third by attribution or nothing else is readable
instrument_changed: scope: all twelve features rather than exponent_high alone, with the band-position hypothesis added.
outcome_detail:
METHOD FAILS at G2, and THE GATE DID ITS JOB -- it stopped a twelve-feature audit from being reported when the procedure had not been shown to work. emg_index ranked 7 of 12 by attribution, so the method could not recover muscle in the one feature designed to measure muscle.

DIAGNOSIS 1: THE POSITIVE CONTROL WAS INVALID, AND E69 HAD ALREADY SAID SO. emg_index is a scalp proxy computed from Fpz-Cz and Pz-Oz, and E69 recorded that it shows NO REM atonia (REM 0.312 against N3 0.127). Measured directly against the real submental channel it correlates at rho = +0.2048 pooled (n = 709) and +0.30 within subject across the five stages. A weak proxy was pressed into service as ground truth, so its failure to rank first says nothing about the method.

DIAGNOSIS 2, SUBTLER AND MORE EXPENSIVE. A SYNTHETIC positive control -- a feature constructed to BE the submental channel plus noise -- returns d_z = +0.062 for wake versus N3 on a channel whose stage medians are 3.063 against 1.104. The effect is enormous and the standardised effect is nil, because submental EMG amplitude carries a SUBJECT-SPECIFIC GAIN: one subject moves 10->3 and another 1->0.3, so the paired differences have huge between-subject variance. Raw EMG amplitude is not a magnitude, and every attribution number in this run inherits that.

A THIRD BUG WAS FOUND AND FIXED AND TURNED OUT NOT TO BE OPERATIVE. The placebo computed mean(|d_z|) across permutations and differenced it against a singly-folded |d1| -- a folded statistic compared against a folded statistic of different construction (rule 46). Corrected to |mean(d_z)|. The output was byte-identical because the permutation d_z values are consistently signed, so mean(|p|) equals |mean(p)| here. Recorded because the reasoning was right even though this instance was harmless.

E70 IS NOT AFFECTED AND ITS VERDICT STANDS. Its residualisation is WITHIN SUBJECT, so the subject-specific gain is constant across the five stages and is absorbed into the regression slope. And its decisive evidence -- REM's position on the W->N3 axis, +1.189 for exponent_high against +1.099 for submental EMG -- is a rank comparison with no regression and no magnitude in it.

WHAT A CORRECTED SUCCESSOR NEEDS: log-transform or within-subject z-score the EMG before using it as a covariate or an effect size, and build the positive control from the submental channel itself rather than from a scalp proxy already shown to be broken. Logged as rule 57.

deposit: Sleep-EDFx five-stage EEG joined to submental EMG, 142 subjects, 12 real features plus 2 synthetic controls
gates: G1 aliveness per feature: unadjusted W-vs-N3 d_z must exclude zero
G2 bracket: a synthetic muscle feature must rank top two AND a synthetic null must rank bottom three
instrument_changed: the covariate transform (log + within-subject z-score, verified to move the channel own W-vs-N3 effect from d_z +0.062 to -0.550) and the control set (two synthetics replacing a scalp proxy).
outcome_detail:
METHOD FAILS at G2 as registered. The gate is rank-shaped and could not close; the substantive numbers below are therefore NOT licensed by the verdict, and are recorded so the successor has them.

THE COVARIATE FIX WORKED AND WAS VERIFIED BEFORE THE RUN. log(submental EMG) z-scored within subject gives the channel own W-vs-N3 effect d_z = -0.550, correct direction, with stage medians W +0.874 > N1 +0.643 > N2 +0.081 > N3 -0.088 > REM -0.845 -- monotone down the depth staircase, REM lowest, which is what atonia looks like. Raw amplitude gave +0.062, the wrong sign.

THE METHOD DEMONSTRABLY WORKS ON ITS OWN CONTROLS. Synthetic muscle (transformed EMG plus matched-variance noise) scores attribution 0.810 and ranks FIRST of fourteen. Synthetic null (a stage-driven, EMG-independent feature) scores 0.022. That is a 37-fold separation and it is the positive half E71 never achieved.

WHY THE GATE STILL FAILED, AND IT IS THE GATE. G2 required the null control in the BOTTOM THREE. It ranked 10 of 14 -- because four real features (lempel_ziv 0.017, spectral_entropy 0.013, relative_delta_power -0.022, relative_alpha_power -0.275) are themselves null, so a null control necessarily lands INSIDE the null cluster rather than beneath it. A rank criterion cannot express "near zero" when much of the field is near zero; a magnitude criterion could.

THE SUBSTANTIVE READING, UNLICENSED AND MARKED AS SUCH. No real feature approaches the muscle control. The maximum is pac_slow_alpha at 0.171 and exponent_high at 0.158, against synthetic muscle at 0.810 and synthetic null at 0.022. On the WAKE-vs-N3 CONTRAST, submental muscle attribution is small for every feature this project computes.

NO CONTRADICTION WITH E70, AND THE DISTINCTION MATTERS. E70 measured REM's POSITION on the W->N3 axis, where atonia makes muscle maximally distinctive, and found exponent_high at +1.189 against submental EMG at +1.099. E72 measures the W-vs-N3 EFFECT SIZE, a graded contrast in which muscle varies far less. Different estimands, both defensible, and E70's rank-position evidence involves no regression at all. E70 stands.

H1: Spearman(attribution, share of band above 20 Hz) = +0.2099 [-0.4723, +0.8129]. Absent.

PROCESS FAILURE RECORDED AS RULE 58. This gate was revised TWICE in one sitting -- pure noise replaced by a stage-driven synthetic, after which the rank criterion still could not close. Both repairs were individually correct and the sequence was not: by the second I was tuning the apparatus until it returned a verdict. The run stopped there deliberately.
placebo: residualisation against a within-subject PERMUTED EMG vector
primary: H1: Spearman between muscle attribution and the share of each feature band above 20 Hz (carried over verbatim from E71)
question: The E71 muscle audit repeated with a covariate that is a magnitude (log + within-subject z) and two synthetic controls bracketing the method.

deposit: ds004902 sleep deprivation — eyes-open, both sessions, 68 subjects; drug arms carried from E67 (ds005620 propofol, ds004541 GA)
gates: G1 manipulation gate on the deposit's OWN behavioural anchors, not the EEG: a subjective sleepiness anchor must clear zero
instrument_changed: the no-drug arm: a genuine drug-free arousal manipulation (sleep deprivation) replacing natural N3 sleep, whose depth could not be matched to any drug arm.
outcome_detail:
RESPONDS, and it produces the first clean Challenge A discriminator this project has had.

G1 PASSED ON THE SUBJECTIVE ANCHORS AND FAILED ON THE OBJECTIVE ONE, which is reported rather than buried. KSS rises +2.000 (d_z +0.969, n=32) and SSS +1.667 (d_z +0.782, n=33). PVT lapses do NOT move: -0.033, d_z -0.008, n=30. A cohort that feels sleepier without being objectively slower is a different manipulation from the one Q29 assumed, and any "arousal" language here inherits that.

PRIMARY: 7 of 29 features respond, against a permutation placebo of 1.975. Responders: abs_beta, abs_delta, abs_theta, aperiodic_offset, dfa_exponent, lempel_ziv, rel_theta. With 29 features tested the placebo IS the multiplicity control and 7 against ~2 is a real excess, though not an overwhelming one.

THE DISCRIMINATOR, and it is what the experiment was for. Two features have both arms measured:

    lempel_ziv           no-drug d_z -0.324 [-0.583, -0.089]   propofol +1.55   GA +0.95   -> STATE
    whole_head_exponent  no-drug d_z +0.034 [-0.231, +0.258]   propofol +1.11   GA +0.94   -> PHARMACOLOGY

whole_head_exponent moves strongly for two different anaesthetics and NOT AT ALL when arousal falls without a drug. That is precisely the profile Challenge A penalises, and it is the first direct evidence in this project that the aperiodic exponent carries anaesthetic pharmacology rather than state -- which is E36's prediction (spectral amplitude summaries leak drug identity) reached from an entirely different direction, and consistent with E30's sign disagreement between agent classes.

lempel_ziv moves in BOTH arms, which is the profile Challenge A wants. Its SIGN REVERSES between them (down with sleep deprivation, up under both drugs), and E67 already flagged that reversal and could not separate it from depth. This experiment does not separate it either. So lempel_ziv is a state-sensitive measure whose direction is not yet understood, not a Challenge A pass.

LIMITS, STATED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED LATER. Only TWO features have both arms, because ds005620 carries just six of the project's features and the sleep-deprivation table uses a different extraction path. The arms are different deposits, so E53's cross-deposit floor bounds everything except the ordering; and anaesthesia is a far larger state change than one night of deprivation, so every feature must move more in the drug arm and only a feature moving ZERO without a drug is informative. At n=68 the primary excludes a moderate effect (|d_z| ~0.35) and not a small one.

WHAT Q29 ASSUMED AND THE DEPOSIT DOES NOT SUPPORT. A calibrated drug-response / state-response RATIO is unavailable here: eyes-closed exists for only about half the subjects (139 eyes-open recordings against 74), KSS was collected only from sub-39 onward while subjects with two eyes-closed sessions start at sub-01, and the overlap is exactly ZERO. The arm with the larger EEG effect (eyes-closed, exponent_low d_z +0.579) has no behavioural anchor; the arm with anchors has weak EEG effects. S2 confirms the cost: no responder's change correlates detectably with the subjective sleepiness change (max rho +0.321 at n=32, MDE ~0.50).

=========================================================================================================
CORRECTION, MADE THE SAME DAY AND BEFORE ANY OF THIS WAS QUOTED ELSEWHERE. THE HEADLINE CONCLUSION ABOVE IS
INVERTED AND IS WITHDRAWN.
=========================================================================================================
E74 compared each feature's drug-free response against its drug response, and built its DRUG_DZ constants
by hand from E67 -- taking E67's two DRUG columns and leaving E67's NO-DRUG column behind. That column was
natural N3 sleep, and it changes the answer completely:

    feature                N3 sleep    sleep-dep    propofol       GA
    whole_head_exponent      +4.008       +0.034      +1.110   +0.937
    lempel_ziv               -2.281       -0.324      +1.551   +0.947

**whole_head_exponent responds to natural N3 sleep MORE STRONGLY THAN TO EITHER ANAESTHETIC.** It is not
pharmacology-specific and the PHARMACOLOGY label is wrong. Its silence under sleep deprivation (+0.034)
reflects the size of that manipulation -- being sleep-deprived while awake is a far smaller state change
than N3 sleep or general anaesthesia -- not a need for a drug. Its SIGN is consistent across all four
contrasts, which is the profile Challenge A wants. It is the best candidate in this comparison, not the
worst.

**lempel_ziv is the feature whose direction depends on whether a drug is involved**: negative in both
drug-free arms (-2.281 natural sleep, -0.324 deprivation) and positive in both drug arms (+1.551 propofol,
+0.947 GA). E67 flagged that reversal and could not separate it from depth; the second drug-free arm now
agrees in sign with the first, which strengthens the reversal as a fact while leaving its cause open.

BOTH DRUG-FREE ARMS AGREE IN SIGN FOR BOTH FEATURES, which is the one thing this correction adds beyond
fixing an error: the sleep-deprivation arm is a weak version of the natural-sleep arm rather than a
different phenomenon, so the two can be read together.

WHAT SURVIVES UNCHANGED: the primary (7 of 29 features respond against a placebo of 1.975), the G1 result
(subjective anchors move, PVT lapses do not), and the finding that Q29's calibrated ratio is unavailable on
this deposit. What is withdrawn is only the two-feature interpretation, which was the part quoted as the
result. Logged as error-catalogue rule 59.

question: Which measures respond to an arousal change that contains no drug, and how does that compare with their response to anaesthetics?

deposit: fitted on VitalDB (4,930 windows, BIS [20,60), SQI>=50); applied to DOSE-I (10,898 windows, 39 recordings, per-second MOAA/S)
gates: M1 transport gate, label-free: standardised median shift per feature between deposits, with the primary run both with (FULL) and without (SAFE) the drifting features
M2 coverage: >=300 windows across >=10 recordings with >=3 MOAA/S levels must survive the [20,60) refusal
instrument_changed: the reference: a clinician ordinal sedation score on an independent deposit, replacing device BIS on the deposit the index was fitted to.
outcome_detail:
NO TRACKING, in both arms, and it is the most consequential Challenge C result so far because the incumbents on the SAME rows track it well.

    our index, FULL (18 features)   rho = +0.0375 [-0.1501, +0.2893]   38 recordings
    our index, SAFE (11 features)   rho = +0.0417 [-0.1756, +0.1424]   39 recordings
    DOSE-I own PE31                 rho = +0.3974 [+0.3098, +0.4636] / +0.4813 [+0.4093, +0.6332]
    DOSE-I own SEF95                rho = -0.0197 [-0.1155, +0.1109] / +0.2507 [+0.0762, +0.3833]

Depth information IS present in this EEG and IS recoverable -- permutation entropy, the measure E33 named as its incumbent from Ostertag et al., reaches +0.48 on the same windows. Our index reaches +0.04.

IT IS NOT A FLAT-MODEL ARTEFACT, which the registration did not gate for and which was checked afterwards. Predictions vary on DOSE-I at sd 12.02 (FULL, 2nd-98th percentile 39.1-89.1) and 5.04 (SAFE, 30.8-50.1), against sd 5.48 on the VitalDB fit set itself. The model moves; it simply moves independently of what the clinician recorded.

M1 TRANSPORT: 11 of 18 features transport. bis_bsr and bis_quazi have INFINITE shift (near-zero IQR on one side -- burst suppression barely occurs in either cohort), bis_sfs 1.730, multiscale_entropy_slope 1.574, whole_head_exponent 1.288, lempel_ziv 1.203, exponent_high 1.122. The SAFE arm drops all seven and the answer does not change, so drift is NOT the explanation.

M2 COVERAGE differs sharply between arms and is itself informative: the FULL arm places 46.2% of windows inside [20,60) while the SAFE arm places 100.0%, because the SAFE model's whole predicted range (30.8-50.1) sits inside the licensed band. A model whose output cannot leave the band it was fitted in is not being restrained by the refusal rule; it has simply regressed to its training mean.

WHAT THIS DOES TO Q22's DELIVERABLE. Q22 licensed using the index on monitor-free deposits within [20,60) with +/-3.47 attached. That licence rested entirely on agreement with device BIS measured on the recordings it was fitted to. The first external test of whether it measures DEPTH rather than one manufacturer's OUTPUT fails. **The parsimonious reading is that the index learned to reproduce the BIS algorithm on one device and population, not anaesthetic depth** -- and reproducing a proprietary index is not the same as measuring what the index claims to measure.

THE CAVEAT THAT MUST RIDE WITH IT, and it cannot be settled with data in hand. The index was fitted to predict DEVICE BIS, and MOAA/S is a different target; if BIS itself tracked MOAA/S poorly, a BIS-faithful index would too. DOSE-I has no BIS and VitalDB has no MOAA/S, so the two references cannot be compared directly here. Published sedation studies put BIS-versus-MOAA/S correlation in the moderate-to-strong range, which makes +0.04 hard to explain that way, but this experiment does not measure it. **Either reading has the same practical consequence: the index cannot serve as a depth comparator on monitor-free deposits, which was Q22's entire purpose.**

outcome_detail:
BOTH CO-PRIMARIES PASS, and the machinery gate that first refused the run is why the numbers are trustworthy. G4 self-check: pe_raw reproduced the prior pass's mine_pe on all 10,927 shared rows with max |diff| = 0 -- exact, not approximate. G2 tie activity 0.1709, G3 band activity 0.2037, G5 43 recordings (12,170 windows) against a registered floor of 30. A first evaluation at 26 recordings refused at G5 as registered; the shortfall was the launch argument (--n-recordings 40 stops at 10-060 and 14 of those 40 fail the shared non-uniform-time-axis rule), and what was seen before the extension is written down in results/e76_first_pass_note.md.

P1 AGREEMENT vs the deposit's PE31: D = +0.2457 [+0.1468, +0.3601], 0 of 20,000 resamples on the wrong side, identical verdict at three seeds. The arbitrary-wrong-band placebo (0.5-20 Hz) does not merely fail to help, it HURTS: D_placebo = -0.1466, contrast +0.3923 [+0.3385, +0.4469]. So the gain is specific to the DECLARED band, not to low-passing in general.

P2 CLINICIAN vs MOAA/S: D = +0.1609 [+0.0764, +0.2613], placebo -0.1097, contrast +0.2706 [+0.1822, +0.3646]. PASS.

THE DECOMPOSITION IS ONE-SIDED AND IT MATTERS (descriptive, not gated): the 0.5-45 Hz band does essentially all of it -- +0.2383 of P1's +0.2457 and +0.1620 of P2's +0.1609 -- while the 0.5 uV tie threshold contributes +0.0234 [+0.0089, +0.0414] on agreement and +0.0077 [-0.0021, +0.0188] on MOAA/S, the latter including zero. The tie rule was active (16-17 % of embedded windows carry a tied pair) so this is a measured near-null, not an inapplicable arm.

CONSEQUENCE FOR CHALLENGE C: the gap Q36 recorded is explained, and the comparator is now PORTABLE. Computed with the declared recipe our PE reaches median within-recording rho +0.5304 against MOAA/S where the deposit's own PE31 reaches +0.4944 -- DESCRIPTIVE, with no interval comparison performed and no superiority claimed. Q34's 'PE31 is the comparator to use' no longer binds Challenge C to deposits that ship a PE31 column.

deposit: Sleep-EDF Expanded five-stage windows (125 subjects) joined to the submental EMG envelope
gates: G0 the locally parameterised attribution reproduces E72's function exactly at 120 draws
G1 A(synthetic muscle) - A(synthetic null) >= 0.40 on THIS table
G2 |d0| bootstrap interval excludes 0, else NO-EFFECT-TO-ATTRIBUTE not NOT-ATTRIBUTED
G3 >= 40 subjects with all five stages in both tables
outcome_detail:
MUSCLE-ATTRIBUTED AND SMALL, which is the informative combination. All gates passed: G0 the locally parameterised attribution reproduces E72's exactly; G1 separation +0.591 (synthetic muscle +0.772, synthetic null +0.181) against a registered floor of 0.40; G3 141 subjects.

P1 bis_rbr: A = +0.102 [+0.027, +0.191]. Rule 46 followed because the first run's BH p (0.0200) sat inside the Monte Carlo granularity of its own 200 resamples: re-run at 3 seeds and 600 resamples the verdict is STABLE MUSCLE-ATTRIBUTED with p 0.0100-0.0167 against a BH threshold of 0.025.

P2 bis_sfs: A = +0.059 [-0.009, +0.132], STABLE NOT-ATTRIBUTED at 3 seeds; does not survive BH.

THE MAGNITUDE IS THE RESULT AND IT DEFENDS Q35. bis_rbr's wake-versus-N3 effect is d_z = -2.743 [-3.418, -2.228] -- the largest of any feature measured on this table -- and after adjustment for real submental EMG it is still 1.440. Roughly a tenth of it is muscle. Anchors, recomputed here: exponent_high A = +0.151 [+0.028, +0.302], relative_alpha_power A = -0.307 [-0.619, -0.007].

BOTH READINGS OF THE SCALE ARE REPORTED, because A is normalised by |d0| and that flatters a large effect. RELATIVE: bis_rbr (0.102) loses less of itself to muscle than exponent_high (0.151). ABSOLUTE: bis_rbr's shrinkage |d2|-|d1| is 0.280 against exponent_high's 0.172, so it loses MORE d_z units. Both are true; the registered statistic is the relative one.

A REGISTERED PREDICTION WAS WRONG AND IT IS A FINDING. bis_bsr and bis_quazi were predicted 'identically zero in physiological sleep, because there is no burst suppression there'. They are not. bis_bsr is nonzero in 61.3 % of REM windows, 52.8 % of N1, 29.1 % of N2, 19.7 % of W and 10.6 % of N3 -- highest in the LOW-AMPLITUDE stages, which is the signature of an amplitude-threshold suppression detector false-positiving -- with one W window at BSR = 1.000, i.e. 100 % suppression in wake, which cannot be physiological. Medians are ~0 and p90s are 0.001-0.06, so the magnitudes are small, but the pattern is systematic. bis_quazi behaves the same way (nonzero in 75.4 % of REM and N1). bis_bsr's own W-vs-N3 contrast is d_z = -0.133 [-0.253, -0.098]; bis_quazi failed G2 and is reported NO-EFFECT-TO-ATTRIBUTE.

SCOPE, unchanged from the registration and the sentence most likely to be dropped: this is a wake-versus-deep-sleep contrast in physiological sleep. Q35's +0.5258 is a MOAA/S contrast under anaesthesia, where muscle tone is a different quantity. This removes one specific objection in one setting; it does not clear bis_rbr on DOSE-I, and Q35's owed registered replication is owed either way.

question: Is bis_rbr's wake-versus-deep-sleep effect explained by submental muscle tone, measured on a real submental EMG channel rather than a scalp proxy? The control Q35 owes for its +0.5258.

deposit: Stieger et al. MI-BCI (62 channels, 62 subjects, up to 11 sessions each)
gates: G1 coverage: >= MIN_SUBJECTS for D1, >= MIN_PAIRS consecutive pairs for D2
G2 capability: the primary must vary non-degenerately across subjects (rule 53)
outcome_detail:
CHALLENGE B'S FIRST INTERPRETABLE NULL. The pre-declared primary, wpli_alpha_global_efficiency, gives D1 rho -0.086 [-0.329, +0.166] between subjects and D2 rho +0.093 [-0.077, +0.252] on consecutive-session change. Both gates passed (G1 coverage, G2 capability, primary sd 0.0266). 185 sessions, 62 subjects.

WHAT MAKES THIS A REAL NULL RATHER THAN AN ATTENUATION ARTEFACT: E68 measured this deposit's label ceiling at 0.9652 within session and 0.8087 for a stable-ability design, so unlike E41 -- capped at 0.5402 by eegmmidb's 0.2918 reliability -- there is room for an effect to appear. Power stated in advance: at 62 subjects a true 0.53 (Blankertz) attenuates to ~0.43 and is detectable; a true 0.25 attenuates below detection. THE NULL EXCLUDES A LARGE EFFECT AND NOT A MODEST ONE.

THE PRIMARY WAS NOT THE NETWORK MEASURE IT WAS CHOSEN TO BE, AND THAT IS THE METHODOLOGICAL RESULT. Across the 62 subject means, wpli_alpha_global_efficiency correlates with wpli_alpha_mean_degree at rho +0.9962 and with plain wpli_alpha at +0.8639. On an unthresholded weighted graph, shortest paths are dominated by direct edges, so global efficiency is mean connectivity strength restated. Rule 28 in reverse: a measure was chosen because it is a DIFFERENT KIND of quantity and is not one. Any successor testing 'network' predictors on this deposit must sparsify or threshold first, or it is re-running the same test.

THE FAMILY SURVIVOR IS A HYPOTHESIS, NOT A RESULT, AND THE REGISTRATION SAID SO IN ADVANCE. wpli_alpha_clustering reaches D1 rho +0.396 [+0.163, +0.591], BH q = 0.0398 over 17 features, and 0 of 400 accuracy permutations reach it. It is also nearly orthogonal to the primary (rho -0.076 across subject means), which is why it is not the same test. THREE REASONS IT IS NOT PROMOTED: it was not pre-declared; the registration states 'a measure that wins only here has not won'; and IT REVERSES SIGN IN D2 (-0.129 [-0.287, +0.036]) on the same subjects, which is what a between-subject confound looks like and what a genuine state-like predictor does not do.

P3 WAS REGISTERED AND WAS ABSENT FROM THE FIRST RUN OF THE FILE. It existed only in the docstring. Implemented rather than dropped (rule 48's second half). On the primary it returns NOT INFORMATIVE by construction -- a placebo cannot validate a null -- and says so instead of printing a pass.

deposit: Sleep-EDFx W->N3 (142 subjects); ds005620 propofol (21); ds004541 GA (7) -- all bsde-path
gates: G1 aliveness: the paired d_z interval must exclude zero in each arm (rule 53)
G2 monotonicity: medians across W, N1, N2, N3 monotone on the no-drug arm, else the feature is NOT DEPTH-MONOTONE and its cross-arm sign is uninterpretable
instrument_changed: the placebo (pairing shuffle -> within-subject label permutation), the pipeline (mixed -> bsde-path only), and depth monotonicity from assumption to gate
outcome_detail:
THE REGISTERED PLACEBO REFUSES THE AGGREGATE, AND THE FIRST RUN PRINTED THE OPPOSITE. As first written the NOT-INFORMATIVE branch compared |real - 0.5| against |placebo_mean - 0.5|. That gate COULD NOT FAIL: the placebo mean is ~0.500 by construction over 300 draws, and with an ODD number of testable features the real rate can never be 0.500. Rule 40 inside the verdict code, which is rule 37's family and its fifth occurrence in this project. Corrected to compare against the placebo DISTRIBUTION -- which makes the test stricter after seeing a pass, never looser, and changes no threshold, cohort, contrast or gate. 0.487 of placebo draws reach the observed rate of 0.571 or better; 4 of 7 is the MEDIAN of a Binomial(7, 0.5). The aggregate verdict is NOT INFORMATIVE and the earlier SPLIT is withdrawn.

WHAT SURVIVES AS DESCRIPTIVE. Each per-feature sign is determined by its own G1 interval and those numbers stand; what fails is the claim that the AGREE set is a class. Same-sign: critical_slowing_ar1 (+3.256 / +0.515), emg_beta_gamma_fraction (-1.906 / -0.900), spectral_edge_95 (-2.868 / -0.772), whole_head_exponent (+4.008 / +1.120, and agreeing on drug-B too). Reversing: exponent_low (+3.157 / -1.238), lempel_ziv (-2.281 / +1.505, reversing on drug-B too), multiscale_entropy_slope (+3.612 / -1.372). Both of the features E74 named behave here exactly as E74 found.

TWO OBSERVATIONS THE DESIGN WAS NOT BUILT FOR AND WHICH ARE NOT SOFTENED. (1) emg_beta_gamma_fraction, a MUSCLE measure, is in the same-sign set -- which is what 'sign agreement is necessary, not sufficient' looks like when it bites, and it is a warning against reading that set as candidates. (2) uce_v1, this project's flagship candidate, is EMPTY in all 710 rows of the Sleep-EDFx five-stage table, so it could not enter the no-drug arm at all; exponent_high failed the depth-monotonicity gate.

question: Do measures move the SAME WAY when consciousness falls with a drug and without one, compared within a single extraction pipeline and with the depth-monotonicity premise tested rather than asserted? E67's successor.

outcome_detail:
TIE, which is the registered prediction and the outcome that settles Q35's debt. D = rho(bis_rbr) - rho(pe_declared) = -0.0168 [-0.0447, +0.0131] over 62 held-out recordings and 19,299 windows, 12.5 % of resamples on the wrong side, identical verdict at three seeds. outcome_detail:
PARTIAL by the conservative rule registered in advance, and read honestly it means E78's +0.0500 is WINDOW LENGTH. 62 held-out recordings, 19,299 windows, all gates passed, and both window-matching operations were shown to be real changes rather than no-ops (G3: median within-recording rho between pe_8 and pe_30 is +0.8834, between PE31 and its 30 s trailing mean +0.8532 -- both well under the 0.99 identity threshold).

THE SINGLE MOST LEGIBLE NUMBER IS G4, WHICH GATES NOTHING: median rho against MOAA/S rises MONOTONICALLY with our window -- +0.4261 at 8 s, +0.4532 at 16 s, +0.4686 at 30 s. That is the smoothing explanation quantified, and it was declared as such before the run.

P1, SHORTEN OURS TO THE DEPOSIT'S OWN DECLARED 8 s: D = +0.0067 [-0.0232, +0.0379], 34.2 % of resamples on the wrong side. WINDOW-EXPLAINED. At matched window the two implementations are indistinguishable.

P2, SMOOTH THEIRS TO 30 s WITH A CAUSAL TRAILING MEAN: D = +0.0381 [+0.0030, +0.0755], 1.6 % on the wrong side. The medians tell the same story more plainly (our 30 s +0.4686 against their smoothed +0.4672, a difference of 0.0014).

WHERE THE DISAGREEMENT LOCALISES, which is what the two-armed design was for: P1 needs no model and says explained; P2 needs a model of their smoothing and barely clears at the boundary. **E78's descriptive +0.0500 is withdrawn as evidence of a better implementation.**

WHAT IS ESTABLISHED AND IS MORE USEFUL THAN THE CLAIM THAT WAS DROPPED. (1) Once support is matched the two independent implementations AGREE -- a stronger validation of ours than a spurious edge would have been. (2) Window length is worth +0.042 in clinician tracking across 8 s to 30 s, more than the entire disputed difference between the two implementations, so **Challenge C's portable comparator should specify a 30 s window** and any future comparison of depth measures must match support before ranking them.

outcome_detail:
NO MEASURE IS STATE-LIKE. 42 held-out recordings, 11,124 windows, 29 features; G1 (zero overlap with the 43 already-used recordings), G2 (20 recordings, 32 cells) and G3 (bracket) all PASSED.

**STATE-LIKE: none. DRUG-LIKE: 16. UNDETERMINED: 12. NOT-COMPUTABLE: 1 (bis_bsr, 0 cells).** At matched MOAA/S, every feature that could be classified reads DIFFERENTLY on the way down than on the way up -- including whole_head_exponent (+0.588 [+0.071, +1.143]), lempel_ziv (-1.038 [-1.492, -0.559]), spectral_entropy (-0.751 [-1.272, -0.252]), the deposit's own their_sef95, and bis_rbr (+0.537 [+0.200, +0.860]). The equivalence margin was +-0.25 within-recording SD, declared in advance.

**THE PLACEBO WAS WIRED AND NOTHING WAS WITHDRAWN BY IT.** Rule 64 predicted the danger exactly -- a split keyed to an extremum is a time split in disguise -- and the random-split placebo does produce same-signed gaps of real size (e.g. whole_head_exponent placebo [+0.136, +0.422], bis_rbr [+0.153, +0.478]). Every DRUG-LIKE call lies OUTSIDE its own placebo interval, so the classification is not the split structure. The bracket held: _CTRL_time -2.379 [-2.645, -2.099] DRUG-LIKE, _CTRL_noise -0.060 [-0.232, +0.126] STATE-LIKE.

WHAT IT MEANS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. A STATE-LIKE call was defined in advance as a NECESSARY and not a sufficient condition, so this is a clean elimination rather than a discovery: on this deposit no candidate -- ours, the deposit's, or the vendor's -- indexes behavioural state independently of where the drug concentration is going. UNDETERMINED is not evidence of invariance for the 12 that got it.

ONE ASYMMETRY WORTH RECORDING FOR SUCCESSORS: the placebo withdrawal is applied only to DRUG-LIKE calls. A STATE-LIKE call is an equivalence claim and could in principle be manufactured by a placebo-sized gap; it did not bite here because no feature was STATE-LIKE, but a successor that finds one owes the symmetric check.

deposit: OpenNeuro ds007554, 15 subjects x 3 sessions x 7 tasks, 33 channels -- zero prior ledger use
gates: G1 coverage: >= 10 subjects with a motorimagery/passivemotor pair
G2 the incumbent must be alive: activemotor vs passivemotor d_z interval must exclude zero, else a null on covert attempt says nothing about covert attempt (rule 53 / E33)
G3 every pair taken WITHIN session, count reported not assumed
RULE-60 PRE-CHECK (run before registering, and it changed the design): wpli_alpha correlates with spectral_edge_95 at -0.9179 across subject means, so no family claim is made
outcome_detail:
G2 FAILED AND THE GATE WAS RIGHT. The overt anchor -- activemotor versus passivemotor, the contrast that MUST be detectable if the pipeline can see task-related change at all -- gives the incumbent relative_alpha_power d_z = +0.393 [-0.028, +0.934] over 11 subjects. The interval includes zero, and the point estimate has the WRONG SIGN for sensorimotor ERD. So the primary was not evaluated: a null on covert attempt would have said nothing about covert attempt (rule 53, in E33's formulation).

G1 and G3 passed: 13 subjects carry a motorimagery/passivemotor pair across 31 within-session pairs.

DIAGNOSIS, AND IT IS ABOUT THE EXTRACTION RATHER THAN THE DEPOSIT. ds007554_features.csv holds ONE WHOLE-RECORDING SUMMARY PER RUN, median-reduced across 33 channels. Sensorimotor alpha ERD is transient (~1 s around movement onset), time-locked to a cue, and focal to C3/C4. Averaging a whole task run across all channels removes all three properties, so the anchor is not merely weak here -- it is not measurable in principle from this table. **The deposit carries the right paradigm and the table carries the wrong reduction.**

THE RULE-60 PRE-CHECK IS THE OTHER THING WORTH KEEPING. It ran BEFORE registration, as rule 60 requires, and it changed the design: the intended primary wpli_alpha correlates with spectral_edge_95 at rho -0.9179 across the 15 subject means, with whole_head_exponent at +0.8893 and uce_v1 at +0.8714. This table's eight features are one family, so no family claim was made. That is the first time the check has been run in advance and it prevented a repeat of E73's error rather than diagnosing one afterwards.

deposit: OpenNeuro ds007554, motorimagery/passivemotor/activemotor, sub-001 EXCLUDED (smoke-test burn)
gates: G1 coverage: >= 8 contributing subjects of the 14 available after the exclusion
G2 anchor alive: activemotor minus passivemotor must exclude zero AND be negative -- a wrong-signed anchor fails as surely as a null one
G3 specificity: erd_wholehead on identical timing; if it matches, the verdict is NOT-SENSORIMOTOR-SPECIFIC rather than a detection
instrument_changed: whole-run median over 33 channels -> per-trial cue-locked pre/post alpha ratio on the sensorimotor strip; nothing else moved
outcome_detail:
G2 FAILED AGAIN, AND THE LITERATURE CHECK AFTERWARDS SHOWS THE ANCHOR WAS THE WRONG STATISTIC. With the instrument replaced exactly as registered -- per-trial cue-locked log10(post/pre) alpha on nine sensorimotor channels, 203 runs over 30 subjects, sub-001 excluded as the smoke-test burn -- the overt anchor activemotor minus passivemotor gives d_z = +0.271 [-0.190, +0.565] over 20 subjects. Interval includes zero and the sign is again wrong for ERD. G1 passed (23 subjects). The primary was not evaluated. Rule 58: E82 was the attempt, E83 was the one repair, the run is over and the failure is the result.

THE LITERATURE CHECK THAT SHOULD HAVE RUN FIRST (rule 21). PubMed via E-utilities, records verified rather than summarised:
  * PMID 31425038 (IEEE Trans Neural Syst Rehabil Eng 2019), 'EEG Sensorimotor Correlates of Speed During Forearm Passive Movements': passive forearm oscillations delivered by a haptic device elicit mu and beta ERD, and the authors hypothesise and test a PROPORTIONAL relationship between SMR features and passive movement speed.
  * PMID 27529874 (IEEE Trans Neural Syst Rehabil Eng 2017), 'EEG Analysis During Active and Assisted Repetitive Movements': in a 2x2 of volitional intention against robotic assistance, 'statistically significant ERDs began EARLIER in conditions requiring subject's volitional contribution'.

**So passive movement produces ERD of its own, and the published volitional difference is in LATENCY.** A fixed [+0.5, +2.5] s average of alpha power cannot see a latency difference, and the anchor contrast was therefore small by construction. Both E82's and E83's failures are explained by the same thing and it is not the deposit and not the epoching -- it is the choice of summary statistic, predicted by physiology that was available before either run. ds007554 remains a good deposit for this question; the successor must use ERD ONSET LATENCY, and it must carry a stopping rule so this is not attempted indefinitely.

primary: erd_sm = per-trial log10(post-cue alpha / pre-cue alpha) on C1 C2 C3 C4 Cz FC3 FC4 CP1 CP2; within-session motorimagery minus passivemotor, Cohen's d_z across subjects, subject bootstrap; direction PREDICTED NEGATIVE; REVERSED branch named first
question: Does cue-locked sensorimotor alpha ERD separate covert command-following from passive stimulation within subject, once the reduction that killed E82's anchor is replaced?

deposit: DOSE-I held-out partition (shares its table with E80; both registered before extraction)
gates: G1 held out: zero overlap with the 43 used recordings
G2 coverage: >= 15 recordings and >= 25 (recording, MOAA/S level) cells
G3 the marker marks something: ecg_hr, a NON-EEG channel, must be STIMULUS-SENSITIVE, else the Endoscopy column is not marking stimulation and nothing downstream is interpretable
G4 negative control: a per-window Gaussian draw must not come back SENSITIVE
outcome_detail:
ABSENT AT G3 -- the positive control could not be classified, so no feature was, and the design refused to emit a verdict (rule 31). 42 recordings, 11,124 windows, 39 recordings contributing 64 cells; G1 (zero overlap with the 43 already-used recordings) and G2 (coverage) both PASSED.

**G3 heart rate: ecg_hr gap +0.056 [-0.241, +0.345] -> UNDETERMINED.** An endoscope in the airway is a strong noxious and mechanical stimulus; heart rate is the one variable in this table that must respond to it. The interval neither excludes 0 nor lies inside the declared +-0.25 equivalence margin, which is **no power, not invariance** -- exactly the distinction the design was written to preserve. If the control cannot be placed, no EEG feature's placement is interpretable.

G4 noise: _CTRL_noise gap -0.005 [-0.083, +0.074] -> STIMULUS-INVARIANT, so the estimator is not manufacturing gaps; the failure is power, not machinery.

WHAT THIS COSTS. The anaesthesia-side muscle test that E77's scope limit asked for is NOT delivered, and `bis_rbr`'s 30-47 Hz numerator remains untested against a causal artefact handle. This is not evidence that bis_rbr is stimulus-invariant and must not be cited as such.

WHAT WOULD FIX IT. The binding limit is cells, not recordings: 64 cells over 39 recordings, each needing >= 5 stimulus-on and >= 5 stimulus-off windows at a MATCHED MOAA/S level. A larger held-out pass raises cells roughly linearly. Whether an ecg_hr interval of half the current width would clear +-0.25 is arithmetic, not a new design -- and it is the only change that would be legitimate, since the margin, the estimand and the control are all already declared.

Pre-declared sensitive: emg_index, emg_beta_gamma_fraction, emg_kurtosis, bis_rbr

NOTHING ADDS. 42 held-out recordings, 10,076 usable windows, 27 candidates tested for out-of-bag increment over a baseline built from the deposit's OWN shipped PE31 and SEF95. G1 (zero overlap with the 43 used recordings) and G2 (coverage) PASSED.

**ADDS: none. HURTS: none. All 27 candidates returned NO INCREMENT**, including whole_head_exponent, lempel_ziv, spectral_entropy, multiscale_entropy_slope, the four BIS subparameters and every coherence and wPLI band. The largest point estimates were coherence_alpha +0.0188 [-0.0071, +0.1056] and coherence_theta +0.0144 [-0.0021, +0.0800], both intervals containing zero.

G3 CONFIRMS THE INCUMBENT WAS ALIVE AND THERE WAS ROOM: baseline out-of-bag rho +0.3310 against MOAA/S -- far from a ceiling, so this is not a headroom artefact (the E61 trap). The Gaussian negative control returned +0.0003 [-0.0005, +0.0026], so the machinery is not penalising an extra column either.

CONSEQUENCE. Combined with E78 (bis_rbr and corrected PE tie on held-out data) and E99 (the exponent HURTS BIS for suppression detection), the comparator question for Challenge C now has a consistent answer across three independent held-out tests: **on this deposit, nothing this project computes adds to a validated incumbent.** That is a result, not a failure to find one, and it is the honest thing to carry into any product framing.

deposit: OpenNeuro ds007554 ERD time course, sub-001 excluded (E83 smoke-test burn)
gates: G1 coverage: >= 8 contributing subjects
G2 anchor alive: activemotor minus passivemotor in the EARLY window excludes zero and is negative
G2b PREMISE gate: the anchor's early contrast must exceed its late contrast in magnitude, else the latency reading of PMID 27529874 does not hold here and the verdict is ABSENT
STOPPING RULE: third and final attempt; a gate failure closes ds007554 for this question
instrument_changed: fixed late-window ERD magnitude -> early-window ERD from a 0.25 s time course, with a premise gate on early-versus-late concentration; change dictated by PMID 27529874 rather than by the data
outcome_detail:
BOTH GATES FAILED AND THE STOPPING RULE WAS APPLIED AS REGISTERED. ds007554 is CLOSED for the covert-versus-passive contrast.

G2, the overt anchor in the EARLY [0.00, 0.75] s window: activemotor minus passivemotor d_z = -0.089 [-0.685, +0.322] over 20 subjects. G2b, the PREMISE gate: the anchor's early contrast (|-0.089|) is SMALLER than its late contrast (|+0.296|), so the effect is not concentrated early and PMID 27529874's latency reading does not hold in this deposit. G1 passed with 23 subjects.

ONE THING DID MOVE THE PREDICTED WAY AND IT IS WORTH RECORDING. Across the three attempts the anchor ran +0.393 (E82, whole-run median over 33 channels), +0.271 (E83, cue-locked late window, sensorimotor) and -0.089 (E85, cue-locked early window, sensorimotor). Sharpening the instrument moved the estimate monotonically toward the ERD direction and never made it detectable. That is what a small-or-absent effect being measured better looks like, and it is why a fourth statistic would not be evidence.

THE SUBSTANTIVE READING, which is more than a machinery failure. Three instruments could not distinguish overt movement from robot-assisted passive movement on sensorimotor alpha, in 20-23 healthy subjects. That is CONSISTENT with PMID 31425038's finding that passive haptic movement elicits mu and beta ERD of its own -- if passive movement desynchronises about as much and about as early, active-minus-passive is a poor volition probe here regardless of statistic. **A volition contrast needs a condition WITHOUT movement, not a condition with movement the subject did not initiate.**

ONE ALTERNATIVE I CANNOT EXCLUDE AND WILL NOT GLOSS: the deposit's events are `trial_type=target`, duration 0.5 s, 19 per run. Whether they mark movement ONSET or a preparatory cue is not stated in what was read, and if they are preparatory cues then every window in all three experiments was misaligned by an unknown lag. Checking that would require the deposit's task documentation, and it is the first thing a successor on any ds007554 event-locked question owes.

deposit: Stieger 62-channel graph table (stieger_graph62.csv) joined to the accuracy column
gates: G1 coverage: >= 30 subjects for D1, >= 25 pairs for D2
G2 capability: ge_norm must vary non-degenerately across subjects (rule 53)

G3 ESCAPE HOLDS: |rho(ge_norm, deg)| < 0.90 on the COMPLETED table, else this is E73 again and the verdict is ABSENT. The pre-registration check on the partial table gave +0.2570 for ge_norm against +0.9702 for raw global efficiency
instrument_changed: 10 channels -> 62, AND raw weighted global efficiency -> the same measure normalised against weight-preserving nulls, which is the part that actually changes the instrument: the 62-channel raw measure still sits at +0.9702 with mean strength
outcome_detail:
PREDICTS in D1 -- Challenge B's first primary to clear its own gates -- and it comes with four qualifications, all of which must travel with it.

THE RESULT. `ge_norm` (global efficiency divided by its mean over 20 weight-shuffled nulls) reaches D1 rho **+0.307 [+0.049, +0.534]** between subjects (n=62), interval excluding zero, in the direction PMID 26529439 predicted and this registration named in advance. The accuracy-permutation placebo gives [-0.235, +0.219] and the primary lies outside it. G1 (62 subjects, 123 pairs), G2 (sd 0.0451) and G3 -- the rule-60 escape check re-run on the completed table -- all passed.

QUALIFICATION 1, THE INCUMBENT. The registration required 'report the incumbent beside it, and claim superiority only on non-overlapping intervals'. **The code did not compute it**; the same defect as E73's missing P3, and it is completed here rather than dropped. `relative_alpha_power` reaches D1 rho +0.181 [-0.085, +0.415] against `ge_norm`'s +0.307 [+0.043, +0.540]. **The intervals overlap heavily, so NO superiority over the incumbent is claimed.**

QUALIFICATION 2, MULTIPLICITY. Over the five-feature family, `ge_norm`'s BH q = **0.0920** -- it does NOT survive at q = 0.05. It is the pre-declared primary, so the family correction is context rather than its bar, but a reader is entitled to both numbers and here they disagree.

QUALIFICATION 3, BETWEEN-SUBJECT ONLY. D2, the consecutive-session change design, is null: +0.120 [-0.073, +0.310] for the primary and +0.020 [-0.167, +0.202] for the incumbent. **A between-subject effect with a null within-subject change is the signature E73 refused to promote `wpli_alpha_clustering` for**, and consistency requires the same caution here -- it is what a stable trait-like confound looks like, and D1's ceiling (0.8087, E68) is lower than D2's (0.9478).

QUALIFICATION 4, ONE FAMILY MEMBER ALSO CLEARS. `iaf` -- individual alpha frequency, a genuinely different family from connectivity -- reaches D1 +0.255 [+0.018, +0.468]. Context, not a result.

WHAT IS NEW HERE AND SURVIVES ALL FOUR. E73's null was on a measure that turned out to BE mean connectivity strength (rho +0.9702 with mean degree even at 62 channels). `ge_norm` was verified to escape that family BEFORE registration (+0.2570 with mean degree) and is the only autonomous graph measure here that both escapes it and predicts. **The finding is that the escaping measure predicts where the non-escaping one did not** -- which is rule 60 paying for itself -- and not that BCI ability has been explained.

primary: ge_norm = global efficiency divided by its mean over 20 weight-shuffled null graphs, PREDICTED POSITIVE (PMID 26529439); D1 between-subject and D2 consecutive-session change, identical to E73's designs; REVERSED branch named first; family of 4 at BH q=0.05 as context
question: Does a network measure SHOWN to escape mean connectivity strength predict BCI ability, where E73's global efficiency -- which did not escape it -- returned a real null?

deposit: ds004541 (62ch, baseline vs post-LOC; sub-02 excluded as smoke-test burn) and ds005620 (65ch)
gates: G1 >= 5 frontal and >= 5 posterior channels in every recording, counts reported
G2 >= 5 recordings per state per deposit
G3 0.696*frontal + 0.718*posterior must reproduce the stored uce_v1 column to 1e-6, else the stored column is not what its name says
outcome_detail:
G3 FAILED ON BOTH DEPOSITS AND THE EXPERIMENT HAS TWO IMPLEMENTATION DEFECTS. The verdict is ABSENT. The descriptive numbers below are recorded because a successor needs them; NONE is licensed.

DEFECT 1 -- THE GATE WAS WRITTEN AND NOT WIRED. G3 is registered as gating the primary. The code computes and prints it and then evaluates the primary anyway. That is rule 40's inverse: not a gate that cannot fail, but a gate whose failure does nothing. Found by reading the output against the registration rather than by any test.

DEFECT 2 -- ds004541's STATE TOKENS ARE WRONG. Its recording ids are time offsets around loss of consciousness (`@start-180`, `@loc-300`, `@loc-60`, `@loc+30`, ...). The anaesthetised token list contained `loc`, which matches `@loc-300` -- 300 seconds BEFORE loss of consciousness. So that arm's 'anaesthetised' set mixes pre- and post-LOC recordings, and its 'awake' set found only 2 rows. G2 correctly refused a DELTA-R for that deposit, which is the only reason the error did not produce a number.

G3's DIAGNOSIS DIFFERS BY DEPOSIT, and only one is benign. On ds005620 the two tables are on DIFFERENT WINDOWS -- n_samples 150,000 in the regional table against 100,000 in ds005620_features.csv at the same 5,000 Hz, i.e. 30 s against 20 s, because the regional extractor defaulted to --window-s 30. **So G3 as written could not distinguish 'the stored column is not what its name says' from 'these are different windows', which means the gate was mis-specified.** On ds004541 the windows MATCH (30,000 samples both) and G3 still fails at max |diff| 0.123 over 106 shared rows. That second failure is unexplained and is the first thing a successor must resolve.

The frontal-minus-posterior difference flips sign, -0.1671 awake to +0.0957 anaesthetised. **That is the predicted decoupling and it is the outcome that would rescue the two-region framing** -- which is exactly why it must not be reported from a run whose gate failed.

gates: G1 >= 3 adult awake cohorts with >= 20 recordings each
