outcome_detail:
NO TRANSPORT, and it is unambiguous: **0 of 6 adult awake pairs land within +-0.5 weighted-SD units of zero. Five FAIL and one is UNDETERMINED.** Referenced to LEMON, awake eegmmidb sits at -0.963 [-1.242, -0.676] and awake ds005620 at +1.212 [+0.757, +1.647]; referenced to eegmmidb, ds005620 sits at +1.649 [+1.290, +1.990]. The awake centre moves by up to 1.6 weighted SD depending only on which cohort supplied the reference.

**The sentence 'UCE = 0 means the average awake reference population' is therefore not defensible outside the cohort the reference came from**, and every absolute threshold, alert level and cross-dataset comparison built on it inherits that displacement. This is the red-team objection stated in its own terms -- z-scoring can look stable when the raw centroids are not -- confirmed on three independent adult awake cohorts totalling 589 recordings.

G4 passed: self-referencing gives exactly 0, so the standardisation is implemented correctly and the failures are not arithmetic. G3 passed: no reference SD is near zero.

TWO WEAKNESSES, BOTH MINE, BOTH STATED RATHER THAN BURIED. (1) **THE POSITIVE CONTROL IS ABSENT.** HBN was to supply it -- children should show a LARGE offset, and a scheme showing none would not be measuring what it claims -- but HBN returned n = 0 usable recordings, because its EGI `E<n>` channel names match neither region set (QUEUE.md Q39). So the design cannot demonstrate that the scheme detects a difference it SHOULD detect, and 'it shows offsets everywhere' is not fully excluded as an alternative to 'the centroids really move'. (2) **ds004541 contributed 2 recordings instead of ~59**, because E88's cohort selector matches the substring `baseline` while that deposit's awake recordings are labelled `@start-*` and `@loc-*` -- the same rule-61 defect E92 fixed in the state parser and which E88 inherited. The six pairs reported are all between LEMON, eegmmidb and ds005620 and are unaffected; ds004541 was dropped for a bug, not a reason.

ONE DESCRIPTIVE NUMBER WORTH KEEPING: eegmmidb's frontal SD is 0.9538 against LEMON's 0.4394 and against its own posterior SD of 0.2586. A frontal spread twice any other cohort's is more likely a channel-quality property than a population one, and any successor should look at it before treating eegmmidb as a reference.

deposit: VitalDB vitaldb_grid.csv, 6,679 windows / 250 cases, BIS+SQI+EMG+event timestamps
gates: G1 the incumbent must be alive: BIS alone out-of-bag AUC > 0.55, else 'the exponent adds to BIS' is a statement about the label (the E61 trap)
G2 >= 100 cases and >= 200 positive windows
G3 negative control: a Gaussian column must not return ADDS
outcome_detail:
G2 FAILED AT 173 POSITIVE WINDOWS AGAINST A REGISTERED FLOOR OF 200 -- AND THE REASON IS THE FINDING. G1 passed decisively: BIS alone reaches out-of-bag AUC 0.8094 for emergence proximity, so the incumbent is very much alive and this is not the E61 trap. The primary was not evaluated; the verdict is ABSENT.

THE MISSINGNESS IS OUTCOME-RELATED AND SEVERE (rule 14). Of the 579 windows within 600 s of anaesthesia end, only 173 carry a finite BIS -- 29.9 % retention -- while 5,672 of 6,100 windows elsewhere do, 93.0 %. **The loss is entirely BIS's.** The EEG-derived aperiodic exponent is finite in 435 of the same 579 emergence windows (75.1 %), two and a half times BIS's coverage, and median SQI is essentially unchanged (90.4 at emergence against 92.3 elsewhere), so this is not a quiet signal-quality collapse.

THE REGISTERED DESIGN WAS THEREFORE ASKING A QUESTION THE DEPOSIT CANNOT ANSWER IN THAT FORM. Requiring a finite BIS conditions on the monitor still reporting -- precisely when it is being removed. Any increment-over-BIS analysis at emergence is conditioned on the incumbent's own availability, and the feasibility count that set the 600 s horizon (579 windows) measured the wrong denominator because it did not require covariate completeness. The horizon is NOT widened here: changing a threshold after a gate failure is the move DISCOVERY_LOOP.md forbids.

WHAT THIS IMPLIES, and it reframes the use case rather than killing it. The proposed first indication -- an emergence or lightening trend -- needs a measure that EXISTS at emergence. On this deposit the incumbent largely does not, and a self-computed aperiodic index largely does. **The defensible question is therefore availability, not increment**, and it is registered as E90. Note the interpretation that must travel with it: BIS is written by the vendor's device while the exponent is computed here from the raw wave, so an availability gap is a fact about device behaviour, not about the brain.
placebo: A3 MUSCLE -- the monitor's own EMG channel added to the baseline, not a gamma-power proxy. E69/E71 measured this project's scalp proxy at rho +0.20 against a real submental channel, so a device EMG channel is a materially better control
primary: out-of-bag AUC increment of BIS + whole_head_exponent over BIS alone for |rel_aneend_s| <= 600 s, clustered on CASE, 400 replicates; UNRESTRICTED (rule 49 -- the BIS<60 band is a declared secondary arm because it selects on the incumbent); HURTS branch named first
question: Does a single-channel aperiodic exponent add to BIS for predicting proximity to a timestamped clinical emergence event -- the one endpoint on VitalDB that BIS did not define?

deposit: VitalDB vitaldb_grid.csv, 250 cases
gates: G1 >= 80 cases with >= 3 windows in each cell
G2 the per-case DiD must vary across cases
G3 random-landmark placebo, 200 draws: a real DiD inside the central 95 % is WITHDRAWN, because an arbitrary moment reproducing the gap would make it about time-in-case or record edges
instrument_changed: the endpoint moves from increment-over-BIS to availability-of-either, because requiring a finite BIS conditions on the incumbent still reporting -- precisely when it is being removed. No threshold, cohort or horizon changed
outcome_detail:
AVAILABLE AT EMERGENCE, and the effect is large, specific and survives its placebo. DiD = +0.3678 [+0.3215, +0.4152] over 134 cases. The two halves show where it comes from: away from emergence the two indices are nearly equally available (gap +0.0830), while within 600 s of anaesthesia end the self-computed aperiodic exponent is available about 45 percentage points more often than BIS (gap +0.4509).

THE PLACEBO IS WHAT MAKES IT AN EMERGENCE FINDING. A landmark drawn uniformly at random within each case's own span, same half-width and same cell minima, 200 draws, gives [-0.0612, +0.0214]. The real DiD is far outside it, so this is not about time-in-case, record edges, or a general availability difference -- all of which the difference-in-differences and the placebo were built to absorb.

WHAT IT IS NOT, and both sentences must travel with the number. **This is a fact about DEVICE BEHAVIOUR.** BIS is written by the vendor's monitor; the exponent is computed here from the raw waveform. The finding is that the monitor stops publishing its index near anaesthesia end while the amplifier keeps publishing a wave. It is not a claim that the exponent is more accurate, and it is not a claim about the brain. **And availability is not validity.** The windows where a monitor withdraws its own index are exactly the windows where artefact is most likely -- E22 and E58 measured that this deposit's light-end windows are overwhelmingly facial EMG. Establishing that the exponent is TRUSTWORTHY in those windows is a separate experiment and was not attempted.

WHY IT MATTERS ANYWAY. E89 could not run its increment test because requiring a finite BIS conditions on the incumbent still reporting, and 70 % of emergence windows fail that condition. The same fact, asked as a question rather than suffered as an exclusion, is the one operationally meaningful thing this deposit can say about an emergence-trend use case: an index you compute yourself exists in periods where the vendor's does not. Whether it should be BELIEVED there is the next question, not this one.
placebo: a FAKE landmark drawn uniformly within each case's own span, same half-width and cell minima
primary: DiD = mean_case[ (P(exponent finite) - P(BIS finite) | within 600 s of anaesthesia end) - (the same gap over all other windows) ], case-level bootstrap; PREDICTED POSITIVE; WORSE-AT-EMERGENCE branch named first
question: Is a self-computed aperiodic index AVAILABLE in the peri-emergence period where the commercial index is not -- and is that gap specific to emergence rather than general?

deposit: awake recordings of eegmmidb, ds004541 baseline, ds005620 awake; both-state arms on ds004541 and ds005620; HBN children in a separate block
gates: G1 >= 3 adult awake cohorts with >= 20 recordings
G2 >= 2 deposits carrying both states with >= 5 recordings each
G3 construction check: S5 self-centring must transport at 0 to 1e-9
G4 >= 5 frontal and >= 5 posterior channels per recording
outcome_detail:
**RANK/PERCENTILE REFERENCING IS THE RECOMMENDATION, AND IT COSTS NOTHING.** S3_rank is the only autonomous scheme whose worst held-out awake centre stays inside the +-0.5 margin (worst 0.2982), and it ALSO has the best discrimination of any autonomous scheme (mean Cohen's d +1.1261) -- better than the z-score scheme UCE v1 uses (+1.0091), better than the unreferenced exponent (+0.8599), and better than the S5 ceiling that is allowed to use the target cohort's own awake data (+1.0519). It is a Pareto winner, not a trade.

TRANSPORT, worst |mean| over four leave-one-out held-out awake cohorts: S3_rank 0.2982; S7_contrast 0.2254; S4_pooled 1.1757; S1_z_mean_sd 1.2124; S2_z_median_iqr 1.2611; S6_raw 1.8821. **Neither robustness nor pooling repairs the z-score scheme** -- median/IQR is slightly WORSE than mean/SD, and pooling across all reference cohorts barely moves it. What repairs it is dropping the assumption that the measure is on a common interval scale at all, which is exactly what a percentile does.

DISCRIMINATION, mean Cohen's d over ds004541 and ds005620: S3_rank +1.1261, S5_self +1.0519, S4_pooled +1.0149, S1 +1.0091, S2 +1.0063, S6_raw +0.8599, S7_contrast +0.6228. **S7 shows the trade the design was built to expose**: the scale-free within-recording contrast transports well and throws away most of the state signal doing it. S3 does not.

A REGISTERED PREDICTION WAS RIGHT AND ANOTHER WAS WRONG. Right: 'S3 RANK transports best among the autonomous schemes, because it is the only one invariant to a monotone rescaling of the measure.' **Wrong: 'S6 RAW discriminates as well as S1'** -- raw is +0.8599 against S1's +1.0091, a gap of 0.15 d. Referencing does buy discrimination on these deposits, modestly, and the prediction that it would not was made from the redundancy algebra and is not supported.

G3 construction check passed at 3.05e-16: S5_self transports at exactly zero, so the standardisation machinery is sound and the failures of S1/S2/S4 are real.

WEAKNESSES, both stated. **The children positive control is absent** -- HBN returned n = 0 because its EGI `E<n>` channel names match neither region set (Q39), so the design cannot show that S3 would flag a genuinely different population rather than being merely insensitive. That is the single most important thing a successor owes. And discrimination rests on two deposits whose effects differ fourfold (ds004541 d ~1.58, ds005620 d ~0.44), so the mean is not a stable ranking statistic on its own.

RULE 61, THIRD OCCURRENCE, MINE TWICE OVER: the substring tokens were fixed in this file's awake-cohort dict and left standing in its sibling state dict, so ds004541 dropped out of the both-state arm and G2 refused the first run. Both now call E92's parsers -- one implementation rather than two token lists that can drift (rule 20).
placebo: S5_self is the built-in ceiling: it transports perfectly and discriminates identically BY CONSTRUCTION, which is why AUTONOMY is a declared property and S5 is excluded from the ranking rather than allowed to win it

gates: G1 >= 5 frontal and >= 5 posterior channels per recording
G2 >= 5 recordings per state per deposit
G3a formula exact to 1e-9 on rows where both passes agree on the input (STRICTER than E87's 1e-6)
G3b < 5 % of shared rows non-reproducible between independent fetches, every one NAMED and EXCLUDED
all gates return before the primary -- E87's G3 was written and not wired
instrument_changed: state assignment moves from substring matching to entity parsing; the ds005620 window is matched to its comparison table; G3 is split into a stricter formula check and a separate reproducibility check that excludes rather than kills
outcome_detail:
ds004541: NO DECOUPLING, all four gates passed, and it REVERSES the impression E87 left. ds005620: ABSENT on a gate I mis-specified.

ds004541, clean: awake n=59 r(frontal, posterior) = +0.7523 [+0.6186, +0.8439] (implied PC1 VE 87.6 %); anaesthetised n=34 r = +0.7315 [+0.5248, +0.8801] (VE 86.6 %). **DELTA-R = -0.0208 [-0.2395, +0.1797].** The regions are as collinear under anaesthesia as awake. G3b excluded the two non-reproducible rows by name (sub-04@loc+30, sub-04@loc+180, 1.87 % of shared rows); G3a passed at max |diff| 9.98e-10; 12 rows matched neither parser and were left unassigned rather than forced.

**E87's 'DECOUPLES' WAS THE LABELLING BUG.** That result came only from ds005620, whose awake set had been contaminated by `acq-rest` sedated recordings matching the token `rest` (rule 61). With the BIDS `task-` entity parsed the deposit holds 59 awake and 143 anaesthetised, not 164 and 38. The striking number is gone and the gate that refused E87 is the only reason it was never reported.

WHY ds005620 IS ABSENT, AND IT IS MY DESIGN ERROR. G3a required the recomputed 0.696*F + 0.718*P to match the stored uce_v1 to 1e-9. ds005620 came in at **1.05e-9** and ds004541 at **9.98e-10** -- the two deposits sit either side of the threshold by a few percent. **At 5 kHz over a 20 s window that tolerance is at the scale of double-precision accumulation, so the gate cannot distinguish a formula error from float noise.** I set it. Rule 58 permits one repair per question and E92 was it, so ds005620's verdict stands as ABSENT rather than being rescued by a third revision; the cost is paid rather than argued away.

WHAT IS LICENSED. On the one deposit that cleared every gate, the frontal/posterior split does NOT earn its second coefficient under anaesthesia -- consistent with `uce_v1.py`'s algebra (equal PC1 loadings are a necessity for two standardised variables, and 96.8 % VE is r = 0.936 restated) and with the three-cohort redundancy already recorded there. One deposit and one agent; a successor on ds005620 would need a tolerance specified from the arithmetic rather than from a round number.

deposit: LEMON reference (215) placing eegmmidb, ds004541, ds005620, Sleep-EDFx five-stage, VitalDB BIS bands and DOSE-I MOAA/S levels
gates: G1 transport holds in percentile units: eegmmidb awake median within +-0.10
G2 monotone staircase W > N1 > N2 > N3 on Sleep-EDFx; REM EXCLUDED because its placement is P3
G3 >= 30 recordings per reported stratum
G4 direction check: N3's median must be NEGATIVE, guarding the deliberate sign flip
outcome_detail:
G2 FAILED AND THE DIAGNOSIS IS A SUBSTANTIVE FINDING ABOUT RANK REFERENCING. The verdict is ABSENT. G1 passed (eegmmidb awake median +0.0674, inside the +-0.10 transport margin) and G4 passed (N3 negative, so the sign convention is right).

**THE PERCENTILE COORDINATE SATURATES.** The staircase requires W > N1 > N2 > N3 and returns +0.4674, -0.2837, **-0.5000, -0.5000**. N2 and N3 are both pinned at the floor -- -0.5 means BELOW THE ENTIRE LEMON AWAKE REFERENCE DISTRIBUTION, i.e. the 0th percentile. So are VitalDB's BIS [20,40) and [40,60) bands, and ds004541's anaesthetised arm. The coordinate cannot order them because they are all off the bottom of it.

**THIS QUALIFIES E91'S RECOMMENDATION MATERIALLY AND E91 COULD NOT HAVE SEEN IT.** E91 scored discrimination on a BINARY awake-versus-anaesthetised contrast, where saturation is harmless and rank won on both axes. On a GRADED depth staircase rank loses the ordering entirely. Rank referencing buys transport and pays for it in dynamic range below the reference, and the two-axis bake-off had no way to charge it that cost. For the anaesthesia use case this is decisive: a percentile-referenced index would sit pinned at 0 % through most of general anaesthesia, however well it transports.

**THE GATE PREVENTED A WRONG HEADLINE.** Had G2 not fired, P1 would have returned TWO-SIDED: DOSE-I MOAA/S 4 sits at +0.3512 [+0.1279, +0.4023], above the awake centre with an interval excluding it. But MOAA/S 4 is LIGHT SEDATION, not a hyperexcitable state. That positive placement is a cross-deposit offset -- the same displacement E88 measured -- not a Goldilocks positive arm, and it would have been reported as one.

DESCRIPTIVE AND NOT LICENSED, but each is a transport observation worth keeping: Sleep-EDFx WAKE sits at +0.4674, near the TOP of the reference, so sleep-lab awake subjects have flatter spectra than LEMON's awake adults; ds004541 sits at -0.4907 awake and -0.5000 anaesthetised, essentially its whole range below LEMON's; eegmmidb awake at +0.0674 is the only cohort that lands where the reference says awake should be. Three different awake populations, three different places on a coordinate whose zero is supposed to mean awake.

WHAT A SUCCESSOR NEEDS: **a reference that spans the range it intends to measure, not only the awake part of it.** A percentile is only informative inside the support of its reference distribution, and an awake-only reference has no support below wakefulness -- which is the entire region an anaesthesia or sleep index has to resolve.
placebo: none applicable -- this places strata on a measurement axis and consults no outcome. The construction guard is G4 and the transport guard is G1, both on data the reference never saw
primary: P1 does any non-reference stratum have a median UCE-R above zero with a cluster-bootstrap interval excluding it; NOT-A-DEPTH-AXIS branch named first; PREDICTED ONE-SIDED. P2 is the awake IQR tighter than every suppressed stratum's (is wake a zone or an endpoint). P3 REM's placement, carrying E70's 58.7 % muscle caveat
question: Is the Goldilocks axis an inverted U or a floor? Under a percentile reference built from 215 awake adults, does ANY state stratum this project can reach sit ABOVE the awake centre?

deposit: R-SPAN = LEMON awake (215) + ds005620 anaesthetised (143); tested on Sleep-EDFx stages and eegmmidb awake, neither in either reference
gates: G1 disjoint: no reference subject appears in the staircase or transport cohorts, asserted on ids
G2 support exists: under R-SPAN < 5 % of staircase recordings at an extreme percentile -- the mechanism P1 depends on, so monotonicity without it must not be credited to the span
G3 >= 30 per stage and >= 100 in each reference half
G4 direction: N3 below W under both references
instrument_changed: the reference distribution gains support below wakefulness; the scoring machinery, cohorts and margins are unchanged
outcome_detail:
G2 FAILED AT 0.2028 AGAINST A 0.05 FLOOR, SO THE VERDICT IS ABSENT -- and the gate did exactly the job it was registered to do. It was written as 'the mechanism P1 depends on, so monotonicity without it must not be credited to the span', and monotonicity appeared while a fifth of the staircase stayed saturated.

WHAT THE SPAN REFERENCE ACTUALLY DID, and it is most of the way there. Extreme-percentile fraction on the staircase cohort fell from **0.5168 under R-AWAKE to 0.2028 under R-SPAN** -- from more than half the recordings pinned at an extreme to a fifth. The staircase went from NOT monotone (N2 and N3 tied at the floor, both -0.5023 with zero-width intervals) to **monotone**: W +0.3073, N1 -0.2025, N2 -0.5279, N3 -0.5838. And transport did NOT degrade -- awake eegmmidb sits at +0.0419 under R-SPAN against +0.0651 under R-AWAKE, both inside the +-0.10 margin. **Had G2 not gated, both co-primaries would have passed.** G1 confirmed zero shared subject ids between the references and the test cohorts.

WHY IT IS STILL SHORT, and the diagnosis is specific. **N3's interval is zero-width at -0.5838: every single N3 recording is at the floor of the extended reference.** N2 separated from N3 only because N2 is partly inside the reference's support. The suppressed anchor is ds005620's propofol SEDATION, which does not reach the depth of N3 sleep, so the reference gained support -- but not enough of it, and not in the region that matters most.

SO RULE 62 SURVIVES AND SHARPENS: it is not enough for the reference to span 'awake to suppressed'. **It must reach as deep as the deepest state to be measured**, and a sedation cohort cannot anchor a scale that has to resolve deep NREM or surgical anaesthesia. The obvious remedy is a deeper anchor with a comparable montage -- ds004541's post-LOC general anaesthesia, 62 channels, which E93 placed at the floor of the awake-only reference -- and that is E95, registered with a stopping rule because E93, E94 and E95 are three passes at one question.
placebo: R-AWAKE is the built-in comparison arm: the identical machinery on E93's awake-only reference, recomputed here rather than quoted across experiments
primary: P1 is the Sleep-EDFx staircase W>N1>N2>N3 strictly monotone under R-SPAN; P2 does awake eegmmidb stay within +-0.10 of the reference's own awake landmark; BOTH must hold; RANGE-BOUGHT-WITH-THE-ORIGIN branch named first; PREDICTED both hold
question: Does a reference SPANNING the measured range restore the graded staircase that a percentile reference loses to saturation, without giving back the cross-cohort landmark it was chosen for? Rule 62's own prescription, tested.

deposit: R-SPAN-DEEP = LEMON awake (215) + ds005620 anaesthetised (143) + ds004541 post-LOC (36); tested on Sleep-EDFx and eegmmidb, neither in any reference
gates: G1 disjoint reference and test subjects
G2 extreme-percentile fraction < 0.05
G3 coverage
G4 direction
instrument_changed: the reference gains a deeper anchor (ds004541 post-LOC, 62 channels); cohorts, margins, gates and scoring unchanged
outcome_detail:
G2 FAILED AT 0.0705 AGAINST MY 0.05 FLOOR. **THE STOPPING RULE APPLIES AND THE LINE IS CLOSED**, as registered. But the evidence points one way and the honest report is the trajectory, not the binary.

THREE REFERENCES, EACH ADDING SUPPORT, EVERY NUMBER MOVING THE RIGHT WAY:
   R_AWAKE      n=215   extreme fraction 0.5168   staircase NOT monotone   transport +0.0651
   R_SPAN       n=358   extreme fraction 0.2028   staircase monotone       transport +0.0419
   R_SPAN_DEEP  n=394   extreme fraction 0.0705   staircase monotone       transport +0.0381

Saturation fell by roughly half at each step; transport improved at each step; and **N3's interval is no longer degenerate** -- [-0.6193, -0.6117] under the deep reference against a zero-width -0.5838 under the sedation-only span and -0.5023 under awake-only. The deep anchor gave the bottom of the scale resolution it did not have. Both co-primaries would have passed: staircase W +0.2792 > N1 -0.1840 > N2 -0.5025 > N3 -0.6168, and transport +0.0381, the best of the three.

**THE FAILURE IS MY THRESHOLD, AND THIS IS THE SECOND TIME.** I set 0.05 as a round number without asking what fraction is ACHIEVABLE given a 394-recording reference and the tail of the test distribution -- exactly as I set E92's G3a at 1e-9 when double-precision accumulation over a 20 s window at 5 kHz sits right at it, and two deposits landed either side by a few percent. A gate whose threshold is a round number measures the round number.

WHAT IS ESTABLISHED DESCRIPTIVELY, and it is the usable result: **a reference that spans the range you intend to measure restores a graded ordering AND improves cross-cohort transport, and the deeper the anchor the better both get.** Rule 62 is supported by three points of a monotone trend. What is NOT established, by my own pre-commitment, is that any of these references reaches a pre-specified saturation criterion, because the criterion was not derived from anything.

A successor -- if the line is ever reopened, which requires a reason external to this evidence -- must derive the criterion from the arithmetic before looking, and should test whether a reference containing burst-suppression-depth recordings closes the remaining 7 %.
placebo: R_AWAKE and R_SPAN recomputed in the same run as the two comparison arms
primary: P1 monotone Sleep-EDFx staircase and P2 transport within +-0.10, both required; STOPPING RULE: if G2 fails again the line is closed and percentile referencing is recorded as unable to resolve deep states on the deposits this project holds
question: Does a span reference with a DEEP anchor (post-LOC general anaesthesia) resolve the deep states a sedation anchor could not? Third and final pass, with a stopping rule.

deposit: LEMON awake reference (215); Sleep-EDFx staircase and eegmmidb awake as tests, neither in the reference
gates: G1 bulk unchanged: hybrid == rank to 1e-9 inside the reference IQR (a legitimate tolerance here -- same arithmetic on same inputs, unlike E92's)
G2 the tail extrapolates: distinct inputs above the reference max must get distinct scores
G3 disjoint reference and test subjects, asserted on ids
G4 direction: N3 below W under every scheme
outcome_detail:
THE REGISTERED VERDICT IS (c) AND I AM WITHDRAWING IT, because the criterion it cleared was satisfied VACUOUSLY and I wrote the criterion.

WHAT RAN. All four gates passed -- G1 the hybrid equals rank to 1e-9 inside the reference IQR, G2 259 distinct inputs above the reference maximum received 259 distinct scores, G3 zero shared subject ids, G4 direction. S8 satisfied C1 (staircase monotone, N3 interval non-degenerate) and C2 (transport +0.0651, exactly equal to rank's, since the tail never touches the bulk where awake eegmmidb lives).

**WHY IT IS WITHDRAWN: N3's interval under the hybrid is 0.000002 wide.** N2's is 0.000386. Against E95's span-deep reference on the same data, N3 is 0.007614 and N2 0.025381 -- **three to four orders of magnitude more resolution.** The exponential tail decays so fast that every N3 recording compresses into a two-parts-per-million band. The ordering exists; the scale does not. C1 was written as 'non-degenerate (width > 0)' precisely to avoid a round-number threshold after rule 63 was earned twice today -- **and a structural criterion turned out to be satisfiable by a hair, which is the same failure wearing different clothes.** A criterion must be able to distinguish a real effect from its own resolution whether it is a threshold or a structural property.

THE SUBSTANTIVE ANSWER, WHICH THE EXPERIMENT DID PRODUCE. **The span reference DOMINATES the tail model on both axes.** Span-deep: N3 resolution 0.0076, transport +0.0381. Hybrid: N3 resolution 0.000002, transport +0.0651. Reworking the FLOOR beats reworking the SCALING, and it is not close. That answers the question this experiment was commissioned to answer, in the opposite direction from its prediction.

A THIRD DEFECT, IN C2 ITSELF. S1_z's transport is reported as +0.2177 against rank's +0.0651, and **those are not on the same scale** -- one is in standard deviations, the other in percentile units. The S8-versus-S3 comparison is valid because both are percentiles of the same reference; the comparison against z is not, and no conclusion may be drawn from it. z's genuine property, visible in its stage medians (W +2.18 to N3 -4.69, N3 interval 0.488 wide), is that it has real dynamic range -- which was never in doubt and is not what E88 refuted.

WHAT SURVIVES: the hybrid is a correct implementation of a sound idea that buys almost nothing here, because an exponential tail fitted to an awake reference's decile is far too light for a distribution whose suppressed states sit at 2.7 against a reference maximum of 2.0. A heavier-tailed model (a GPD with a fitted positive shape rather than shape 0) might do better and was not tried; but the span reference already achieves what it would be trying to achieve, using data instead of extrapolation, and 'unverifiable exactly where it is used' is a permanent property of any tail model.
placebo: z and rank on the identical reference, plus E95's span-deep rank, are the comparison arms -- the criteria are comparisons against them rather than thresholds (rule 63)
primary: C1 range: monotone staircase AND a non-degenerate N3 bootstrap interval; C2 transport: awake landmark offset no worse than rank's on the same reference; C3 both required. TAIL-MODEL-COSTS-TRANSPORT branch named first; PREDICTED both hold, which is the comfortable prediction and is flagged as such
question: Is the transport/range tension fundamental, or an artefact of only ever trying the two extreme tail models? A hybrid: empirical CDF inside the reference's support, a fitted exponential tail outside it.

deposit: Stieger 62-channel graph table: 62 subjects, 186 sessions, all subjects with >= 2 sessions
gates: G1 >= 40 subjects with >= 2 sessions
G2 the trait control's ICC must exceed the noise control's, else the estimator cannot separate its own controls and no feature can be placed between them
instrument_changed: the estimand moves from feature-to-accuracy association to feature test-retest reliability; no cohort, threshold or contrast changes
outcome_detail:
TRAIT-LIKE, but only moderately, and the interesting finding is what the normalisation cost.

`ge_norm` ICC(2,1) = **+0.4288 [+0.2486, +0.5438]** across 186 sessions in 62 subjects, closer to the trait control `iaf` (+0.6039 [+0.4920, +0.6870]) than to the per-session noise control (+0.0559 [-0.0976, +0.2102]). G2 passed decisively -- the estimator separates its own controls by 0.55 ICC.

**CONSEQUENCE FOR E86: qualification 3 dissolves.** A measure that is stable within a person cannot produce a positive change-score correlation, so D2's null (+0.120 [-0.073, +0.310]) is expected by construction rather than evidence against D1. E86's other three qualifications -- overlapping intervals with the incumbent, BH q = 0.0920, and `iaf` also clearing -- are untouched.

**THE RECIPROCAL OBLIGATION, WRITTEN INTO THE REGISTRATION, FIRES.** E73 refused to promote `wpli_alpha_clustering` for three reasons, the third being a sign reversal in D2. For a trait-like measure a change score is noise and noise takes either sign, so **that third reason is not valid** and E73's refusal now rests on two: it was not pre-declared, and a measure that wins only in the family scan has not won. The refusal stands; one of its legs does not.

**THE FINDING NOBODY ASKED FOR, AND IT IS A REAL COST OF RULE 60's REMEDY.** The raw graph measures are far more reliable than the normalised one: `ge` +0.7830, `deg` +0.7847, `alpha_prom` +0.8411 against `ge_norm`'s +0.4288. Dividing by a weight-shuffled null removes the between-subject strength component -- which is exactly the most reliable part of the signal -- so the measure that escapes mean connectivity (rule 60's requirement) pays for it in test-retest reliability. **Escaping a confounded family and being reliable are in tension, and this is the first time this project has measured that price.**

DESCRIPTIVE ONLY, and post-hoc: at ICC 0.429 for the feature and E68's 0.8087 for stable-ability accuracy, E86's observed +0.307 disattenuates to roughly +0.58. That is an attenuation correction, not a measurement, and it is quoted so a reader can see the scale of the reliability cost -- not as a result.

SCOPE: reliability is not validity. A perfectly reliable measure can be reliably irrelevant, and this decides only how D2's null should be read.
placebo: the two controls ARE the placebo structure: a measure known to be reliable and a per-session random draw, both through the identical estimator on the identical sessions
primary: ICC(2,1) of ge_norm across sessions within subject, subject bootstrap; the verdict is whether it lies closer to the TRAIT control (iaf) or the NOISE control (per-session Gaussian) -- a comparison, not a threshold (rule 63); NOT-COMPUTABLE branch named first
question: Is ge_norm a TRAIT or a STATE? If trait-like, E86's null within-subject change design is expected by construction and its qualification dissolves; if state-like, the null is evidence against the between-subject result.

deposit: VitalDB vitaldb_grid.csv, 250 cases; 92 contribute a (case, BIS band) cell, 106 cells
gates: G1 >= 40 cases and >= 60 cells
G2 bracket: the timestamp control must be DIRECTION-DEPENDENT by construction and a per-window Gaussian must not be
G3 both sides of every cell come from the same BIS band, asserted not assumed
instrument_changed: the state label moves from a clinician's MOAA/S to the monitor's BIS, which changes the estimand to the EEG component BIS does not capture; the docstring states this rather than eliding it
outcome_detail:
NO FEATURE IS DIRECTION-DEPENDENT. Seven are DIRECTION-INVARIANT at +-0.25 within-case SD (emg_beta_gamma_fraction, emg_kurtosis, exponent_gamma, relative_alpha_power, relative_delta_power, spectral_edge_95, spectral_entropy); eleven are UNDETERMINED. 94 cases, 110 (case, BIS band) cells. Both machinery controls bracketed correctly -- the timestamp at -1.413 [-1.469, -1.359] and a per-window Gaussian at -0.058 [-0.182, +0.063].

**THE PLACEBO FIRED SEVEN TIMES AND THAT IS THE RESULT.** Seven features returned a gap whose interval excluded zero -- critical_slowing_ar1 -0.125 [-0.191, -0.065], exponent_high -0.166 [-0.267, -0.064], exponent_low -0.097, lempel_ziv -0.117, multiscale_entropy_slope -0.149, pac_slow_alpha +0.126 and **whole_head_exponent -0.159 [-0.247, -0.069]** -- and EVERY ONE lay inside the random-split placebo distribution. Without the placebo this experiment would have reported seven direction-dependent features including the aperiodic exponent itself.

WHY, AND IT GENERALISES. The BIS minimum sits near the middle of a case, so 'before vs after the minimum' is very nearly 'first half vs second half'. **Any feature with a within-case time trend produces a gap, and the trend has nothing to do with hysteresis.** The random-split placebo preserves the group sizes and the band structure and destroys only the direction of travel, so it isolates exactly that. Now rule 64.

**THIS IS A WARNING FOR E80**, which is registered and unrun on DOSE-I with the same split-at-the-extremum structure. E80 carries the same random-split placebo, so it will catch the same artefact -- but its results must be read placebo-first, and a direction-dependent feature there means nothing until it clears that comparison.

THREE FEATURES WERE NOT COMPUTABLE (n=0): uce_v1, wpli_alpha and spatial_participation_ratio, all empty on VitalDB because it is a single-channel deposit. Consistent with Q39 and reported rather than silently dropped.

SCOPE, restated because it is the sentence most likely to be lost: at matched BIS these are statements about the component of the EEG that BIS does NOT capture, since BIS is computed from the same signal. They are not statements about drug versus state. And DIRECTION-INVARIANT is a necessary condition passed, never a sufficient one.
placebo: each case re-split at a RANDOM index preserving group sizes, BIS band structure intact, 200 draws; destroys direction of travel and nothing else
primary: per feature, standardised descent-minus-emergence gap at matched 10-point BIS band, case-level bootstrap; EQUIVALENCE at +-0.25 within-case SD for DIRECTION-INVARIANT, interval excluding 0 for DIRECTION-DEPENDENT, UNDETERMINED named as its own outcome
question: At MATCHED BIS, does the aperiodic exponent depend on direction of travel through the anaesthetic? Equivalently: does the component of the EEG that BIS does not capture carry hysteresis information?

deposit: VitalDB vitaldb_grid.csv, 5,798 windows with SR+BIS+exponent, 977 positive (16.9 %), 140 of 247 cases
gates: G1 the incumbent must be alive out of bag, else the result is about the label (the E61 trap)
G2 >= 100 cases and >= 300 positive windows
G3 a Gaussian negative control must not ADD
instrument_changed: the endpoint moves from emergence proximity, where BIS is missing in 70 % of windows, to device-measured suppression, where it is not
outcome_detail:
**CORRECTED 2026-08-01. THE RECORDED VERDICT WAS HURTS AND IT WAS A MISSING INTERCEPT COLUMN.**

`oob_auc_increment` fits an IRLS logistic that carries no intercept of its own, and its docstring says the
design matrix must already include one. E99 passed `[BIS]` and `[BIS, whole_head_exponent]` bare, so both
models were fitted THROUGH THE ORIGIN. Reproduced exactly: without the intercept the call returns
**-0.0320 [-0.0544, -0.0111]** against the recorded -0.0306 [-0.0524, -0.0101]; with it, on the identical
5,798 windows, 247 cases and 977 positives, it returns **+0.0168 [+0.0049, +0.0269]**. The sign was an
artefact of the design matrix, not a property of the feature.

RE-RUN WITH THE INTERCEPT, EVERY ARM AND EVERY GATE OF THE ORIGINAL DESIGN:
    G1 incumbent alive   BIS alone, out-of-bag AUC 0.7848
    A1 PRIMARY           +0.0160 [+0.0009, +0.0265]   ADDS
    A2 ARTEFACT-CLEAN    +0.0207 [+0.0028, +0.0334]   ADDS   (4,944 windows)
    A3 MUSCLE            +0.0260 [+0.0082, +0.0393]   ADDS
    A4 NEGATIVE CONTROL  -0.0005 [-0.0029, +0.0002]   correctly null
So the aperiodic exponent ADDS to BIS for detecting device-measured burst suppression, and it survives the
monitor's own EMG channel.

INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATED BY THREE OTHER ESTIMATORS on the same rows (E173): cluster bootstrap with the
logistic +0.0160 [+0.0044, +0.0266], cluster bootstrap with a linear ridge +0.0162, and 5-fold grouped
cross-fitting +0.0235 at p = 0.0000. A training-fraction sweep from 50 % to 95 % stays between +0.017 and
+0.023 throughout. There is no estimator disagreement; there was one broken call.

SCOPE unchanged from the registration: one retrospective deposit, a device-measured suppression endpoint,
no claim about consciousness or awareness. E89 carries the same defect in the same template line, but it
gate-failed at coverage before that line was reached, so no number of its own changes; it is patched
anyway. `stats.py` now RAISES when a design matrix's first column is not a constant, so this cannot recur
silently.
placebo: A3 MUSCLE -- the monitor's own EMG channel added to the baseline, not a gamma or scalp proxy
primary: out-of-bag AUC increment of BIS + whole_head_exponent over BIS alone for meta_sr > 0, clustered on CASE, 400 replicates, UNRESTRICTED (rule 49); HURTS branch named first
question: Does the aperiodic exponent add to BIS for detecting device-measured burst suppression -- against an incumbent that partly computes suppression as one of its own subparameters?

deposit: Sleep-EDFx five-stage windows, per-channel Fpz-Cz and Pz-Oz, 142 subjects; SC4001E0 excluded as smoke-test burn
gates: G1 >= 50 subjects with all five stages in both tables
G2 non-degenerate W-to-N3 axis per subject per measure; failures dropped and counted
G3 known effect: delta must increase W->N3 in more subjects than a Gaussian control (rule 63 -- a comparison, not a fixed fraction)
G4 muscle: submental EMG's own axis position reported, and P1 recomputed after residualising on it; a P1 that survives only before adjustment is muscle and the verdict says so
instrument_changed: the spatial reduction: whole-head median -> the two derivations kept separate, which is the one thing E93's coordinate could not express
outcome_detail:
**THE MEASURE IS NOT THE PROBLEM.** The improvement is real, tiny, not posterior-specific, and entirely muscle. E95's reading -- that the coordinate tracks arousal rather than experience -- survives the best available challenge to it, which strengthens it.

P1 cleared its interval: position(posterior 1-4 Hz) - position(whole-head exponent) = d_z **-0.257 [-0.367, -0.159]**, so posterior delta does place REM closer to wake. **But the median shift is -0.052 on a 0-to-1 axis** -- REM moves from 0.479 to 0.440, which is not a stage crossing, it is a nudge.

**G4 KILLS IT. After residualising every measure on submental EMG within subject, P1 is d_z -0.000 [-0.134, +0.245].** The effect vanishes exactly. And the reason is visible in the EMG's own placement: submental muscle sits at REM position **+1.094**, i.e. BEYOND the N3 end of the axis -- REM has less muscle than deep sleep. Textbook atonia, independently confirming E70's finding on a different measure and a different statistic.

**P2 FOUND NO POSTERIOR SPECIFICITY**: posterior minus frontal d_z +0.011 [-0.118, +0.367]. The locality that motivated the whole design is absent, so even the nudge is about low-frequency power generally rather than about posterior cortex. (The frontal position statistic is also unstable -- IQR [-1.355, +0.293] -- because it is a ratio and frontal delta's W-to-N3 span is small or reversed in some subjects. Posterior is well behaved at IQR [+0.255, +0.556]. A ratio-based position statistic needs a non-degenerate denominator and G2 only excluded exact zeros.)

G3 passed decisively: delta increases from W to N3 in 92.1 % of subjects frontally and 97.9 % posteriorly, against a 52.9 % Gaussian control. The machinery reproduces the textbook effect, so the null is not about broken staging or a broken spectral estimate.

**WHAT THIS DOES NOT SHOW, AND THE DISTINCTION MATTERS.** It does NOT refute Siclari et al. (PMID 28394322). They used high-density EEG with serial awakenings and dream reports, contrasting the PRESENCE and ABSENCE of experience within stage; we have two bipolar derivations, no dream reports, and a between-stage contrast. This shows their remedy does not transfer to what this deposit can measure -- not that their result is wrong. A proper test needs dream reports, and no deposit this project can reach has them.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FRAMING: three independent routes now place REM with sleep rather than wake on this project's measures -- E69's fraction-nearer-wake, E95's axis position, and E100's per-channel low-frequency version -- and in two of the three the placement has been measured to be substantially muscle. **The coordinate should be described as an arousal axis.**
placebo: the frontal channel IS the specificity control -- Siclari's claim is posterior, so a frontal effect of equal size refutes the locality that motivated the design
primary: P1 position(posterior 1-4 Hz relative power) - position(whole-head exponent) on each subject's own W-to-N3 axis, paired d_z; PREDICTED NEGATIVE; REVERSED branch named first. P2 locality: posterior minus frontal, predicted negative -- if frontal matches, there is no locality
question: Does a POSTERIOR low-frequency measure place REM closer to wake than the whole-head aperiodic coordinate does -- i.e. is the spatial reduction what loses REM, rather than the claim being wrong?

deposit: Stieger BCI stieger_graph62.csv joined to stieger_labels.csv; 61 subjects with EXACTLY 3 sessions, so n is identical at every k and no coverage difference can masquerade as an averaging effect
gates: G1 >= 30 subjects with exactly 3 sessions
G2 rho_1 finite and in (0,1), else rho_3 is undefined and the prediction does not exist -> ABSENT
G3 |r(1)| >= 0.05 -- identifiability, not significance: below it both predictions collapse onto 0
G4 the two predictions must differ by >= 0.02, else no amount of data separates them
instrument_changed: from a qualitative placement between two controls to the QUANTITATIVE consequence that placement implies for E86's own correlation -- the first thing in Challenge B that can falsify a verdict we already like
outcome_detail:
UNDETERMINED -- and it was named as the likely outcome before the first pass, which is the only reason that sentence is worth anything.

**THE FIRST PASS WAS WITHDRAWN BEFORE IT WAS LOGGED** (`results/e101_first_pass_note.md` records the numbers that were seen and the flaw). Its registered rule required d_signal = r(3) - r(1) to exclude zero, and that is satisfied BY CONSTRUCTION for any imperfectly reliable measure: for three independent noise columns r(3) = sqrt(3) * r(1) exactly, so d_signal = 0.73 * r(1). The __gauss__ control went +0.1127 -> +0.1441 and would have passed that limb itself. Rule 33, recurring. The correction replaced one uninformative comparison with two competing MODELS the same theory already implied -- H_error (gain = sqrt(rho_3/rho_1) = 1.267) and H_noise (gain = sqrt(k) = 1.732) -- and changed no threshold, cohort, horizon or estimator.

RESULT on 61 subjects with exactly 3 sessions each: ICC(2,1) 0.4349; r(1) +0.2428, r(3) +0.3236 [+0.0679, +0.5440]. **d_error +0.0161 [-0.0456, +0.0710]** and **d_noise -0.0969 [-0.2096, +0.0173]** -- BOTH models lie inside the interval. 61 subjects cannot separate a gain of 1.267 from 1.732.

G5 CALIBRATION, which the first pass lacked entirely and which is the part worth keeping: 200 INDEPENDENT Gaussian features run through the whole procedure (median |r(1)| 0.0490). The H_error limb fires on pure noise **0.0 %** of the time and the H_noise limb **0.5 %**. So the machinery is not manufacturing verdicts; the null is a power null. The C- control was stated in the original docstring and never wired -- the E87 pattern, second occurrence -- and it is now a real gate.

CONSEQUENCE FOR E86/E97. E97's trait reading of ge_norm is neither confirmed nor refuted by its own quantitative consequence. **E86's qualification 3 stays dissolved on E97's grounds and does not gain additional support from E101.** Anyone quoting E97 should quote this beside it.

BRACKETING CONTROLS behaved: alpha_prom (ICC 0.8400) predicted gain 1.058 and went +0.0894 -> +0.1036; iaf (ICC 0.6041) predicted 1.166 and went +0.2396 -> +0.2645.
placebo: C- a per-session Gaussian draw must stay at r ~ 0 for every k, else averaging itself is the effect. C+ alpha_prom (ICC 0.8411) must show the SMALL predicted gain of 1.058, not a large one -- a high-reliability measure has almost nothing to gain from averaging.
primary: r(3) against two pre-stated competing values computed on the same data: r(1)*sqrt(rho_3/rho_1) [measurement error, predicted gain 1.271] and r(1) [no gain]. d_error and d_signal both reported; 4000-rep subject bootstrap with ICC, r(1) and r(3) all REFIT inside each resample because rho and r(1) sit inside the prediction. Wrong direction (averaging HURTS) named first; UNDETERMINED named in advance as the likely outcome.
question: Does averaging sessions raise E86's D1 by the amount E97's ICC(2,1)=0.4288 predicts under Spearman-Brown -- i.e. is the session-to-session variation in ge_norm measurement error on a trait, as E97's verdict assumed when it dissolved E86's qualification 3?

deposit: VitalDB vitaldb_emergence.s?.csv -- a NEW dense pass, every 30 s from -900 s to +300 s around the recorded aneend, 250 cases, 8,509 planned windows. Needed because vitaldb_grid.csv has exactly ONE case with >= 3 peri-emergence windows in both cells, which would make the contrast between-case and therefore between monitors.
gates: G1 >= 40 cases with >= 5 exponent-finite windows in EACH cell
G2 both cells vary -- a rank correlation on a constant is undefined, not zero (rule 32)
G3 TIME OVERLAP: primary re-run inside the 10th-90th percentile overlap band; a sign reversal withdraws the unrestricted estimate, because BIS-absent windows sit later by construction
G4 emg_index reported per cell, never adjusted for -- EMG at emergence is downstream of waking, so conditioning on it is a collider (rule 13)
instrument_changed: the endpoint moves from AVAILABILITY (is the number computable?) to VALIDITY (does the number behave?), which required a new anchor -- clock time relative to anaesthesia end -- because the incumbent is missing in exactly the windows tested
outcome_detail: WITHDRAWN BY PLACEBO. 6,007 peri-emergence windows over 250 cases; 101 cases with >=5 exponent-finite windows in BOTH cells, so G1 passed at 101 >= 40. The primary looked clean: rho(exponent, time-to-aneend) was -0.0940 where BIS was ABSENT and -0.3003 where PRESENT, D = +0.2063 [+0.0875, +0.3279], excluding zero and exceeding the 0.1501 equivalence margin. THE PLACEBO KILLED IT. A CONTIGUOUS RANDOM SPLIT of the same windows into cells of the same sizes reproduces D at [+0.0812, +0.2822] and the real D sits INSIDE. The contrast is about POSITION IN TIME, not about whether the monitor was publishing -- rule 64 exactly: a split keyed to a landmark is a time split in disguise, and only a random-split placebo shows it. G3 flagged the same thing independently: median rel_aneend_s -60 s ABSENT against -435 s PRESENT, and the restricted overlap band [-300,-180] s contained 0 cases, so the cells barely share a time range. G3 FAILED on its own terms and the placebo confirmed why. G4 reported, not adjusted (collider, rule 13): emg_index 0.2573 ABSENT vs 0.3810 PRESENT.
placebo: CONTIGUOUS random split of the same windows within each case, preserving cell sizes AND the temporal block structure; a permuted label would destroy the clustering that defines the real split and would be too easy to beat (rule 64). Real D inside the placebo's central 95 % is WITHDRAWN, and the placebo GATES the verdict (rule 34).
primary: D = mean over cases of [ spearman(exponent, rel_aneend_s | BIS absent) - same | BIS present ], within case, 4000-rep case bootstrap. Anchor is clock time relative to anaesthesia end because BIS cannot be the reference in the windows where BIS is missing. PREDICTED D > 0 (WORSE where BIS is absent) -- i.e. predicted against the product framing. Equivalence margin fixed in advance at half |rho_present|; UNDETERMINED named as its own outcome.
question: Where BIS is ABSENT at emergence, does the aperiodic exponent still carry emergence information -- the believability question E90 measured availability for and explicitly refused to answer?

deposit: ds005620 acq-tms, 55 recordings, 53 ok / 2 too_few_pulses; 64 ch at 5 kHz, task-awake and task-sed WITHIN subject. Pulses detected from the SIGNAL, never from a marker file, because both shipped marker formats are temporally wrong (rule 65). sub-1016 and sub-1074 excluded as burn-in (rule 26), leaving 14 subjects with both conditions.
gates: G1 >= 12 subjects with both conditions
G2 a perturbation was actually measured: real_evoked_rms > sham_evoked_rms, interval excluding 0; failure gives ABSENT, not negative (rule 31)
G3 DETECTION PARITY on n_pulses, iti_median and det_separation -- any difference downgrades to CONFOUNDED-BY-DETECTION regardless of the primary (rule 32)
G4 positive control: spont_exponent must itself separate the states, vs a Gaussian on the same pairs (rule 63)
G5 non-degenerate regressor -- residualising on a constant is vacuous (E96's C1 failure)
instrument_changed: E92 asked whether two REGIONS of the spontaneous signal decouple and found they do not. E103 changes the instrument to a PERTURBATION -- an externally imposed input with a sham arm cut from the same recording -- which is the one thing a spontaneous measure cannot be made into by re-deriving it.
outcome_detail:
ABSENT AT G4 -- the positive control failed and the design refused to emit a verdict (rule 31). spont_exponent separated awake from sedated at d_z -0.4765 (RIGHT direction: sedated higher) against a Gaussian 95th of 0.5982 over 14 subjects, so it did not clear.

G1, G2, G3 and G5 all PASSED, and G2 is worth recording because it was the gate the feasibility note demanded: **a perturbational response WAS measured**, real-minus-sham evoked RMS +4.1139 [+0.0910, +9.4649]. Detection parity held on all three statistics -- n_pulses +0.4762 [-0.1667, +1.2143], iti_median -0.0012 [-0.0356, +0.0327], det_separation +103.98 [-411.42, +629.40] -- so the arms were not being detected differently. Extraction drop-out was balanced: too_few_pulses 1 of 17 awake and 1 of 38 sed (rule 14).

THE CAUSE IS A BUG IN THE EXTRACTOR, NOT THE DEPOSIT, and the diagnostic is independent of the primary. On the SAME deposit and the SAME subjects, the existing non-TMS extraction separates the states at d_z -0.9909 over 20 subjects against a Gaussian 95th of 0.4858 -- it CLEARS comfortably. What differs is how the exponent was computed: the perturbation extractor concatenated ~46 pre-pulse segments of 0.4 s each and then ran Welch with a 1.0 s window, so **every window straddled ~2.5 segment boundaries**. That is rule 27 -- a mask that compresses out bad samples glues time together -- and it corrupts a spectral slope whatever the result would have been. The bug is identifiable without reference to the outcome; the positive control is what made anyone look, which is what positive controls are for.

The verdict stands as ABSENT. E104 is the successor with the spectral estimate fixed; the primary, the cohort, the gates, the thresholds and the placebos are unchanged.
placebo: PRIMARY PLACEBO: awake/sed labels flipped at random within subject, 500 draws -- the exact permutation null for a two-condition paired design; real d_z inside its central 95 % is WITHDRAWN. SECOND PLACEBO, the one that matters most: the identical analysis on sham_evoked_lz ALONE. If the sham matches the primary, what separates the states is the complexity of ongoing EEG and 'perturbational' is decoration.
primary: paired d_z, awake minus sedated, of the residual of (real_evoked_lz - sham_evoked_lz) after regressing out spont_exponent measured on the same bytes. DECOUPLING, not increment. INVERTED (sedated higher) named first. PREDICTED: a second axis is detected, at ~40 %.
question: IS THERE A SECOND AXIS? Does a perturbational (TMS-evoked) response carry state information beyond the spontaneous aperiodic exponent -- the discovery-shaped version of Challenge A, asked because every measure this project has taken so far reduces to one arousal axis.

deposit: ds005620 acq-tms, ds005620_perturbation_v2.csv -- inter-pulse PSDs averaged on their own contiguous samples rather than the time series concatenated. Same recordings, same burn-in exclusions (sub-1016, sub-1074).
gates: G1-G5 unchanged from E103
G4 is the gate that failed in E103 and the reason this successor exists
instrument_changed: the SPECTRAL ESTIMATE only. v1 concatenated ~46 pre-pulse segments of 0.4 s and Welched with a 1.0 s window, so every window straddled ~2.5 discontinuities; v2 transforms each inter-pulse interval on its own samples and averages only the power spectra. outcome_detail:
NO SECOND AXIS DETECTED -- and the sham arm, which was built as a control, is the informative part.

ALL FIVE GATES PASSED, which is what makes this a real null rather than E103's ABSENT. G2: a perturbational response WAS measured, real-minus-sham evoked RMS +4.1139 [+0.0031, +9.8610]. G3 detection parity held on all three statistics (n_pulses +0.4762 [-0.1667, +1.2143]; iti_median -0.0012 [-0.0356, +0.0327]; det_separation +99.28 [-445.75, +659.49]), so the arms were not detected differently. G4, the gate that killed E103: spont_exponent now separates the states at d_z **-0.8424** against a Gaussian 95th of 0.5982 -- the fixed spectral estimate recovered the known effect, and its spread rose from 0.9675 to 1.3498. Extraction drop-out balanced (1 of 17 awake, 1 of 38 sed).

**PRIMARY: residual(real_evoked_lz - sham_evoked_lz | spont_exponent), awake minus sedated, d_z +0.1712 [-0.3894, +0.7598] over 14 subjects.** The interval contains zero. The perturbational contrast carries no state information beyond the spontaneous aperiodic exponent on this deposit. The label-flip placebo ([-0.6038, +0.6197]) is NOT informative here and is not cited as a withdrawal: there was no effect for it to fail to reproduce (rule 48).

**THE SHAM ARM SEPARATES THE STATES AND THE REAL-MINUS-SHAM CONTRAST DOES NOT: d_z -0.7116 [-1.5936, -0.2066], outside its own label-flip placebo [-0.6221, +0.5817].** So on the same recordings, the same channels and the same pipeline, the complexity of ONGOING EEG in the inter-pulse intervals carries state information beyond the exponent, while the response to stimulation adds nothing on top of it. That is the cleanest statement of the single-axis reading this project has: the perturbation was delivered, was measurable, and bought nothing.

PREDICTION CALIBRATION: registered at ~40 % that a second axis would be detected. It was not. This is the fourth measure predicted to be new that turned out not to be (rule 28's tally).

SCOPE, and it is a real limit rather than a hedge. Sedation here is light, not general anaesthesia; n = 14 subjects; `evoked_lz` is a PCI-FAMILY measure on a fixed per-channel threshold, **not** PCI-st and not Casali's bootstrap significance map. A null against a simplified estimator at this n does not refute Casali et al. (PMID 23946194) -- it says this construction, on this deposit, does not decouple from the spontaneous exponent. Nothing here is evidence about consciousness: the deposit carries no experiential report, no responsiveness assessment and no behavioural measure.

outcome_detail:
ABSORBED BY THE FAMILY -- the outcome given 55 % before the run, and it locates E104's sham result precisely rather than leaving it as a loose end.

**G1, the rule-60 escape check, PASSED and is the informative part.** sham_evoked_lz is genuinely not any one of the family: rho -0.3964 (spont_exponent), +0.1533 (spont_lziv), -0.1984 (spont_perm_entropy), +0.5581 (spont_spectral_entropy). So this was NOT E73's failure -- the measure is distinct from every family member individually. It is the family COLLECTIVELY that absorbs it, which is a different and more interesting fact, and one that only a multiple adjustment could have found.

G2 (14 subjects), G3 (condition number 316.4), G4 (spont_exponent d_z -0.8424 vs Gaussian 95th 0.5853) and G5 all PASSED. G5 confirmed the premise survives in v3: E104's quantity -- sham_evoked_lz residualised on spont_exponent alone -- reproduces at d_z **-0.7116 [-1.5664, -0.2077]**, and the v2 and v3 tables were verified byte-identical on both columns across all 53 shared recordings.

**PRIMARY: residual(sham_evoked_lz | whole family), awake minus sedated, d_z -0.3814 [-0.9221, +0.1492] over 14 subjects.** Adding three standard complexity measures to the single exponent adjuster takes the effect from -0.7116 (interval excluding zero) to -0.3814 (interval containing it). The state information E104's sham arm carried is shared with spontaneous complexity measures already in this project's inventory. The placebo ([-0.6413, +0.5619]) is NOT informative here and is not cited as a withdrawal: there was no effect for it to fail to reproduce (rule 48).

ONE DESCRIPTIVE NUMBER WORTH RECORDING, and it is not a claim E104 made: the RAW sham_evoked_lz separation is d_z -0.3467 [-1.0401, +0.1427]. E104's effect was always the exponent-adjusted quantity; an earlier draft of G5 asked the raw column to reproduce an adjusted result, which is a mis-specification and is recorded in the docstring rather than quietly repaired.

WHERE THIS LEAVES CHALLENGE A. E103 (ABSENT, extraction bug), E104 (no second axis, perturbation measurable but useless) and E105 (the promising control is absorbed by the amplitude-complexity family) close the ds005620 perturbational line. **Every candidate remains inside one axis.** The next attempt (E107) changes instrument rather than deposit: time-irreversibility is PROVABLY orthogonal to the whole spectral family -- the autocovariance is symmetric in lag, so the PSD is invariant under time reversal -- and its permutation form is invariant to any monotone amplitude transform, so it cannot be muscle amplitude the way E70/E100's results were.

primary: paired d_z, awake minus sedated, of sham_evoked_lz after a MULTIPLE fit on [spont_exponent, spont_lziv, spont_perm_entropy, spont_spectral_entropy] is removed. E104 removed one line; a family can hide behind three. REVERSED named first. PREDICTED: ABSORBED BY THE FAMILY ~55 %, second axis survives ~25 %, G1 failure ~20 %.
question: E104's SHAM arm -- built only as a control -- separated awake from sedated beyond the aperiodic exponent while the perturbational contrast did not. Does that ongoing-EEG complexity measure escape the exponent AND the spontaneous complexity family, or is it that family restated?

This changes the COMPARATOR to the spectral measure that also predicts accuracy, which is the family E86 never checked, and makes the test symmetric so 'which one survives' is answerable rather than assumed.
outcome_detail:
IT IS THE NETWORK MEASURE -- but read the two caveats printed with the verdict before using it.

**ge_norm and iaf are nearly orthogonal: rho +0.0781.** So E86's primary is not individual alpha frequency wearing a graph-theoretic name, which was the qualification this experiment existed to test and the outcome that would have cost the most. G1 (escape), G2 (62 subjects) and G3 (both raw associations reproduce: ge_norm +0.2934 [+0.0330, +0.5199], iaf +0.2538 [+0.0042, +0.4601]) all PASSED.

SYMMETRIC PRIMARY, both limbs always reported (rule 59):
  A  partial(ge_norm, accuracy | iaf) = **+0.2837 [+0.0046, +0.5213]**, one-sided p 0.0232, permutation p 0.0288 -- OUTSIDE its placebo.
  B  partial(iaf, accuracy | ge_norm) = **+0.2423 [+0.0092, +0.4426]**, one-sided p 0.0204, permutation p 0.0610 -- INSIDE its placebo.

SEED STABILITY (rule 46), and it is the reason the intervals are trustworthy at all: both lower bounds sit within 0.01 of zero, so the binary was re-run at 5 seeds and 20,000 replicates. A excluded 0 in 5/5 and B in 5/5, with lower bounds ranging +0.0064 to +0.0126 (A) and +0.0070 to +0.0095 (B). The verdict does not turn on the RNG.

**TWO CAVEATS THAT MUST TRAVEL WITH THIS RESULT, both printed in the verdict string itself:**
1. RESOLVABILITY. G0 fixed in advance that the minimum detectable partial |rho| at n = 62 is ~0.365. Both partials (0.284, 0.242) are BELOW it. The deposit is underpowered for this comparison and a limb that separates here is liable to the winner's curse.
2. MARGIN. The verdict separates A from B at permutation p 0.0288 against 0.0610 -- close. At 500 placebo draws the same data returned MUTUALLY ABSORBED; 5,000 draws were needed for a stable 97.5th percentile, and raising them is a legitimate fix that changes no threshold. **Treat the DIRECTION as the finding and the binary as unstable.**

WHAT E86 NOW CARRIES. Of its four qualifications: D2's null is explained (E97 trait-like); the quantitative consequence of that is E101; the alpha-frequency alternative is now excluded as a REDESCRIPTION though not as a co-predictor; and **BH q = 0.0920 across the family is untouched and still stands.** That last one is the binding limitation on Challenge B's only positive.
placebo: accuracy permuted across subjects, 500 draws, both partials recomputed; a real partial inside its own placebo is WITHDRAWN. The primary's interval is read FIRST (rule 48).
primary: SYMMETRIC and both always reported (rule 59): A = partial spearman(ge_norm, accuracy | iaf) and B = partial spearman(iaf, accuracy | ge_norm). Rank-partial via residualising both on the control's ranks; 4000-rep subject bootstrap with the residualisation refit inside each. 'IT IS ALPHA FREQUENCY' named FIRST. PREDICTED: mutually absorbed ~45 %, alpha ~30 %, network ~15 %, independent ~10 %.
question: Is E86's ge_norm result just individual alpha frequency? iaf also clears D1 at +0.2552 [+0.0185, +0.4685], and E86's escape gate was aimed at the connectivity family, never at the spectral quantity that also predicts the outcome.

G2 agreement must EXIST -- median within-case rho clearly negative vs a Gaussian control, else there is nothing for age to modulate

instrument_changed: the ENDPOINT stops being 'does our measure beat/add to BIS' -- asked and answered no four times on held-out data -- and becomes 'where does BIS stop tracking the EEG'. That question has no incumbent to beat and needs no ground truth, because disagreement between two simultaneous readings is measurable without knowing which is correct.
outcome_detail:
AGREEMENT DEGRADES WITH AGE -- Challenge C's first genuine positive, and it arrived only after the question changed.

**PRIMARY: spearman(within-case agreement, age) = +0.2592 [+0.1367, +0.3761] over 240 cases.** Agreement is NEGATIVE when BIS and the exponent track each other, so a POSITIVE estimate means they come apart more in older patients. Placebo (age shuffled, 2000 draws) [-0.1292, +0.1210] -- the real estimate is outside it.

EVERY GATE PASSED.
  G1  240 of 247 cases contribute (>= 10 windows, both measures varying).
  G2  Agreement EXISTS to be modulated: median within-case rho(BIS, exponent) = **-0.2822** against a Gaussian 2.5th percentile of -0.1549. The two readings do track each other on average.
  G3  ATTENUATION, the whole methodological risk, and it is not the explanation. Both attenuation routes bias in the SAME direction as the predicted effect, so both were adjusted: range restriction (within-case SD of BIS and of the exponent) and sample size (log n_windows). **None of the three correlates with age at all** -- +0.0555, -0.0656, +0.0109 -- and the partial given all three is **+0.2490 [+0.1234, +0.3684]**, essentially unchanged from the raw estimate.
  G4  Quality does not explain it either: rho(median SQI, age) -0.1323, rho(median emg_index, age) +0.0171, median SQI 92.3. Reported and NOT adjusted, because SQI is the monitor's own confidence and EMG is partly what BIS suppresses -- conditioning on either would condition on the mechanism (rule 13).
  G5  Not a paediatric artefact: only 4 of 240 cases are under 18, and adults-only gives **+0.2409 [+0.1187, +0.3578]**.

**WHAT THIS IS NOT, and the limit is structural rather than a hedge.** This deposit has no ground-truth depth of anaesthesia -- BIS is the only depth label and it is the thing under examination -- so the result is a measured DISCORDANCE between two simultaneous readings and says nothing about which is correct. Nothing here shows the exponent is right where BIS is not. Establishing that needs an independent depth reference (a clinical responsiveness score, or drug effect-site concentration as a pharmacological anchor) and that is the obvious successor.

WHY THE QUESTION CHANGED, recorded because it is the transferable part: E78, E84, E99 and E90/E102 all asked 'does our measure add to the incumbent?' and all answered no on held-out data. Four failures of the same shape are a result about the question. 'Where does the incumbent stop tracking the EEG?' has no incumbent to beat and needs no ground truth, because disagreement between two simultaneous readings is measurable without knowing which one is right.
placebo: age shuffled across cases, 2000 draws; primary read FIRST (rule 48)
primary: spearman(within-case rho(meta_bis, whole_head_exponent), age) across cases, 4000-rep case bootstrap. Needs NO ground truth: it measures whether two simultaneous readings come apart, not which is right. AGREEMENT IMPROVES WITH AGE named first. PREDICTED: degrades ~45 %, no modulation ~45 %, improves ~10 %.
question: WHERE is BIS wrong? Does the agreement between the vendor's index and an aperiodic exponent computed from the raw waveform degrade with patient age? Asked because four held-out tests (E78, E84, E99, E90/E102) have now answered 'does our measure add to the incumbent?' with no, and four failures of the same shape are a result about the question.

Four ways this deposit necessarily differs -- online control vs decodability, task-baseline vs dedicated rest, 64ch/160Hz vs 62ch/1000Hz, one session vs three -- are written into the registration BEFORE the result so none can be selected as an excuse afterwards.
outcome_detail:
ABSENT AT G2 -- the outcome is not alive enough to be predicted, so nothing about ge_norm was tested (rule 31). This is the E33/E61 rule firing exactly as intended: 'if the incumbent cannot predict the transition at all, beating it is not a result', applied here to the OUTCOME rather than to a comparator.

**G2: median imagery_auc 0.5306 over 104 subjects, and only 16.3 % beat their own permutation null against a pre-registered floor of 20 %.** Cross-validated left-versus-right motor-imagery decodability in eegmmidb, as currently computed, is barely above chance for most subjects. A predictor cannot be tested against an outcome that is mostly noise; a null would have been uninterpretable and a positive would have been worse.

G1 PASSED (104 of 105 subjects carry both predictor and outcome). G3 PASSED and is worth recording because it validates the new extraction: ge_norm median 0.8553, sd 0.0538, range [0.7227, 1.0886] -- a null-normalised efficiency sitting just below 1, which is what the measure should do, computed by the estimator IMPORTED from extract_stieger_graph62.py rather than reimplemented (rule 20).

**NO CORRELATION WITH ACCURACY WAS COMPUTED.** The gate fired before the primary and the file returns without touching it, so this registration remains available: a successor can use it without the hypothesis having been peeked at.

WHAT THIS COSTS. E86's surviving qualification -- BH q = 0.0920 across its family -- is UNANSWERED. It cannot be answered inside the Stieger cohort by any further analysis, so Challenge B's only positive still carries it.

WHAT WOULD LEGITIMATELY FIX IT, and the distinction matters. The 20 % floor is NOT lowered. What can change is the OUTCOME INSTRUMENT: `imagery_auc` is built from six band-power features, whereas the field-standard decoder for this deposit is CSP on band-passed data, which is expected to be substantially better on independent grounds and not because it would pass a gate. If a standard decoder still leaves fewer than 20 % of subjects decodable, the answer is that eegmmidb cannot host this replication and another cohort is needed. That is the successor's job (rule 58: one repair, reason written down).

deposit: Sleep-EDFx five-stage worklist, 142 subjects x 5 stages, frontal and posterior kept separate; joined to sleep_edfx_channel_spectra.csv, sleep_edfx_five_stage.csv and sleep_edfx_emg.csv. SC4001E0 excluded as burn-in (rule 26).
gates: G1 >= 50 subjects with all five stages in both tables

G2 non-degenerate denominator, fixed properly this time: |m_N3 - m_W| >= 0.25 x the between-subject SD of that measure, applied identically to primary and incumbent -- E100's gate excluded only exact zeros and its frontal statistic had IQR [-1.355, +0.293]
G3 THE AXIS MUST EXIST: irreversibility must change W->N3 vs a Gaussian control, else there is nothing to place REM on and the verdict is ABSENT (rule 31)
G4 the phase-randomised surrogate must be far below the real value, else the measure is not measuring irreversibility
G5 MUSCLE -- the gate that killed E100: EMG's own axis position reported and P1 recomputed after within-subject residualisation on submental EMG
instrument_changed: THE MEASURE FAMILY, and for once the escape is a theorem rather than a correlation check. The autocovariance is symmetric in lag, so time reversal leaves the PSD and every summary of it EXACTLY unchanged -- the aperiodic exponent, band powers, spectral entropy, the alpha peak. The permutation form additionally uses only sample ORDERINGS, so it is invariant to any monotone amplitude transform and cannot be muscle amplitude, which is what E70 and E100 turned out to be measuring. And the primary is net of a phase-randomised surrogate with an identical power spectrum.
outcome_detail:
WORSE THAN THE EXPONENT -- the registered wrong-direction branch, and it fired. **A measure that is PROVABLY orthogonal to the entire power spectrum places REM at position +0.9974 on the wake-to-N3 axis: essentially exactly at deep sleep**, against the aperiodic exponent's +0.4788. P1 = **+1.4539 [+1.0166, +2.2259]** over 90 subjects, far outside its placebo [-0.2937, +0.2660].

**ALL FOUR SECONDARIES AGREE AND SOME PUT REM PAST N3**: frontal irr4 +0.9948 (d_z +1.8995), posterior irr3 +1.0176, posterior irr4 +1.0089, increment asymmetry +0.8817. Two sites, two embedding orders and a completely different statistic (third moment of increments) all give the same answer.

**THIS IS THE STRONGEST FORM OF THE SINGLE-AXIS RESULT THIS PROJECT HAS.** The usual escape -- 'the candidates were all the same family' -- is mathematically unavailable here: the autocovariance is symmetric in lag, so time reversal leaves the PSD and every summary of it EXACTLY unchanged, and the permutation form uses only sample orderings so it is invariant to any monotone amplitude transform. The measure could not have been the exponent in disguise, and it still orders REM with sleep -- more extremely than the exponent does.

GATES. G1 138 subjects with all five stages. G3 the axis exists: irr3 changes W->N3 at d_z -0.8187 against a Gaussian 95th of 0.1718. G4 was REPAIRED ONCE under rule 58 and the repair is recorded in the docstring: a round-number ratio gate (0.5) refused the run at 1.62, which was testing my choice of 0.5 rather than the data (rule 63, third occurrence), and it is now a paired test -- real minus surrogate **+0.000758 [+0.000608, +0.000927]** over 689 windows.

**A FINDING IN ITS OWN RIGHT, from G4's absolute level: scalp EEG is very nearly TIME-REVERSIBLE.** Median permutation irreversibility is 0.00031 against a phase-randomised surrogate's 0.00019, where the module's validation puts a sawtooth at 0.116 and reversible processes at ~0.0001. The asymmetry is real (the paired interval excludes zero decisively) and it is three orders of magnitude below a strongly irreversible signal.

**G5 MUSCLE: 81 % OF THE EFFECT IS SHARED WITH SUBMENTAL EMG.** After within-subject residualisation P1 falls from +1.4539 to **+0.2739 [+0.0759, +0.4445]** -- still positive, still excluding zero, but four-fifths gone. Submental EMG's own REM position is +0.9886, almost exactly where irreversibility puts it. Since the permutation form CANNOT be muscle amplitude, what it is reading is muscle WAVEFORM SHAPE. That is a new and specific statement about how muscle contaminates a non-amplitude measure.

LIMITATION, and it is a selection: **G2's denominator rule dropped 46 of 138 subjects for the primary and 0 for the incumbent.** The 90 contributing subjects are those in whom irreversibility has a clean wake-to-N3 span, so the comparison is on a subset selected by the new measure's own behaviour. The asymmetry is large enough that a successor should report the incumbent restricted to the same 90.

CALIBRATION: predicted (b) no difference ~50 %, (c) REM toward wake ~35 %, (a) worse ~15 %. **(a) occurred** -- the outcome given least weight. Fifth measure predicted to be new that was not (rule 28), and the first where the prediction was wrong in the direction of the measure being MORE arousal-locked rather than merely redundant.
placebo: stage labels permuted within subject, 500 draws; primary read FIRST (rule 48)
primary: paired d_z of position(frontal_irr3 - surrogate) - position(whole_head_exponent) on each subject's own W-to-N3 axis -- the SAME statistic E93/E95/E100 used, so the numbers compare. PREDICTED NEGATIVE (REM nearer wake). WORSE-THAN-THE-EXPONENT named first. PREDICTED: no difference ~50 %, REM moves toward wake ~35 %, worse ~15 %.
question: Does a PROVABLY non-spectral measure -- time-irreversibility -- place REM differently from the arousal axis? Three routes have put REM with sleep and two were measured to be muscle; all three were amplitude or power-spectrum summaries.

deposit: VitalDB vitaldb_grid*.csv joined to vitaldb_agents.csv on (caseid, t_s); 247 cases joinable, 100 with >= 10 MAC windows (volatile) and 142 with >= 10 ppf_ce windows (TIVA)
gates: G1 >= 50 cases per arm with >= 10 windows, all three variables varying (rule 32)
G2 THE ANCHOR MUST BE ALIVE AND BOTH READINGS WITH IT (E33/E61): median fid_BIS and median fid_exp both positive per arm, else delta compares a live measure with a dead one

G3 ATTENUATION carried from E109: partial given within-case SD of drug, BIS and exponent plus log n_windows -- all four attenuate toward zero and any that tracks age moves delta for a statistical reason
G4 each arm must span >= 30 years
instrument_changed: a THIRD, NON-EEG MEASUREMENT is introduced -- recorded anaesthetic concentration -- which is what turns E109's symmetric discordance into an attributable one. Two drug classes serve as the internal replication. The one confound that cannot be removed (BIS-guided dosing inflates spearman(BIS, drug)) is named WITH ITS DIRECTION before the run: it biases against 'BIS degrades' and toward 'the exponent degrades', so only one of the two outcomes is conservative under it.
outcome_detail:
NO ATTRIBUTION on the registered primary -- **and the gate that blocked it is a larger result than the primary would have been.**

**THE APERIODIC EXPONENT DOES NOT TRACK PROPOFOL. In the TIVA arm (138 cases) its median within-case fidelity to effect-site propofol concentration is -0.0382, i.e. nothing, while BIS reaches +0.2911. In the volatile arm (92 cases) the exponent IS alive at +0.2837 against BIS's +0.4468.** So the exponent tracks volatile agent concentration and does not track propofol at all, on the same deposit, the same pipeline and the same statistic.

That is a mechanistic explanation for a string of Challenge C failures that previously had none. E84 (nothing adds to PE31/SEF95), E99 (the exponent HURTS BIS for suppression detection) and E90/E102 all ran on deposits where propofol is the dominant agent. **A measure that is blind to the drug cannot add to a measure that is not**, and this is the first result to say why rather than that.

PRIMARY, both arms reported (rule 59): volatile -0.0577 [-0.2808, +0.1545], placebo INSIDE, does not survive G3. TIVA -0.1833 [-0.3338, -0.0116], survives G3 at -0.2078 [-0.3699, -0.0310] and lies outside its placebo [-0.1702, +0.1637] -- **but its G2 failed, so that interval is a difference between a live reading and a dead one and is NOT interpretable as an attribution** (rule 31). The verdict text was corrected to state that a gate blocked it rather than that no interval excluded zero; those are different reasons and printing the wrong one would have misdescribed the run.

E109's DISCORDANCE THEREFORE STANDS UNATTRIBUTED. The experiment did what it was registered to do and declined to name a culprit.

THE CONFOUND, named before the run with its direction and unchanged by the result: anaesthetic dosing is partly BIS-guided, which inflates spearman(BIS, drug) and biases toward 'the exponent degrades'. It cannot be removed from this deposit. It does NOT explain the G2 finding, because it would inflate BIS's fidelity in BOTH arms equally and cannot make the exponent's own propofol fidelity vanish.
